messages.content: Hi, I’m Tessa. I’m trying to sketch a September recruitment loop from Salt Lake City through Boise, the Palouse, and Spokane. I need to avoid backtracking if we can. The rough pieces are Boise high-school visits, an evening fair in Nampa, a counselor breakfast near Pullman, and then a Spokane-area fair before I come home.

Absolutely. To make the route workable, can you give me the dates and the fixed event times? Also, is a one-way rental car allowed, or does reimbursement strongly favor returning the car to the same airport?

Travel week is September 16. I have a Monday morning office handoff in Salt Lake, so I’d like to leave after noon. Tuesday is Boise High at 8:15 and a Meridian visit at 10:15, then the Nampa fair from 6:30 to 8:30. Thursday morning is a 7:30 counselor breakfast near WSU in Pullman, then Thursday evening is the Spokane fair. Delta is nice if it’s comparable, but schedule matters more. Coach is fine. I’d rather not do more than one connection, and I don’t want a tiny 35-minute layover.

Given that order, the cleanest routing is Salt Lake City to Boise, then drive north, and fly home from Spokane. Quick comparison: open-jaw SLC to BOI and GEG to SLC gives the least backtracking and a manageable car path, but you may see a one-way rental fee. Boise round trip likely saves some rental complexity but adds a long Spokane-to-Boise return drive at the worst point of the trip. Spokane round trip is the weakest because it front-loads a long drive to Boise before your first school visits.

That’s what I suspected. The Spokane fair is currently Thursday 5:30 to 7:30. I wondered if I could fly home that same night, but I don’t want to be sprinting through the airport with display materials.

Same-night is possible only if there is a late nonstop and the fair ends on time, but it is fragile. You would still need to pack the table, drive to GEG, refuel, return the rental, and clear security. A Friday afternoon return is much more reliable and still keeps the trip to four hotel nights: Monday and Tuesday Boise area, Wednesday Pullman area, Thursday Spokane area.
The Spokane fair is at a venue in Spokane Valley, not downtown. Pullman breakfast is near WSU. I’ll have one suitcase and a couple of small boxes in the car.

Spokane Valley helps, but I still would not make Thursday night the main plan. If the fair ends at 7:30, you might leave the venue around 7:50, reach the airport around 8:20 to 8:30, then still have the car return and security. That is okay for a very late flight, not okay for anything around 9:00. Friday afternoon gives you breathing room and avoids ending the loop on a scramble.
Let’s treat Friday afternoon as the preferred version, but I’d still like to see the Thursday late option as a backup if finance pushes on the hotel night.

Flight shortlist to verify: outbound Monday SLC to BOI, look first at a mid-afternoon nonstop around 2:30 to 4:00 arrival, ideally Delta if the fare is reasonable. That gets you into Boise early enough to pick up the car, check in, and prep for Tuesday. Return option A is Thursday late GEG to SLC, only if there is a nonstop after about 9:45 p.m.; lowest hotel cost, highest stress. Return option B is Friday afternoon GEG to SLC, around 1:00 to 3:30 p.m.; one more hotel night, much better reliability. Return option C is a one-stop Friday itinerary through Seattle, Portland, or Denver; acceptable only if nonstop pricing is bad and the connection is comfortably over an hour.

Hotels are the other piece. Breakfast included helps a lot on school-visit mornings, and I’d like not to be stranded for dinner after the Nampa fair. One queen bed is fine; I don’t need anything fancy.

For the hotel pattern, I’d separate it by the next morning’s first appointment. Boise area for Monday and Tuesday nights, Pullman or Moscow for Wednesday night, and Spokane Valley for Thursday night if you take the Friday return. I’ll favor places with breakfast listed and restaurants close by, but I’d still verify breakfast start times before booking because early visits can expose vague hotel listings.
For Boise, Tuesday morning is Boise High first and Meridian second, then Nampa in the evening. I’d rather not stay all the way in Nampa if that makes the morning annoying.

Best Boise-area fit is probably Hampton Inn and Suites Boise-Meridian or a similar Meridian/I-84 property. It keeps the morning drive reasonable, puts you near restaurants, and makes the Nampa fair an easy evening drive. Hyatt Place near Boise Towne Square is closer to central Boise dining but a bit farther from Nampa, and breakfast can depend on rate or membership. A Nampa hotel is best only if the fair matters more than the morning visits.
For Pullman, I need to be near the WSU-area breakfast by 7:30. I don’t mind Moscow if it’s the better hotel, but I don’t want to start that morning with a surprise drive.

For Wednesday night, Holiday Inn Express Pullman is the straightforward choice if the rate is acceptable: close to WSU and likely the easiest early morning. Best Western Plus University Inn in Moscow is also practical, often has breakfast, and has better nearby dinner options, but you add roughly 15 minutes in the morning. Courtyard Pullman is convenient and has an on-site Bistro, but breakfast may not be included, so it is less ideal unless location or rate wins.
For Spokane, I’m thinking Spokane Valley rather than the airport because of the fair and because I may have one more Friday morning school visit if someone opens a slot.

Spokane Valley makes sense. I’d shortlist Hampton Inn and Suites Spokane Valley, Tru by Hilton Spokane Valley if available, or a similar I-90 property near restaurants. That keeps Thursday after the fair simple and still positions you well for Coeur d’Alene or the airport on Friday. The only thing I would confirm is breakfast start time and whether they have a grab-and-go option if you add that Friday visit.
That gives me enough to take to my director. I’m not ready to book yet; I’ll check the one-way rental fee and the final fair packet. Can you leave me with the route order and risks?

Recommended route: Monday afternoon fly SLC to Boise, pick up a one-way rental at BOI, and stay in Meridian for two nights. Tuesday do Boise and Meridian visits, then the Nampa fair, returning to the same hotel. Wednesday drive Boise/Meridian to Pullman or Moscow and stay near the Thursday breakfast. Thursday attend the Pullman breakfast, drive to Spokane Valley, work the evening fair, and stay in Spokane Valley. Friday fly GEG to SLC, ideally on an afternoon nonstop. Main risks: the one-way rental fee could change the cost comparison; Thursday night return is too tight unless a very late nonstop exists; Pullman-area hotel breakfast times need verification; and the Spokane Valley hotel should be chosen with Friday morning flexibility in mind.

messages.content: Update on the Inland Northwest loop: the Spokane fair moved later, now 7:00 to 9:00 Thursday night, and I added a Friday morning school visit in Coeur d’Alene. So the same-night return is out. Can you revise the return plan and keep it to four hotel nights if possible?

Yes. Four hotel nights should still work if Thursday stays in Spokane Valley and Friday becomes the flight home. What time is the Coeur d’Alene visit, and do you need to check a bag or return display materials with the rental car? That affects how tight the airport timing can be.
Coeur d’Alene High is 8:45 to 9:45 Friday. It could run to 10 if the counselor wants to talk. I’ll have one checked suitcase, the little boxes, and I need to gas up before returning the car at GEG.

Then I’d build around these return choices: 1:00-ish nonstop GEG to SLC is workable only if the visit ends on time and you leave Coeur d’Alene by 10:10; it gives limited lunch and limited recovery from delays. A 3:00 to 3:45 nonstop is the best reliability choice; you can wrap the visit, drive about 50 minutes to the airport area, fuel, return the car, and still not rush. A one-stop route through Seattle, Portland, or Denver only makes sense if the nonstop is badly priced, and I would avoid any connection under about an hour.
Reliability matters more here. I’m fine getting home around dinner, but I don’t want a long layover or a connection that turns a short return into a whole evening.

Then the recommendation is Friday afternoon nonstop from Spokane to Salt Lake, targeting roughly 3:15 p.m. if available. It keeps the four-night structure intact: Monday and Tuesday in Meridian, Wednesday in Pullman or Moscow, Thursday in Spokane Valley. It also gives you enough room for the Coeur d’Alene visit to run a little long without making the airport stressful.
Would the 1:00-ish return be too close if I end up doing a quick debrief after the school visit?

It becomes uncomfortable. If the visit ends at 10:00, a brief debrief can push departure to 10:20 or 10:30. Add the drive to GEG, gas, rental return, and checked-bag cutoff, and the 1:00 flight has very little slack. It is not impossible, but it depends on everything behaving. The mid-afternoon flight is the safer planning choice.
What if the nonstop choices are only morning or evening when I actually book?

Morning would not work with the Coeur d’Alene visit. Evening is acceptable but makes for a long Friday, so I’d compare it against a one-stop itinerary departing early to mid-afternoon with a comfortable connection. If the connection is 60 to 90 minutes and the total travel time stays reasonable, it can be a backup. I would not add a Friday night hotel unless afternoon and evening options both fall apart.
Can you update the hotel sequence with the Friday visit in mind?

Keep Monday and Tuesday in Meridian for the Boise/Nampa segment. Keep Wednesday in Pullman if you want the simplest 7:30 breakfast morning; Moscow is okay only if the hotel value is clearly better. For Thursday, choose Spokane Valley along I-90 rather than the airport. It is better for the late fair, better for the Coeur d’Alene morning, and still reasonable for the airport afterward. Confirm Thursday-night hotel breakfast starts early enough, or plan coffee and a portable breakfast before the school visit.
Great. Give me the revised recommendation in a small summary I can send with the approval note.

Revised recommendation: fly SLC to BOI Monday afternoon, rent one-way from BOI to GEG, stay two nights in Meridian, one night in Pullman, and one night in Spokane Valley. Do not attempt the Thursday night return now that the Spokane fair ends at 9:00. On Friday, do Coeur d’Alene High from 8:45 to about 9:45 or 10:00, then drive to GEG and take a mid-afternoon nonstop to SLC if available. Use a one-stop return only if the nonstop is not viable and the layover is comfortably timed.

That still fits the loop well. The Monday flight gets you into Boise with daylight left for the rental and check-in, and the Friday 3:20 return is the right buffer after Coeur d’Alene. Hotel sequence works: Meridian for the Boise/Nampa day, Pullman for the 7:30 breakfast morning, Spokane Valley after the late fair and before Coeur d’Alene. If Spokane breakfast is vague, is that a booking blocker? I can do coffee and a granola bar if needed, but I don’t want a bad surprise.

Not a blocker if the hotel otherwise works. I’d call or message the Hampton before checkout and ask two things: breakfast start time on Friday and whether they can note a late arrival after the Thursday fair. Perfect. Can you give me the final booking summary in travel-request language?

Hotels: Hampton Inn and Suites Boise-Meridian Sept. 16-18, Holiday Inn Express Pullman Sept. 18-19, Hampton Inn Spokane Valley Sept. 19-20. messages.content: I’m done enough with the Northwest loop and need to start the Texas one. It’s Oct. 14-17: Monday late-morning counselor meeting near Fort Worth, Monday evening Dallas fair, Tuesday visits in Waco and Temple, and a Wednesday evening alumni event that may be somewhere between Austin and San Antonio. I’m trying to decide open-jaw into DFW and home from AUS or SAT versus a simple round trip. Hotels and rental car are not settled.

This is a north-to-south route, so the simple round trip may make the driving harder. Before I tighten the flight and hotel map, what time is the Fort Worth meeting, the Dallas fair, the Tuesday visits, and do you need to be home Thursday?

Fort Worth is 11:30 near TCU, Dallas fair is 6:30-8:30 at Market Hall. Tuesday: Waco high school at 9:00, Baylor counselor lunch at 11:30, Temple school at 2:15. Wednesday event is likely 6-8 but venue not final. I’d like to be home Thursday, no Friday stay.

Initial read: open-jaw wins unless reimbursement punishes the one-way rental. DFW in / AUS out is the cleanest if Wednesday is Austin or north Austin. DFW in / SAT out is best only if the event lands in San Antonio or New Braunfels. DFW round trip is simple on paper but adds 3+ hours of backtracking Thursday, or a bad late drive Wednesday after the event. AUS round trip is the worst fit because you would have to drive to Fort Worth before the 11:30 meeting. I’d plan DFW in and hold the return airport until the Wednesday venue firms up.
Could I fly in Monday morning, or am I kidding myself and should come Sunday night?

Same-day can work, but only with a nonstop that lands DFW around 9:15 or earlier. You need time to deplane, get the rental car, exit DFW, and drive 35-55 minutes to TCU. A 9:45 arrival is possible on paper but gives you almost no cushion for a late inbound, rental counter line, or Fort Worth traffic. If the clean flight lands after about 9:30, I would move to Sunday night.
Early Monday is fine for this trip. Include Delta if it’s clean, but I’m not taking a weird connection just for the carrier.

Then I’d use a practical flight rule: take the earliest nonstop into DFW that arrives before the buffer cutoff. If Delta has that, great; if Delta connects or lands closer to 10:00, use American or another nonstop into DFW. For the return, Austin usually gives you more workable SLC routings than San Antonio. San Antonio is only worth it if the event is truly south.
Assume no Sunday. How ugly is the road piece if Wednesday ends up Austin versus San Antonio?

If Wednesday is Austin or a north suburb, the route is clean: Dallas after the fair, early Tuesday drive to Waco, Temple after lunch, then continue to Round Rock or North Austin for Tuesday and Wednesday nights. If Wednesday is San Antonio, North Austin becomes a long evening return or a late hotel change; San Marcos, New Braunfels, or north San Antonio would be less painful. The pinch points are Monday DFW-to-Fort Worth after landing, Fort Worth-to-Dallas before the fair, and Tuesday Dallas-to-Waco. For that last one, I’d leave around 6:30 for a 9:00 visit.
I don’t love switching hotels every night. Could I do Dallas Monday and then one southern base Tuesday and Wednesday?

Yes, if the Wednesday venue is Austin, Round Rock, Cedar Park, or even San Marcos. After the Temple visit, you would keep moving south, check into the same hotel Tuesday and Wednesday, and avoid unpacking twice. If the event lands in downtown San Antonio, though, a North Austin base turns into a 90-120 minute drive each way depending on traffic. Then I’d switch the base to San Antonio or use San Marcos/New Braunfels as the compromise.
For hotels, I need to stay inside the university reimbursement range, breakfast included if I can get it, and decent food nearby after the evening events. Nothing fancy.

For Monday, I would not sleep in Fort Worth after the Dallas fair. Look at Dallas Market Center/Medical District, Las Colinas, or North Dallas near the fair, with the deciding factor being late dinner access and a clean route to I-35 for Waco. For Tuesday/Wednesday, if Austin is likely, look at Round Rock, Cedar Park, or the Domain/Arboretum area. Those areas have practical chain hotels, easier dinner options, and breakfast-included rates to verify. If San Antonio becomes likely, shift to New Braunfels or north San Antonio rather than central San Antonio.
My director asked whether staying in Waco Tuesday would make Wednesday easier because Waco hotels may be cheaper. Does that make sense?

Only as a cost play. Waco Tuesday saves some hotel money, but your last Tuesday stop is already in Temple, south of Waco. If you go back to Waco, you push the longer drive into Wednesday: about 1.5-2 hours to North Austin and closer to 3 hours to San Antonio before traffic or setup time. If the venue is likely Austin-area, continuing to Round Rock or Cedar Park after Temple is less stressful.
I can set one Wednesday counselor coffee wherever it helps. The alumni host just has not picked the restaurant yet.

Then place the Wednesday coffee near the eventual hotel base. If you choose Round Rock or Cedar Park, schedule the coffee there or at the Domain and keep Wednesday compact. If the event shifts south, make the coffee in San Marcos or north San Antonio. I would avoid putting the coffee in Waco because it anchors you north and lengthens the event-day drive.
Can you leave me with a plain comparison I can send for approval, including the drive-time risk?

Approval comparison: choose open-jaw unless the one-way rental fee is extreme. Working plan is SLC-DFW early Monday, arriving by about 9:15; pick up a one-way rental; Fort Worth meeting; Dallas Market Hall fair; Monday hotel in Market Center or Las Colinas. Tuesday drive early to Waco, then Temple, then continue south. If the alumni venue is Austin-area, stay Tuesday/Wednesday in Round Rock, Cedar Park, or North Austin and fly home Thursday from AUS. Use SAT only if the venue is south of San Marcos. Main risks: DFW arrival later than 9:30 jeopardizes the Fort Worth buffer; DFW round trip adds a tiring Thursday backtrack; Waco Tuesday is cheaper but moves the long drive to Wednesday.

messages.content: Update on Texas: Wednesday event is confirmed in Cedar Park, 6:00 to 8:00. I need to lock hotel areas. We get reimbursed up to about $185 before taxes. I’m thinking one Dallas-area night Monday and two nights north Austin, but my director still asked if Waco Tuesday is smarter.

Cedar Park simplifies it. I’d use one Dallas-area hotel Monday and one North Austin/Round Rock/Cedar Park hotel for Tuesday and Wednesday. Waco Tuesday only helps the nightly rate; it does not help the flow once your last Tuesday appointment is in Temple.

Monday fair is at Dallas Market Hall until 8:30. The Fort Worth meeting is near TCU. Tuesday is Waco 9:00, Baylor lunch 11:30, Temple 2:15. I’ll need food after the fair and again after the Cedar Park event.

Overnight sequence comparison: A) Dallas Market Center or Las Colinas Monday, then Round Rock/Cedar Park Tuesday-Wednesday: least stressful overall; Tuesday after Temple is about 50-75 minutes to the hotel, Wednesday is local, Thursday AUS is manageable. B) Waco Tuesday, Cedar Park Wednesday: cheaper possibility but adds a hotel change and a longer Wednesday drive. C) Stay south of Dallas Monday to shorten Tuesday: helps the Waco departure a little but usually sacrifices better late dinner choices after the fair. I’d choose A.
For the Dallas night, would you pick Market Center, Las Colinas, or something south toward Waco?

Market Center is best if you want to be off the road quickly after the fair. Las Colinas is a little farther after the fair but often has better chain-hotel value and plenty of restaurants. South toward Waco only makes sense if you are comfortable driving 20-35 minutes after the fair at night and you find a clear breakfast-included rate. My practical pick is Las Colinas if the rate is within cap; otherwise Market Center.
Can you name the hotel styles I should search? I don’t need a luxury place, just predictable.

For Dallas, search Holiday Inn Express, Hampton Inn, Fairfield Inn, or Home2 Suites in Market Center/Medical District and Las Colinas; verify breakfast is included on the rate because some nearby Hilton and Marriott brands charge separately. For the Austin side, search Round Rock/La Frontera, Cedar Park, or the Domain/Arboretum for Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Home2 Suites, SpringHill Suites, or Fairfield. Round Rock/La Frontera is likely the best price and food balance.
The Domain sounds easy for dinner but maybe over the cap. Would Round Rock make Cedar Park annoying?

No. Round Rock/La Frontera to Cedar Park is typically 20-35 minutes, and after the Temple visit it is an easy continuation south. It also keeps Thursday’s drive to AUS reasonable, usually 35-50 minutes if you leave with cushion. The Domain is nicer for restaurants, but it can cost more and may add traffic. Cedar Park is closest to the event but can be less convenient for the airport.
Okay, please answer the Waco question directly and give me the least-stressful overnight sequence.

Direct answer: do not stay in Waco Tuesday unless the savings are large enough to justify an extra hotel change and a longer Wednesday drive. Least-stressful sequence: Monday night in Las Colinas or Dallas Market Center after the fair, preferably a breakfast-included chain with late dinner nearby; Tuesday morning leave early for Waco; after Temple, drive to Round Rock/La Frontera or Cedar Park and stay there Tuesday and Wednesday; set the Wednesday coffee near that hotel; after the Cedar Park event, return to the same hotel; Thursday fly home from AUS. Round Rock/La Frontera is my first choice if it prices under the $185 cap, with Cedar Park second and the Domain only if the rate is surprisingly good.

messages.content: Last Texas piece: I’m ready to book flights. Delta can do SLC-DFW Monday arriving 9:35, but the return from Austin has a late Atlanta connection and gets me home after 10:30. American has SLC-DFW arriving 9:10 and AUS-DFW-SLC Thursday, home about 4:30, for a little less. Which would you choose?

I’d book American for this trip. The 9:10 DFW arrival gives a better cushion before the 11:30 Fort Worth meeting, and the Austin return gets you home at a sane hour without a long late connection. The Delta return adds fatigue without solving a schedule problem.
The Austin return connection in DFW is 65 minutes. Is that comfortable enough or should I worry?

Sixty-five minutes at DFW on one airline is workable for a domestic connection, but it is not roomy. If there is an 80- to 100-minute connection that still gets you home before dinner, I would pay a modest difference. If the choice is 65 minutes versus the late Atlanta return, I’d still take the 65-minute DFW option.
There is an American return leaving AUS 11:25, DFW 12:35, then DFW to SLC at 2:05, landing 3:55. It’s $32 more.

That is the better itinerary. The 90-minute DFW connection is much more comfortable, and landing in SLC before 4:00 is a strong return. I would book that over both the 65-minute version and the late Delta connection.
Good. Main cabin/economy, and I’ll pick a window if there’s one. Anything else to note for reimbursement?

Book main cabin rather than basic economy if seat selection or changes matter. Save the fare comparison and note the reason: DFW arrival improves the Fort Worth buffer, AUS return avoids the late Delta connection, and the open-jaw matches the approved DFW-to-Cedar Park route with a one-way rental.
Can you give me the final booking language?

Book American open-jaw: SLC to DFW Monday Oct. 14, arriving about 9:10 a.m. for the 11:30 Fort Worth meeting; AUS to SLC Thursday Oct. 17 via DFW, departing AUS 11:25 a.m., about a 90-minute DFW connection, arriving SLC about 3:55 p.m. Main cabin/economy; select a window seat if available. Reimbursement note: schedule reliability and shorter return justify choosing this over the late Delta connection; rental is one-way DFW pickup, AUS return.

messages.content: I ticketed the AUS to SLC return you suggested. Before the hotel cancellation deadline, can you sanity-check Texas? Monday DFW about 9:10, Fort Worth 11:30, Market Hall fair 6:30-8:30; Tuesday Waco and Temple; Wednesday Cedar Park 6-8. I’m holding Fairfield Dallas Market Center Monday and Hyatt Place Round Rock/La Frontera Tuesday and Wednesday, both under cap. A Round Rock school just offered Wednesday 9 a.m. Does that fit, and what should I call to verify?

Yes, the Round Rock school fits without moving hotels. The pieces I would verify are hotel breakfast hours, whether breakfast is truly included in the booked rate, and the rental-car one-way cost. The Dallas hotel is better for the late fair than an airport-area stay; the Round Rock/La Frontera hotel is exactly the right side of town for Wednesday morning and Cedar Park.
Waco is 9:45 and Temple is 1:15. Rental is DFW pickup 9:30 Monday, AUS return 9:30 Thursday. I care most about breakfast and late dinner access this time.

That works. Monday: if the rental line is normal and you leave DFW by 9:45 or 10:00, the 11:30 Fort Worth meeting is still okay but not roomy. Tuesday: leave Dallas around 7:15-7:25 for Waco; after Temple, continue to Round Rock and avoid the extra hotel change. Call Fairfield to confirm weekday breakfast start, parking, and late arrival back after the fair. Call Hyatt Place to confirm breakfast start and nearby kitchens still open after the Cedar Park event.
Should I change the rental return to 9:00 instead of 9:30 for the 11:25 flight?

Aim to be at the AUS rental return by about 9:15, but a 9:30 reservation time is usually fine if the actual contract starts after the DFW pickup line. I’d call the rental agency for total one-way price, toll policy, grace period, and whether the DFW-to-AUS drop fee is already included.
Okay. Final go/no-go list?

Go: keep Fairfield Dallas Market Center Monday if breakfast is included and starts early enough; keep Hyatt Place Round Rock/La Frontera Tuesday and Wednesday; keep the Wednesday 9 a.m. Round Rock visit; use DFW pickup and AUS return. Phone-call items before purchase: Fairfield breakfast and parking, Hyatt breakfast and post-8 p.m. dinner options, rental one-way/drop/toll total. No hotel move is needed.

messages.content: I’m starting the next fall loop and need the sane version before I request approval. Late October: Monday counselor breakfast in Eden Prairie, Monday evening fair in Saint Paul, Tuesday visits near Rochester, Wednesday transfer fair in La Crosse, and Thursday morning high school visit in Eau Claire. I’d like to leave SLC Sunday and get home Thursday afternoon if that’s realistic. Should I do MSP round trip and drive the loop, or use a smaller return airport after La Crosse or Eau Claire?

I’d make MSP round trip the baseline. It keeps the flight inventory and rental-car pricing much cleaner. The smaller-airport idea only wins if the exact return has one clean connection and the one-way rental fee is modest. Quick read: MSP round trip is the reliable choice, with a Thursday drive from Eau Claire back to MSP; EAU out shortens the drive but can have thin schedules and fragile connections; LSE or RST out is awkward if you still need to be in Eau Claire Thursday morning.

Dates are Sunday Oct. 27 to Thursday Oct. 31. Eden Prairie breakfast is 8:00 Monday, Saint Paul fair is 6:30-8:30 Monday. Tuesday is Rochester 8:45, Byron 11, and maybe Stewartville at 2. Wednesday La Crosse is listed 4-6 but might move. Eau Claire just says Thursday morning. I can leave SLC Sunday after about 1.

Since the Monday breakfast is at 8, I would not risk a same-day arrival. Search Sunday SLC to MSP after 1 p.m., ideally arriving early enough to pick up the car and sleep near Eden Prairie or west Bloomington. The main trade-off is Monday night: either stay near Saint Paul/Eagan after the fair and drive early to Rochester, or drive to Rochester after the fair and make Tuesday morning easier.
I’m okay with one longer post-fair drive, but not two in a row. I also don’t want to roll into a hotel after 11 if I can help it.

Then drive to Rochester Monday after the Saint Paul fair, as long as weather looks normal. If you leave the fair area around 8:50-9:00, Rochester arrival is roughly 10:15-10:30. That keeps Tuesday much calmer. I would not also plan a long late drive Wednesday unless the La Crosse fair stays at 4-6 and you are feeling fresh.
The listed La Crosse conference hotel is expensive. Are Onalaska or downtown La Crosse okay? I need breakfast included if I can get it, and somewhere I can get dinner after the fair.

Both are workable. Downtown La Crosse is better for walkable dinner and anything near the convention center or UWL. Onalaska is better for chain hotels, easier parking, and a simpler highway departure. For included breakfast, Onalaska is more likely to price well. For dinner after a 6 p.m. fair, downtown gives more choices; in Onalaska, verify restaurant hours instead of assuming.
What about flying home from Eau Claire? Is that a trap?

It can be. I would treat EAU as a comparison point, not the plan. The risk is limited flight frequency, a missed connection creating a long delay, and a one-way rental charge. If there is a Thursday early-afternoon EAU option with one comfortable connection to SLC, it is worth pricing. If it involves odd timing, multiple stops, or a big drop fee, MSP round trip is the safer approval request.
Can you sketch the actual overnight sequence if I do MSP round trip?

Baseline sequence: Sunday night Eden Prairie or west Bloomington for the 8 a.m. breakfast. Monday night Rochester after the Saint Paul fair, with late check-in confirmed. Tuesday night La Crosse or Onalaska after the Rochester-area visits, so Wednesday is not rushed. Wednesday night depends on the final fair time and the Eau Claire appointment: Eau Claire if the fair stays 4-6 and Thursday is not too early; La Crosse or a partway stop if either timing tightens.
Could I stay in La Crosse Wednesday and still make the Eau Claire visit?

Yes if Eau Claire gives you 9:30 or later. It becomes tight if they set it before 9, because you would be leaving La Crosse in the dark around 6 or a little after, and breakfast may not be open. This is the one item I’d confirm before locking the Wednesday hotel.
Let’s assume they give me 9:00, and I want a Thursday afternoon departure with a comfortable airport buffer, not a sprint.

For a 9:00 Eau Claire visit, plan to leave the school around 10:15 if possible, drive to MSP, refuel, and return the car around 12:15-12:30. I’d search MSP departures after 2 p.m. That gives a normal airport buffer and avoids depending on a tiny return airport.
Can you make a recommendation now? The reimbursement person wants to know why I’m not using the smaller airport.

Recommendation: request MSP round trip with an MSP-to-MSP rental. Reason: it has the strongest schedule reliability, avoids a one-way rental fee, and still supports a Thursday afternoon return after Eau Claire. Smaller airports should only be used if a specific itinerary appears with one comfortable connection, no punishing layover, and a total cost that beats MSP after the rental fee is included.
And hotel zones in one place, please.

Use these zones: Sunday, Eden Prairie or west Bloomington near I-494 for the 8 a.m. breakfast. Monday, Rochester south or near Apache Mall/Broadway, because you arrive late and need an easy Tuesday start. Tuesday, Onalaska if you want value and easy parking, downtown La Crosse if dinner access matters more. Wednesday, hold flexible until Eau Claire time is firm: Eau Claire for an easy Thursday morning, or La Crosse/partway if the Wednesday fair runs later.
Great. Leave me with a flight-and-car search instruction, not ticketing language yet.

Search SLC to MSP on Sunday Oct. 27 after 1 p.m., prioritizing a clean arrival that leaves time for rental pickup and a normal hotel check-in. Search MSP to SLC Thursday Oct. 31 after 2 p.m. Compare nonstop and one-stop options, but skip anything with multiple connections or a long layover. Rental: MSP pickup Sunday evening, MSP return Thursday around 12:30, and price one EAU-return scenario only as a sanity check.

messages.content: Update on the Midwest loop: La Crosse shifted an hour later, now 5-7 p.m., and Eau Claire confirmed 8:15 Thursday morning. I do not want to drive all the way to Eau Claire after the fair, but I still need to keep this to four hotel nights. Can you rework the middle nights?

Yes. With a 5-7 La Crosse fair and an 8:15 Eau Claire visit, I would not sleep in central La Crosse Wednesday unless you are comfortable leaving before 6 a.m. Lowest-stress four-night sequence: Sunday Eden Prairie/west Bloomington, Monday Rochester, Tuesday Onalaska or La Crosse, Wednesday Black River Falls. That splits the Wednesday night drive and keeps Thursday morning reasonable.
Would staying in La Crosse Wednesday be too risky, or just annoying?

More brittle than risky, but I would avoid it. You’d be checking out very early, driving in the dark, and likely missing hotel breakfast. Any fog, rain, or slow checkout cuts into the 8:15 appointment. Black River Falls reduces Thursday to roughly an hour and still avoids the full La Crosse-to-Eau Claire drive after the fair.
Could I instead eat dinner in La Crosse and then drive to Eau Claire later?

You could, but it puts you into Eau Claire around 9:45-10:15 depending on dinner and road conditions. That makes Thursday easy but turns Wednesday into the tiring night. The partway stop is the better balance: grab a quick dinner in La Crosse or pack something, drive about 50 minutes, then sleep.
What hotel area in Black River Falls should I look at? I don’t know that corridor.

Look near the I-94 and Highway 54 interchange. Choose a straightforward chain hotel with parking, late check-in, and breakfast listed for 6 or 6:30. Do not pick anything rural or resort-style for this night. Dinner choices there are limited, so treat La Crosse as the reliable dinner stop.
For Tuesday in La Crosse, downtown or Onalaska now?

I’d choose Onalaska for Tuesday if the rate is better and breakfast is included. It gives you easy parking, chain-hotel breakfast, and a simpler departure after Wednesday’s fair. Choose downtown only if the fair venue is downtown or you want walkable dinner Tuesday night.
Can you put the four nights together with the drive buffers?

Sunday: west Bloomington or Eden Prairie, close to the Monday 8 a.m. breakfast. Monday: Rochester after the Saint Paul fair; leave the fair area around 8:50-9:00 and confirm late check-in. Tuesday: Onalaska/La Crosse after the Rochester-area visits. Wednesday: after the 5-7 fair, eat quickly or take food to go, then drive to Black River Falls and arrive around 8:30-9:00. Thursday: leave Black River Falls around 6:50-7:00 for the 8:15 Eau Claire visit.
Should I cancel the Eau Claire Wednesday hold now?

Not until the Black River Falls room is confirmed and cancellable. Once you have that, cancel the Eau Claire hold. Keep a La Crosse backup only if Black River Falls is overpriced or unavailable, but make sure you understand that it means a very early Thursday departure.
Give me the short booking note for this change.

Change the middle of the loop to avoid a late full drive: keep Monday night Rochester, book Tuesday night Onalaska/La Crosse with included breakfast, and book Wednesday night Black River Falls near I-94/Highway 54. Plan dinner in La Crosse after the 5-7 fair, then drive partway. Thursday leave Black River Falls by 7:00 for the 8:15 Eau Claire visit, then continue to MSP for an afternoon flight.

I’d book the MSP round trip. The Eau Claire option saves money, but it stacks the two things that are hardest to fix: a tight connection and a rental return at a smaller airport right after a school visit. With the MSP 4:50 nonstop, you can let the visit run a bit late, drive west without rushing, return the car at the same airport, and still avoid a huge dead stretch.
Visit should wrap by 9:30, maybe 10 if the counselor adds students. Is MSP still too much sitting around?

If you leave Eau Claire around 10:00, the drive plus gas and rental return puts you inside MSP around 12:15-12:45. For a 4:50 flight, that is a 3-ish hour cushion after security, not a full day. I would rather have that cushion than a 38-minute connection where a small delay strands you.
Okay, keep MSP. So rental is still MSP pickup and return?

Yes. Pick up Sunday evening at MSP and return Thursday early afternoon at MSP. No one-way return to price, no smaller-counter hours to worry about, and the Black River Falls-to-Eau Claire-to-MSP plan stays intact.
Good. Book economy. If seat selection is open, take window on both legs. What should I put in the receipt packet?

Booking note: buy the Sunday Oct. 27 SLC-MSP nonstop and the Thursday Oct. 31 4:50 p.m. MSP-SLC nonstop in economy, with window seats if available. Receipt packet: airfare receipt showing ticket number and full itinerary, any seat or bag fee receipts, rental confirmation showing MSP pickup and return, and later the final rental receipt with fuel or toll charges. Keep the school-visit schedule attached as the justification for the later MSP return flight.

messages.content: New thing: Denver admissions conference. It starts Tuesday Dec. 10 at noon and ends Thursday around 3. There’s a Wednesday evening reception near the convention center. I’m trying to decide whether to fly in Monday afternoon or Tuesday morning. Reimbursement cap is $190 before tax; the official hotel block is $229 and I can’t tell if breakfast is included.

Since the first required piece is Tuesday at noon, this is a reliability question. Monday afternoon is the safer arrival; Tuesday morning can work from SLC, but it leaves very little recovery time if weather, de-icing, or baggage slows you down. Two quick checks before I narrow it: do you need to be registered by a certain time Tuesday, and is a simple light-rail hop acceptable if it keeps the hotel under cap?
Registration by 11:15 would be ideal. Light rail is fine if it’s one easy ride, not a transfer with bags. I can leave after lunch Monday, but Tuesday would mean the very early flight.

Here’s how I’d weigh it: Monday afternoon arrival costs one extra hotel night but gives you a calm Tuesday morning and a normal check-in. Tuesday morning saves the night, but you’d need a nonstop landing by about 9:00 a.m. to leave room for airport transfer, bag drop, and registration. In December, I would not build this around a connection.
Can you shortlist hotels both ways? I need something I can show my director if she pushes back on the extra night.

Shortlist to compare: 1. Official block near the convention center: easiest for sessions and the reception, but $229 before tax and breakfast is unclear, so it needs reimbursement approval. 2. SpringHill Suites Denver Downtown/Auraria area: usually under or near cap, breakfast included, near a simple rail or ride option, but less convenient after the reception. 3. Element Denver Downtown East or similar edge-of-downtown option: walkable to the convention center, often closer to cap than the block, but dinner choices right outside are thinner.
SpringHill is showing $181 for Monday through Thursday, breakfast included. Element is $197, no clear breakfast, and the block is $229. Does that change the arrival answer?

Yes, it strengthens Monday. Three nights at SpringHill are still close to policy, and breakfast is solved. Two nights at the block cost nearly as much before you add breakfast, and it still needs an exception. If the director denies Monday, I’d still keep SpringHill for Tuesday and Wednesday because it is the cleanest reimbursement story.
What flight times would you search? Not booking yet.

For Plan A, search SLC-DEN nonstop Monday Dec. 9 departing roughly 1:00-4:00 p.m., arriving by early evening. That gives you dinner and a normal hotel check-in without burning the whole day. Return Thursday Dec. 12 after 5:00 p.m.; the conference ending around 3:00 makes anything earlier too tight once you include the airport ride and security.
And Plan B if I get told Tuesday only?

Plan B is a nonstop that lands at DEN by 9:00 a.m. Tuesday, ideally earlier, with no checked-bag dependency if you can avoid it. I’d avoid any Tuesday itinerary with a connection, because a small delay could make you miss registration or the opening session.
Can you give me the note I can send myself, including the hotel caveat?

Note for Denver: Recommended plan is Monday afternoon SLC-DEN nonstop, SpringHill/Auraria for Dec. 9-12 if the $181 breakfast-included rate is refundable and the rail or ride to the convention center is simple. Return Thursday after 5 p.m. If the extra hotel night is denied, use a very early Tuesday nonstop and book SpringHill for Dec. 10-12. Do not use the official block unless finance confirms the $229 rate is reimbursable above the $190 cap and whether breakfast is included or separately reimbursable. For the Wednesday reception, plan a rideshare back if the light-rail timing feels awkward.

Can you rank these for booking?
I can, but one detail affects the order: are these all refundable, and are you now definitely booking only Tuesday and Wednesday nights?

Yes, Tuesday and Wednesday nights for now. SpringHill is refundable until 48 hours out. The block takes a one-night deposit but is refundable 72 hours out. Element becomes nonrefundable tomorrow evening. Cap is still $190 before tax, and the block email just says official conference rate.

My ranking: 1. SpringHill/Auraria at $166 with breakfast: best policy fit, easiest morning food, refundable, and the reception inconvenience is manageable for one evening. 2. Official block at $239 only if reimbursement gives written approval for the over-cap conference rate; otherwise it risks out-of-pocket cost and still leaves breakfast unresolved. 3. Element at $196: close enough to walk, but slightly over cap, nonrefundable soon, and weaker meal logistics, so it does not beat SpringHill.
Would you really not put the block first? It’s right there for the sessions.

If finance approves the $239 block rate in writing, I’d move it to first for convenience. Without that, the location benefit is not enough: you’d be above cap for both nights, may have to buy breakfast, and the deposit creates more cleanup if reimbursement is denied.
SpringHill says breakfast starts at 6:30. Reception ends around 8:30 p.m. The rail ride is 10 or 12 minutes, or I could rideshare. Too much hassle?

No, not for this agenda. Use light rail or a rideshare to the reception, then rideshare back after 8:30 if you do not want to wait. For the day sessions, leave 25-30 minutes from the hotel lobby so you are not cutting it close. Breakfast at 6:30 is early enough.
What exact reimbursement question should I send before I pay?

Ask this: Since the lower-priced conference-block rooms are sold out and the only remaining official block room is $239 before tax, will the university reimburse the actual official block rate above the $190 nightly cap, or will reimbursement be limited to $190 before tax? Also, please confirm whether the cap excludes taxes and required fees, and whether breakfast is reimbursable if it is not included.
If they say yes this afternoon, do I switch to the block?

Yes, if the approval is written and the room is still refundable, switch to the block for the shortest conference day logistics. If the answer is no or unclear, book SpringHill before its rate moves. I would skip Element unless SpringHill disappears or the rail plan becomes a problem.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa chose the reimbursable two-night Denver plan over an extra arrival-buffer night because the noon opening was not mission-critical. messages.content: Finance gave me the Denver answer: no exception for the official block if there are cheaper rooms nearby. Can we decide the actual flight and hotel now? I’m still torn between Monday afternoon with the extra night and Tuesday morning with two nights.

Yes. The decision really comes down to arrival risk versus paying for a night that finance may question. For a Tuesday noon opening, I’d rank it this way:

1. Tuesday early nonstop + SpringHill/Auraria, Tue-Wed nights: lowest clean reimbursement, breakfast included, reasonable rail plan, but less buffer if the flight slips.
2. Monday afternoon nonstop + SpringHill/Auraria, Mon-Wed nights: safest arrival, but adds a third night that is not helped by the block exception.
3. Tuesday early nonstop + walking-distance hotel: easiest convention access, but weaker food setup and not much better than SpringHill for the actual schedule.

Before I push you toward one: is the noon opening something you truly cannot miss, or would it be okay if a delay made you arrive closer to 12:30?
I’m not presenting until 1:30. Noon is welcome and badge pickup, so I’d be annoyed but not sunk if I missed the first bit.

Then I’d book the Tuesday morning nonstop and SpringHill/Auraria for Tuesday and Wednesday only. It protects reimbursement, keeps breakfast easy, and still gets you in with a cushion for a 1:30 commitment as long as the flight is not badly delayed.
Which Tuesday flight would you use?

Use the early nonstop that lands before 9 a.m. My practical pick is the Delta SLC-DEN around 7:15 a.m., arriving about 8:40 a.m. It gives you time for the airport train, a bag drop, and a quick lunch before the noon opening. I would not use anything arriving after 10:15 for this trip unless the fare difference is huge.
Delta is fine if it isn’t much more. What about the hotel cancellation details?

Book SpringHill/Auraria only if the $181-ish rate is refundable until at least 24-48 hours before arrival. Check whether the policy is local hotel time and whether one night plus tax is charged after the deadline. If the rate has changed, I’d still take it up to the $190 cap before switching to the walking-distance option.
The SpringHill rate is still there, breakfast included, and cancellation says Dec. 8 by 11:59 p.m. hotel time. Two queen room, not king.

That works. Two queens are fine for a solo conference stay if that is the room attached to the reimbursable rate. I’d book SpringHill/Auraria Dec. 10-12, refundable rate, and the Tuesday early nonstop into Denver. For the return, keep the after-5 p.m. nonstop so you are not cutting the closing session too tightly.
Should I ignore the walking-distance one completely?

For this version, yes. Its main advantage is the walk to the convention center. SpringHill gives you breakfast, better receipt optics under the cap, and easier casual dinner options around Auraria/Union Station. If the weather looks terrible right before departure, you can use rideshare for the conference legs and still come out ahead versus the block.
Okay. Give me the booking checklist and anything I should confirm before checkout.

Booking checklist:

- Flight: Tuesday morning SLC-DEN nonstop landing before 9 a.m.; Thursday DEN-SLC nonstop after 5 p.m.; economy is fine.
- Seats: choose window seats if the map is open; otherwise set a reminder to check again at check-in.
- Hotel: SpringHill/Auraria, Dec. 10-12, refundable $181-ish rate, breakfast included, two-queen room acceptable.
- Cancellation: save the Dec. 8 by 11:59 p.m. hotel-time deadline.

Confirm before checkout or by quick call:
- Breakfast start time, especially for early conference mornings.
- Whether they hold bags before check-in on Tuesday and after checkout Thursday.
- Any destination/amenity fee or parking charge that appears even without a car.
- Exact rail/walk instructions from Union Station in winter weather.

Receipt packet:
- Airfare receipt with ticket number and full itinerary.
- Hotel folio after checkout showing nightly rate, taxes, and zero balance.
- Conference agenda showing the Tuesday noon start and Thursday closing time.
- Any transit/rideshare receipts if snow makes walking impractical.

messages.content: Denver is next week. I booked the Tuesday morning nonstop and SpringHill for Tuesday and Wednesday. They added a Wednesday 7:30 a.m. breakfast roundtable, and now there’s light snow in the forecast. Can you sanity-check the timing?

Yes. For Tuesday, plan on the airport train if the flight lands on time, but leave yourself permission to rideshare from Union Station if sidewalks are messy. The key pieces are: land around 8:40, reach Union Station around 10:00, bag drop at SpringHill, then head to the convention center by 11:15 so badge pickup is calm before noon.
That sounds right. Should I call the hotel about bag drop or just assume?

Call. Ask three quick things: whether they can hold luggage before check-in Tuesday, whether they can store your bag after checkout Thursday, and what time breakfast starts Wednesday. The 7:30 roundtable makes breakfast hours the only real wrinkle.
If breakfast starts at 6:30, is that enough?

Yes. If it starts at 6:30, go down right at opening, keep it simple, and leave the hotel by about 7:05. If it starts at 7:00, skip the hotel breakfast that morning and grab coffee or something portable near the meeting instead.
What about getting to the convention center from SpringHill in snow?

In clear weather, it is a manageable walk or short rail/rideshare hop. With snow, don’t make the shoes-and-sidewalks gamble before a conference day: use a rideshare Tuesday midday and Wednesday morning if it is actively snowing. For later in the day, you can decide based on conditions.
My return flight Thursday is 5:35 p.m. How early should I leave the closing session?

Leave no later than 2:45 p.m.; 2:30 is better if snow is falling. That gives you time to retrieve your bag, get to Union Station, catch an A Line train around the 3:15-3:30 window, and reach DEN with roughly 75-90 minutes before departure. If you are still in the session at 3:00, switch to rideshare instead of trying to thread the rail timing.
And seat selection?

Check the seat map now and again at check-in. If a window is open on either leg, take it; if the return map is blocked, set a reminder for the 24-hour check-in mark. Also keep one dinner backup near the hotel for Tuesday night—Union Station/Auraria area is easier than searching around the convention center after a long day.

messages.content: New non-work one: my younger one’s soccer team finalized a Phoenix-area tournament. We need SLC flights and a Friday-to-Monday hotel. Friday evening team check-in, Saturday games in Mesa and Gilbert, and maybe a Sunday late-afternoon final.

Got it. For this one I’d compare PHX flights first, then hotel zones in the East Valley. A Sunday late final is the big decision point: flying home Sunday night can work only if the final is early enough and you are okay leaving straight from the field. Monday morning is calmer but costs a school/work morning. Do you know the Friday check-in time and whether a parent must be there?
Check-in is 7:30 p.m. Friday in Mesa. A parent should be there. I’d rather not pull her out before lunch, but I also don’t want to land at 7 and panic.

Then I’d avoid any itinerary landing after about 5:45 p.m. PHX is safer than Mesa Gateway because it has more nonstop choices and easier rental car backup if there’s a delay. Shortlist:

- SLC-PHX about 3:20-5:05 nonstop: best balance after a partial school day, still enough time to get the car and drive to Mesa.
- SLC-PHX about 1:45-3:30 nonstop: more buffer, but pulls her earlier.
- SLC-PHX about 5:40-7:20 nonstop: too tight for a 7:30 check-in.

If the 3:20 fare is reasonable, that is the one I’d hold.
Use Delta if it’s close, but not if Southwest or American is much better. There are three of us: me, my spouse, and the player.

Perfect. For three people with gear, I’d price Delta, Southwest, and American nonstops together and include bag rules in the comparison. If Delta is within roughly $30-40 per person of the best nonstop and the times match, choose it; otherwise take the better timed nonstop. For the room, look for two queens or a queen/king plus sofa bed rather than a single-bed room.
What hotel area makes sense if the fields are Mesa one day and Gilbert the next?

I’d focus on Gilbert/SanTan Village or southeast Mesa. Quick comparison:

- Gilbert/SanTan Village: usually 15-20 minutes to Gilbert fields, 20-30 to Mesa fields, lots of dinner options, easy Target/pharmacy runs. Best all-around for a family tournament.
- Mesa Riverview/Cubs area: good restaurant cluster and easier from PHX, but can be 30+ minutes to far-east Mesa or south Gilbert fields.
- Downtown Mesa: workable for check-in, but fewer family-friendly hotel clusters and dinner choices.
- Chandler edge: good hotels, but only choose it if rates are much better or the Sunday field is closer to Chandler.

My first pass would be SanTan Village/Gilbert.
Breakfast matters because first games can be early. Parking too. I don’t want a resort fee situation.

Then skip resort-style properties. Look at limited-service or suite hotels with breakfast and free parking. Examples to compare in the Gilbert/SanTan area:

1. Hampton Inn & Suites Phoenix/Gilbert or Gilbert/SanTan-adjacent: breakfast included, free parking, two-queen rooms often available.
2. Home2 Suites Gilbert: breakfast included, kitchenette, more space for gear, usually free parking.
3. Hyatt Place Phoenix/Gilbert area if available: larger room with sofa bed, breakfast may depend on rate/member terms, so verify before booking.

For dinner after games, SanTan Village is the easiest of those zones.
Can you put flights and hotel choice together? I’m still unsure about Sunday night versus Monday morning.

For the whole package, I’d pair:

Outbound Friday: SLC-PHX nonstop around 3:20 p.m., arriving around 5:05 p.m. Pick up rental car at PHX and drive straight to Mesa check-in. That leaves a realistic cushion.

Hotel: Home2 Suites or Hampton in Gilbert/SanTan Village, Friday-Monday, two queens or a suite with sofa bed, breakfast included, free parking confirmed. This keeps both Mesa and Gilbert fields manageable and makes dinner easy.

Return: Monday morning unless the Sunday final is canceled or scheduled before mid-afternoon. A late-afternoon final plus awards makes Sunday airport timing too fragile.
What Sunday flight would be the cutoff if we tried it?

For PHX, I would only consider a nonstop departing 8:30 p.m. or later, and even then only if the final ends by about 5:45 and you can go directly from the field to the airport. That assumes no long awards, no dinner stop, and a rental return that goes smoothly. Anything before 8:00 p.m. is too rushed with a possible late final.
The possible final is listed as 4:30, with awards after. So Monday sounds better. But I don’t want Monday to be brutal.

Then choose a Monday return that is early but not pre-dawn. Ideal target is PHX-SLC around 8:30-9:30 a.m., arriving late morning. You would leave the Gilbert hotel around 6:15-6:45 depending on the exact flight, return the car, and still have a decent airport buffer. A 6:00 a.m. flight saves school time but makes everyone miserable after a tournament weekend.
Could we do carry-ons only? Soccer bag is the unknown.

For three people, carry-ons plus one checked soccer/gear bag is more realistic. Price that into the fare comparison. Southwest may look better if bags are included; Delta or American may still win if the schedule is cleaner and the fare gap is small. I would not choose a connection just to save on bags for this weekend.
Good point. What about renting a car versus Ubering?

Rent a car. With Mesa/Gilbert fields, early games, gear, and a possible Sunday final, rideshares will become annoying and may not save much. Book a midsize SUV or roomy sedan at PHX, Friday evening pickup to Monday morning return. Keep the rental return time aligned with the flight so you do not pay for an unnecessary extra day.
Let’s say hotel budget under $220 before taxes if possible. I’d rather pay a little more for breakfast and parking than chase a cheaper room.

That budget should be workable if you book soon. I’d rank the hotel options like this:

1. Home2 Suites Gilbert/SanTan area under $220: best space, kitchenette, breakfast, gear-friendly.
2. Hampton Inn & Suites Gilbert/SanTan area under $210: simplest choice, breakfast and parking usually straightforward.
3. Hyatt Place only if breakfast is clearly included and parking is free; otherwise drop it.

If all three jump above $240, widen to Mesa Riverview before going to Chandler.
Okay, final recommendation?

Book this plan:

- Friday outbound: SLC-PHX nonstop around 3:20 p.m., arriving about 5:05 p.m.; choose Delta if it is close in price, otherwise the best nonstop with that timing.
- Return: Monday PHX-SLC nonstop around 8:30-9:30 a.m.; avoid Sunday unless the final disappears or moves much earlier.
- Hotel: Home2 Suites Gilbert/SanTan area first, Hampton Gilbert second, Friday-Monday, two queens or a suite with sofa bed, breakfast included, free parking, no resort/destination fee.
- Ground: PHX rental car, roomy sedan or midsize SUV, Friday pickup/Monday return.

Before paying, confirm the exact field addresses, hotel breakfast hours on Saturday/Sunday, whether parking is truly free, and the cancellation deadline in case the tournament schedule changes.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa prioritized field proximity, early breakfast, two-queen bedding, and cancellation flexibility for the Mesa tournament. She remained wary of nonrefundable hotel terms while tournament brackets and Sunday field assignments were still uncertain.

messages.content: The Mesa tournament finally posted site assignments, and it changes the hotel question. Most of Saturday is at the far southeast Mesa complex, not the central fields. The team block is a two-queen room near Gilbert/SanTan with early breakfast, but the cancellation cutoff is tomorrow. The airport-area hotel is cheaper and nicer for our Monday flight. Can you help me rank the areas before I do something nonrefundable?

Yes. I’d base this on the worst driving moments, not just the average. Can you remind me of the Saturday game times, Monday flight time, and whether Sunday is also likely to be at the southeast Mesa site?

Saturday is 8:00, 2:15, and maybe 7:00 at Arizona Athletic Grounds. Sunday depends on the bracket, but the likely final is there too. Monday PHX-SLC is 9:20 a.m. We’ll have a rental car. Block hotel is about $214, airport Hyatt Place is $169, Chandler options are around $190 to $205.

That pushes the field-side area to the top.

1. Gilbert/SanTan or southeast Mesa: best for the 8:00 start and the possible 7:00 game. Also easiest if Sunday ends late.
2. Chandler/Ocotillo or Chandler Fashion area: good compromise, especially if you want a refundable room and restaurants nearby.
3. Airport/Sky Harbor area: only best for Monday morning. It creates the longest drives when everyone is tired and gear-heavy.

For Monday, a field-side hotel still works. I’d plan to leave around 6:15-6:30 a.m. for a 9:20 flight.
The block becomes basically nonrefundable after tomorrow night. I’m nervous because youth soccer schedules have lied to me before.

Then I would not prepay the block unless the room terms are clearly refundable through the weekend schedule release. Safer move: hold a refundable Chandler or Gilbert/SanTan option tonight, then switch to the block only if the bracket confirms the southeast-heavy plan before the cutoff.
If rates are within twenty dollars, is Chandler still worth considering?

If the field-side room is refundable, I’d take field-side over Chandler within $20. If the field-side room is nonrefundable and Chandler is refundable, I’d take Chandler. The extra drive is tolerable; the nonrefundable risk is the bigger problem right now.
Room setup matters too. Three of us, tired teenager, gear bag.

Choose two queens over one queen plus sofa bed if prices are close. If it’s a suite, confirm the sofa bed is a true pullout and not just a couch. Also check whether the room has enough floor space for the soccer bag without blocking the door.
Okay, give me the ranking and timing in one place.

Book in this order:

1. Refundable Gilbert/SanTan or southeast Mesa, two queens, breakfast starting by 6:00-6:30.
2. Refundable Chandler, preferably near Loop 202/101 with easy dinner options.
3. Tournament block only if the cancellation terms are acceptable after you call.
4. Airport area only if Sunday becomes light or all field-side/Chandler rooms get bad.

Timing: hold the refundable room now; do not pay nonrefundable until the bracket risk is clearer.
What do I need to verify before clicking anything nonrefundable?

Verify these before paying:

- Exact cancellation deadline, time zone, and whether the first night or full stay is forfeited.
- Room is two queen beds, not doubles, and not “run of house.”
- Breakfast start time on Saturday and Sunday; ask if grab-and-go is available before 6:30.
- Free parking and no resort, destination, or tournament service fee.
- Drive time to Arizona Athletic Grounds and the Sunday alternate site.
- Late check-in policy for Friday after the 7:30 check-in.
- Fridge availability for drinks/snacks.

If any of those are vague, keep the refundable Chandler/Gilbert room instead.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa established the Northern California event sequence, preferred a Monday outbound landing by mid-afternoon for the Sacramento reception, wanted practical hotels under about $190 before tax with breakfast and dinner access, and prioritized clean routing and transfer reliability over carrier loyalty.

I just don’t want to arrive somewhere with no dinner around.

messages.content: I’m back to work travel. I need to rough out a Northern California swing in February: Monday evening admitted-student reception in Sacramento, Tuesday morning community-college fair in Stockton, Wednesday counselor lunch in Walnut Creek, and Thursday morning coffee with families near Santa Rosa. I’m trying to decide whether this is Sacramento in and Oakland home, or just Sacramento round trip with more driving.
Good one to map before buying flights. What are the event times, and do you have a hotel cap or rental-car constraint? Also, can you travel Sunday, or does Monday need to be the outbound?

Monday outbound is preferred. The reception is 6:00-8:00 p.m. in midtown Sacramento. Tuesday fair is 8:30-11:00 in Stockton. Wednesday lunch is 12:30-2:00 in Walnut Creek. Thursday coffee is 9:30-10:30 near Santa Rosa. Hotel cap is around $190 before tax. Breakfast and easy dinner matter because these are long days. I’ll need a rental car. Delta is fine if it’s clean, but don’t make the routing worse for that.

Two realistic shapes:

Option A: SLC to Sacramento, home from Oakland. This can reduce some Thursday backtracking, but only if the Oakland flight is mid-afternoon or later and the one-way car price is not ugly.

Option B: Sacramento round trip. Simpler rental car, likely simpler flight search, and Sacramento is still usable after Santa Rosa if you keep a healthy Thursday buffer.

I’d rule out any Monday flight that lands after about 3:00 p.m.; the 6:00 reception would feel too tight after rental car pickup and hotel check-in.
No Sunday unless Monday is truly unreliable. I’d rather land by 2:30 or 3:00, get the car, check in, and not sprint into the reception.

Then search Monday SLC-SMF departures late morning to early afternoon, landing Sacramento by 2:30 if possible. If the only nonstop lands much later, compare one short connection that still lands before 3:00. Reliability matters more here than squeezing in a later work morning.
Is staying in Sacramento Monday night okay for an 8:30 fair in Stockton?

Yes, with an early start. From midtown or east Sacramento to Stockton, I’d budget 50-70 minutes at that hour. Leave around 6:55-7:05, earlier if the fair site has difficult parking. Staying in Stockton Monday would help the morning drive but would make the reception night less convenient.
I’d rather not stay in Stockton. After the fair I have follow-up calls, so I need somewhere I can land for the afternoon.

After the Stockton fair, I’d drive toward the East Bay before the afternoon commute builds. Walnut Creek, Pleasant Hill, or Concord would let you check in, take calls, and be close to Wednesday lunch without another early drive.
Can you give me hotel zones, not names yet, and note food logistics?

Sure.

Monday: Midtown Sacramento, East Sacramento, or Cal Expo/Arden. Midtown has the easiest dinner; Cal Expo/Arden often has practical chain hotels and parking.

Tuesday: Walnut Creek, Pleasant Hill, or Concord near BART/retail centers. Better dinner access than Stockton and close to the Wednesday lunch.

Wednesday: Santa Rosa, Rohnert Park, or possibly Petaluma. Santa Rosa has the best dinner choices; Rohnert Park may price better; Petaluma is a useful halfway compromise if Santa Rosa rates are high.
Could I just do two East Bay nights Tuesday and Wednesday so I’m not moving bags again?

You could, but Thursday becomes more pressure. From Walnut Creek or Pleasant Hill to Santa Rosa, plan 75-100 minutes with traffic uncertainty. For a 9:30 coffee, that means leaving around 7:15-7:30. Moving north Wednesday after lunch makes Thursday calmer, but it adds one more checkout and hotel search.
Wednesday lunch ends at 2:00, so I could drive north afterward. I just don’t want to arrive somewhere with no dinner around.

That argues for driving north Wednesday and staying near Santa Rosa or Rohnert Park. You’d leave Walnut Creek around 2:15, likely arrive before the worst dinner-hour scramble, and have a shorter Thursday morning. I’d pick a hotel with breakfast included or at least coffee/market access, plus a restaurant cluster within a few minutes.
Open-jaw into Sacramento and out of Oakland looks about $80 more than Sacramento round trip before I check the car. Is that worth it?

Not automatically. From Santa Rosa, Oakland can be faster on paper, but it is not always more reliable. Sacramento is a backtrack, yet the drive is straightforward enough if the return flight is mid- to late afternoon. I’d keep both in the search until you compare total cost and exact departure times.
Right, and the rental may have a one-way fee.

Exactly. Compare the all-in version: airfare plus rental car plus parking and taxes. If Oakland adds $80 airfare and a one-way car fee, it only wins if the flight time is much better. If Sacramento has a clean return around 3:30-5:00 p.m., Sacramento round trip is probably the more practical baseline.
Give me the first-pass itinerary and what to search tonight.

First-pass plan:

- Monday: Fly SLC-SMF, landing by 2:30-3:00. Pick up the rental car at SMF, stay Sacramento near midtown/east side/Cal Expo, attend 6:00 reception.
- Tuesday: Leave around 7:00 for Stockton. After the fair, drive to Walnut Creek/Pleasant Hill/Concord and stay there Tuesday night.
- Wednesday: Counselor lunch, then drive north mid-afternoon. Stay Santa Rosa/Rohnert Park/Petaluma depending on rate, breakfast, and nearby dinner.
- Thursday: Family coffee near Santa Rosa, then return from either SMF or OAK only if the flight gives real buffer.

Search tonight: SLC-SMF Monday arrivals before 3:00; Thursday SMF-SLC departures 3:30-5:30; then compare OAK-SLC only if it departs after about 3:00 and the rental car total is reasonable.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: After the Northern California schedule changes, Tessa favored a reimbursable, low-stress plan over minimizing hotel moves or forcing an Oakland return. The recommendation became a Rohnert Park Wednesday night under cap and a Sacramento return for better buffer and lower rental complexity.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: Pleasant Hill hotels are about $185 with breakfast and restaurants nearby.
What about the Rohnert Park option? It’s under cap, just less interesting for dinner.

messages.content: Two Northern California updates: the Wednesday lunch moved from Walnut Creek to Pleasant Hill, and the Santa Rosa coffee shifted later. I’m now wondering if I really need a Santa Rosa-area hotel Wednesday night. Can we revise before I book?
Yes. What time is the Santa Rosa coffee now, and what are you seeing for East Bay versus Santa Rosa/Rohnert Park hotel rates? Also, which Thursday return flights are the contenders?

Coffee is 10:30-11:30 near Montgomery Village. Pleasant Hill hotels are about $185 with breakfast and restaurants nearby. Santa Rosa is $220-plus, which is over cap. Rohnert Park has one around $189 with breakfast but mostly fast-casual nearby. OAK has a 3:40 nonstop. SMF has a 4:15 nonstop. Oakland adds about $65 on the rental.

This makes two plans viable. Two East Bay nights are now reasonable because the coffee is later, and Pleasant Hill fits the cap with better dinner access. Rohnert Park is still the calmer Thursday morning, but I would not pay over-cap for central Santa Rosa.
I assumed Oakland would be the obvious return if I’m already near Santa Rosa.

Oakland is not a slam dunk here. After an 11:30 coffee, you would want to leave almost immediately for a 3:40 OAK flight, and Bay Area traffic can eat the cushion. Sacramento at 4:15 is a little more backtrack, but the buffer is better and the car cost is cleaner.
Would staying two nights in Pleasant Hill make Thursday too long?

It makes Thursday full, not unreasonable. You’d leave Pleasant Hill around 8:00, aiming to reach Santa Rosa by 9:45-10:00. After coffee, drive to SMF for the 4:15. That is a lot of car time, but it avoids another hotel move and keeps you under cap.
What about the Rohnert Park option? It’s under cap, just less interesting for dinner.

Rohnert Park is a good compromise if the room is cancellable and the breakfast hours work. It shortens Thursday morning, keeps you out of the over-cap Santa Rosa rates, and still leaves a solid drive to SMF after coffee. I’d just pick a property with at least two dinner backups within a short drive.
I don’t need interesting. I need low-stress and reimbursable. Which would you book?

I’d book Sacramento Monday, Pleasant Hill Tuesday, Rohnert Park Wednesday, and return from Sacramento at 4:15. That is the least stressful version that still respects the cap: close enough for the Thursday coffee, no over-cap Santa Rosa room, and a safer airport buffer than Oakland.
So should I keep Oakland in the flight search at all?

Keep Oakland only as a backup if the price drops or a later flight appears. I would not book the 3:40 OAK option with the rental surcharge unless Sacramento becomes much worse.

Before booking, verify the Rohnert Park cancellation deadline, breakfast start time, exact bed setup, parking fee, and two nearby dinner options. Then book the SMF 4:15 return and plan to leave the coffee by 11:45.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa chose the Oakland open-jaw return after a later OAK flight and modest one-way rental fee made it more reliable than backtracking to Sacramento. She considered hotel breakfast, nearby dinner access, cancellation deadlines, parking, bedding, and window seat selection as practical booking checks.

Seat map has 15A on the SLC-SMF leg and 18F on OAK-SLC. Both window seats. I’m ready to click unless you see a problem.

messages.content: The Oakland option changed since we last looked, so I need a real booking call. I can do Monday SLC to Sacramento, arrive 1:45-ish, then Thursday either Oakland at 4:55 or Sacramento at 5:25. The Oakland rental drop adds $38 all-in. Is that enough to make the open-jaw worth it?

Probably, but I want to verify the Thursday morning constraint before I push you toward the earlier airport. Is the Santa Rosa coffee still 10:30 to 11:30, and do you need to return rental materials or check a bag before flying?

Coffee is 10:30 to 11:30 near downtown Santa Rosa. I need to be there about 10:15 to bring brochures in. No checked bag. I’ll have a roller and a box of viewbooks in the car, but I can ship leftovers if needed.

That changes the earlier call: I would book Oakland. Even though the Sacramento flight leaves 30 minutes later, it makes you backtrack east from Santa Rosa and adds more exposure to Highway 37/I-80 slowdowns. With Oakland, you can leave the coffee around 11:40, reach the rental return around 1:20 to 1:50 in normal traffic, and still have a strong buffer for a 4:55 departure. The $38 one-way rental add is reasonable for the shorter route.

Good. For hotels, I found Residence Inn Sacramento Cal Expo for Monday, Homewood Suites Pleasant Hill for Tuesday, and Hampton Inn in Santa Rosa for Wednesday. All have breakfast listed. The Santa Rosa one has the tightest cancellation deadline, though.

That sequence is practical. Monday: Residence Inn Cal Expo keeps parking easy after the Sacramento reception and should have breakfast before you drive to Stockton. Tuesday: Homewood Pleasant Hill is a good East Bay landing spot with easy dinner options nearby and a shorter hop to the Wednesday counselor lunch. Wednesday: Hampton Santa Rosa is the best fit if the coffee location is firm, because you avoid a Thursday morning northbound drive. The cancellation deadline is the main watch item.

Santa Rosa cancellation is this Friday at 6 p.m. Mountain. The host says the coffee is very likely but not 100 percent locked until Thursday afternoon. Petaluma is $22 cheaper and cancels the day before, but it’s farther south.

I’d hold the Santa Rosa room if it is fully cancelable until Friday and set a Thursday 4 p.m. reminder to reconfirm the coffee. Petaluma only wins if the coffee has a real chance of moving south or canceling. For the Thursday timing you described, sleeping in Santa Rosa is worth the $22.
Rental car pickup and drop-off: anything special? I’ve never done SMF pickup and OAK drop on the same reservation.

Book it as one reservation: pickup SMF around 2:15 Monday, drop OAK around 1:45 Thursday. Before paying, confirm the total includes the one-way fee, not just an estimated base rate. Also check whether the toll program is automatic; the Santa Rosa-to-Oakland route may use the Richmond-San Rafael Bridge, and rental toll plans can be pricey if you only use one bridge.
Flights are Delta Main. Seat map has 15A on the SLC-SMF leg and 18F on OAK-SLC. Both window seats. I’m ready to click unless you see a problem.

Click in this order: flight first, rental second, hotels third. Take 15A and 18F, then save the fare receipt and rental total for reimbursement. For hotels, confirm queen or king bedding, breakfast start times, parking fees, and cancellation time zones. Final route: Monday fly into SMF, sleep Sacramento; Tuesday Stockton then Pleasant Hill; Wednesday East Bay lunch then Santa Rosa; Thursday coffee, leave by 11:40, return car at OAK, fly home at 4:55.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: The assistant confirmed the Oakland return remained the safer choice after a 15-minute schedule change, using the coffee timing, no checked bag, rental return buffer, breakfast start time, parking note, and receipt needs.

messages.content: Quick NoCal check: I booked the Sacramento inbound, Oakland return, and the three hotels. Delta just moved OAK-SLC from 4:55 to 4:40. The Santa Rosa host also says park in the west lot and bring materials inside before 10:00. Do I still keep Oakland?

If the coffee still ends by 11:30 and you are not checking a bag, yes, Oakland still looks better than switching back to Sacramento. The 15-minute shift tightens the margin a little but does not flip the decision.
Coffee is 10:30 to 11:30. I can arrive by 9:50 with the brochures. No checked bag. Hampton breakfast starts at 6:00.

Good. Thursday plan: breakfast 7:15, pack and load by 8:15, check out by 8:30, arrive at the west lot around 9:40 to 9:50, carry materials in before 10:00, coffee 10:30 to 11:30, leave by 11:40. Aim for OAK rental return by 1:45. That gives roughly 2 hours 55 minutes before departure.
What about the Wednesday drive from Pleasant Hill to Santa Rosa? I don’t want to hit the worst of it if I can help it.

Leave Pleasant Hill either right after your Wednesday lunch block, around 2:00 to 2:30, or wait until after 6:30. I would take the earlier window if you can. It gives you daylight, easier check-in, and time for dinner in Santa Rosa instead of arriving tired.
Receipts and checkout stuff?

Keep Oakland. Switch to Sacramento only if the coffee slides past noon or Delta moves OAK earlier again. Receipts: airfare confirmation, rental final estimate and fuel receipt, each hotel folio, parking if charged, and any bridge toll record. At Hampton, ask for the folio at checkout even if it also emails later, and keep the west-lot parking note with the trip file.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa prioritized reliable routing, afternoon departure from SLC, avoiding long or risky connections, easy breakfasts, parking, and dinner logistics around event timing.
