messages.content: Northern California is settled, so I’m starting the Puget Sound yield loop. Late March: Tuesday morning counselor breakfast in Everett, Tuesday evening admitted-student reception in Bellevue, Wednesday transfer fair in Tacoma, Thursday morning high-school visit in Olympia. I need flights from SLC, a rental car, and hotel zones that won’t make the mornings awful.
Got it. Before I compare airports and hotel zones, what are the event times, and can you fly up Monday? The Everett breakfast makes arrival day important.

Yes, fly Monday. I can leave SLC after noon. Everett breakfast is Tuesday 8:00 to 9:30. Bellevue reception is 6:30 to 8:00 Tuesday night. Tacoma fair is Wednesday 10:00 to 1:00. Olympia visit is Thursday 9:00 to 10:45.

Then I would shape it north to south: fly in Monday, sleep near Everett or north Lynnwood; Tuesday breakfast in Everett, then Bellevue reception; sleep somewhere that reduces the Wednesday Tacoma drive; Wednesday fair, then move to Olympia/Tumwater; Thursday visit, then drive to the airport for an afternoon flight home.
I’m okay changing hotels each night if it saves morning stress. Free breakfast and parking would help. I also need an easy dinner plan after Bellevue because reception food is usually snacks.

For airports: Seattle-Tacoma is the safer baseline because it has more SLC flights and rental-car inventory. Paine Field is attractive for Everett, but only if the schedule is clean and the car pickup hours work. For the return, SEA is much better than Paine because you’ll be coming from Olympia.

Paine has a Monday option that connects through Boise and gets in at 8:45 p.m. SEA has a 1:35 nonstop landing around 2:45 and a 3:20 nonstop landing around 4:30. Include Delta if it’s comparable, but don’t make the trip worse for it.

I’d skip the Paine connection. It lands late, adds a transfer risk, and still leaves you picking up a car at night. Take the SEA nonstop if the fare is reasonable. The 1:35 departure is strongest because you can drive north before the worst evening traffic; the 3:20 works but may put you into Everett closer to dinner rush.
Where should Monday night be? Everett is running higher than Lynnwood.

If Everett is within about $35 to $45 of Lynnwood, stay Everett and remove the Tuesday morning variable. If the gap is bigger, use north Lynnwood, not south of Alderwood if possible. Look for Hampton, Holiday Inn Express, Homewood, or similar business hotels with breakfast and free parking. For an 8:00 breakfast, I would not stay downtown Seattle.
Tuesday night is the messy one. After Bellevue, should I sleep in Bellevue or start toward Tacoma?

Because the reception ends at 8:00 and you still need real dinner, I would not force a full drive to Tacoma unless you feel wide awake. A good compromise is dinner in Bellevue right after the reception, then drive 25 to 40 minutes to Renton, Tukwila, SeaTac, or Federal Way. That cuts the Wednesday morning drive without a very late arrival.
I can handle 30 to 45 minutes after dinner. I’d rather not get to a hotel after 10:00.

Then aim for Renton or Federal Way. Renton is easier right after Bellevue and has plenty of food nearby; Federal Way puts you closer to Tacoma Wednesday morning. If you leave Bellevue after dinner around 8:45, Renton is usually the less tiring choice. If you eat quickly and leave by 8:20, Federal Way is worth pricing.
And Wednesday night before Olympia?

Stay Olympia or Tumwater, not Tacoma. After the fair ends at 1:00, you can drive south, check in, regroup, and have a normal dinner. Tumwater often has easier parking and practical breakfast hotels; downtown Olympia has better walkable restaurants. For the 9:00 visit, either is fine, but Tumwater is usually simpler with a rental car.
Is Thursday afternoon realistic for flying home from SEA? I don’t want to turn the Olympia visit into a dash.

Yes, if you book a flight after about 3:00 p.m.; after 3:30 is more comfortable. If the visit ends by 10:45, leave Olympia around 11:00, reach the SEA rental return roughly 12:30 to 1:15 depending on traffic, and still have a decent airport buffer. I would not book anything before 2:30.
Okay. What should I search tonight?

Search in this order: Monday SLC-SEA nonstop departing after noon, with the 1:35-ish option first; Thursday SEA-SLC nonstop after 3:00, ideally 3:30 to 6:00; rental car SEA pickup Monday afternoon and drop Thursday around 1:00; Monday hotel Everett/north Lynnwood; Tuesday hotel Renton/Federal Way/Tukwila; Wednesday hotel Olympia/Tumwater.
Can you put that into a simple shortlist with the trade-offs? I’ll price it after dinner.

Shortlist: 1) Best route: fly SLC-SEA Monday early afternoon, rental car at SEA, return SEA-SLC Thursday after 3:30. Trade-off: SEA is farther from Everett than Paine, but much more reliable overall. 2) Monday hotel: Everett if the rate gap is modest; north Lynnwood if Everett is too high. Trade-off: Lynnwood saves money but adds a Tuesday morning drive. 3) Tuesday hotel: Renton if you want the easiest post-reception night; Federal Way if you want the smoother Wednesday morning. Trade-off: dinner timing decides it. 4) Wednesday hotel: Olympia/Tumwater. Trade-off: Tumwater is simpler for parking and breakfast; Olympia is better for restaurants. Before booking, verify breakfast start times, parking charges, cancellation deadlines, and whether the rental total changes if Thursday drop-off is later than 1:00.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: User reported the Redmond venue change and earlier Tacoma setup, confirmed no hosted dinner after the reception, and accepted one longer Tuesday-night drive to improve Wednesday morning reliability. Tentative hotel sequence became Monday Redmond/north Bellevue and Tuesday-Wednesday Federal Way, with breakfast timing and cancellation deadlines still to verify.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: The Redmond hotel I liked is still refundable but breakfast isn’t included anymore. Federal Way is $45 cheaper, has breakfast, and is better for Tacoma. Can you re-rank the hotel sequence?
What about dinner after Redmond if I drive south? I don’t want to arrive hungry at 9:30 and have nothing.

messages.content: The Puget Sound plan got annoying. The Bellevue reception is now in Redmond, not Bellevue, Tuesday 6:30-8:00. Tacoma transfer fair wants table setup by 7:30 Wednesday. The Redmond hotel I liked is still refundable but breakfast isn’t included anymore. Federal Way is $45 cheaper, has breakfast, and is better for Tacoma. Can you re-rank the hotel sequence?

Yes. Because the Tacoma setup is early, I’d weight Wednesday-morning drive reliability over the Redmond breakfast issue. Do you have any hosted dinner after the Redmond reception, or can you leave as soon as it wraps?
No hosted dinner. I may need 10 minutes to box materials, so realistically I’m in the car at 8:15 or 8:20. I don’t love a longer late drive, but it’s not unsafe-late.

Then my ranking is: 1) Monday Redmond or north Bellevue, Tuesday plus Wednesday Federal Way. Best overall: one longer post-reception drive, then no Wednesday checkout and an easier Tacoma morning. 2) Monday plus Tuesday Redmond, Wednesday Federal Way. More comfortable Tuesday night, but Wednesday morning Redmond-to-Tacoma is the least reliable piece. 3) Monday Lynnwood/Everett, Tuesday Redmond, Wednesday Federal Way. Best for reducing individual drive lengths, but three check-ins is fussy.
Would you put Renton or Tukwila between Redmond and Federal Way, or does that just split the difference badly?

Renton or Tukwila is a reasonable fallback, not the lead. It shortens the Tuesday night drive by maybe 15-20 minutes versus Federal Way, but you give some of that time back Wednesday morning and still have more traffic exposure before a fixed setup time. Federal Way is cleaner if the rate and cancellation terms are good.

The Federal Way option is Home2 Suites near the mall, free breakfast, free parking, cancel until 6 pm the day before. Redmond is a Hyatt House, parking $18, no included breakfast on the rate I see, cancel 48 hours out.

That pushes me further toward one Redmond night and two Federal Way nights. Hyatt House is acceptable for Monday because you can solve Tuesday breakfast with a coffee stop or grocery run. The Federal Way terms are better for the part of the trip where timing matters most.
What about dinner after Redmond if I drive south? I don’t want to arrive hungry at 9:30 and have nothing.

Plan dinner before leaving Redmond if the reception food is light: pick up something near the venue or order ahead for 8:10. If you leave by 8:25, Federal Way should still be a late-evening arrival rather than a night-owl arrival. I would not count on a full sit-down dinner after you check in.
Okay, so rank is Redmond one night, Federal Way two nights. Any reason to keep Olympia/Tumwater for Wednesday?

Only if the Thursday Olympia appointment becomes very early or the Federal Way rate loses free cancellation. Tumwater or Olympia improves Thursday morning and dinner options, but it adds another hotel move and makes Wednesday evening less efficient after Tacoma. With the current 7:30 Tacoma setup, the bigger win is sleeping south before Wednesday.
Good. Put the final sequence in plain English so I can price it tonight.

Got it. I’d treat Denver as the main airport and Colorado Springs as a possible return only if the times are clean. For the hotels, the first-night zone is the real trade-off: Fort Collins is easiest Tuesday night, Boulder is easiest Wednesday morning, and Longmont is the middle ground.

Then Longmont is probably the practical first pick. It keeps Tuesday night from becoming a full Boulder drive, makes the Wednesday breakfast reachable in about 25-35 minutes in normal morning traffic, and chain hotels there are more likely to include breakfast and parking than central Boulder.
Can you compare Fort Collins, Longmont, and Boulder plainly? I keep talking myself into all three.

Short version: Fort Collins means easiest dinner/bed after the reception, but you would need a very early departure for Boulder, likely around 6:00. Boulder means the calmest 7:30 breakfast, but a longer late Tuesday drive plus higher rates and parking fees. Longmont is not perfect, but it spreads the inconvenience: about 40-50 minutes after Fort Collins, then 25-35 minutes to Boulder.
What about the Wednesday Aurora table and Thursday Colorado Springs visit? I don’t want to solve one morning and create a worse one.

That points to a split stay. I’d pencil Longmont for Monday and Tuesday nights, then move south after the Aurora table on Wednesday. South Denver/DTC, southeast Aurora, or Castle Rock would all beat staying north for the Colorado Springs morning. DTC is the safest balance for dinner, hotels, and highway access.
Would you put me in Colorado Springs Wednesday night instead?

Only if the Aurora table ends early enough. Aurora to Colorado Springs after an event can be 75-100 minutes, and dinner gets less flexible if you arrive late. DTC or Castle Rock lets you get south of Denver without committing to the whole drive after a long Wednesday.
Okay. For flights, is there any reason to return from Colorado Springs instead of just Denver round trip?

There could be, but I’d be cautious. Denver round trip gives you nonstop choices SLC-DEN both ways and simpler car pricing. Colorado Springs return avoids the drive back north, but many COS-SLC options connect through DEN, PHX, or DFW. If the Thursday visit runs long, a COS connection can become the fragile piece.
The Thursday school visit starts at 9 and should be done by 10:45. I could leave Colorado Springs by 11 if no one needs extra time.

Then a late-afternoon Denver return is probably better than a midday Colorado Springs connection. From Colorado Springs to DEN, budget 90 minutes driving plus rental return and security. A Denver departure around 4:30-5:30 gives you a real cushion; earlier than 3:30 would feel rushed.
What would your rough itinerary be before we price actual flights and hotels?

Monday: afternoon nonstop SLC-DEN, pick up the rental at DEN, drive to Longmont, sleep there. Tuesday: use Longmont as the base, then Fort Collins reception, return to Longmont after. Wednesday: leave Longmont around 6:40 for Boulder breakfast, check out beforehand if possible, drive to Aurora for the transfer table, then sleep DTC or nearby south Denver. Thursday: drive to Colorado Springs, finish the visit, return the car at DEN, fly home late afternoon.
If we end up in Boulder because rates drop, does that change the airport recommendation?

No. Boulder would make Wednesday morning easier but does not change the flight logic. I’d still use DEN round trip unless Colorado Springs has a clean, well-timed one-stop with a comfortable connection and a fare that justifies the extra moving parts.
Give me the shortlist to research tonight.

Research these three paths: 1) Best balance: DEN round trip, Longmont Monday-Tuesday, DTC/south Denver Wednesday. 2) Maximum Wednesday-morning comfort: DEN round trip, Boulder Monday-Tuesday if under cap and cancellation is reasonable, DTC Wednesday. 3) Lowest late-Tuesday effort: Fort Collins Monday-Tuesday, then DTC Wednesday, but only if you accept a very early Boulder departure. messages.content: Switching from conference travel to kid logistics: we have a mid-July Boise-area tournament weekend. We’ll drive from Salt Lake after work Friday and stay two nights. Games may be split between Nampa and west Boise. I need a practical hotel area shortlist with two queens, parking, breakfast, and somewhere to get dinner after a late drive.

I can narrow that. What are the exact dates, how many people, and how early Saturday could start? The Nampa versus Meridian versus west Boise choice really changes if there is an 8:00 a.m. report time.
July 18 to 20, four of us, no pets. First game could be 8:00, but the schedule is not posted yet. We’d probably leave SLC around 4:30, so Boise arrival is more like 10:15 or 10:30.

Given the uncertainty, I’d compare three zones. Nampa is best if Saturday starts early there: shortest morning drive and often easier parking, but fewer late dinner choices. Meridian is the balanced option: usually 15 to 25 minutes to Nampa or west Boise, with better food access. West Boise is best for Friday-night restaurants and could be good if Sunday shifts that way, but it is the least forgiving for an early Nampa start.
Can you make that into a shortlist rather than just the areas?

Shortlist to check live inventory: 1) Hampton Inn & Suites Nampa/Idaho Center area, two-queen refundable room, free parking, breakfast often early enough for tournament mornings, closest to Nampa venues. 2) A Hampton, Homewood, or Tru in Meridian near Eagle Road, two queens if available, free parking, breakfast, best compromise location. 3) Home2 Suites Boise West or Hyatt Place Boise/Towne Square area, good dinner access and breakfast, but longer Saturday drive if Nampa gets the early slot.
The kids will be starving by then, and I don’t want to rely on a hotel pantry at 10:30.

That leans Meridian or west Boise. Around Eagle Road and west Boise you’ll have more late fast-casual options than Nampa. If you choose Nampa, I’d plan dinner in Twin Falls or Burley before the last stretch, or choose a specific Nampa restaurant and confirm the kitchen closing time before you leave Salt Lake.
Saturday morning matters too. If Nampa gets the 8:00 slot, how bad is west Boise?

It is doable but less relaxed. West Boise to a Nampa venue can be 25 to 35 minutes early on a weekend morning, so you might leave the hotel around 7:00 for a 7:35 or 7:40 arrival. Meridian is more forgiving, and Nampa is obviously easiest. Breakfast hours are the pinch: some hotels start at 6:30 on weekends, some later, so verify the actual Saturday time.
Let’s assume I can hold one now. Would you hold Meridian?

Yes, if there is a cancellable two-queen Meridian room with free parking and breakfast starting by 6:30, that is the best temporary hold while the schedule is unknown. If Meridian is too expensive or only nonrefundable, I’d hold west Boise over Nampa for now because of Friday food and possible Sunday flexibility, then switch to Nampa if the posted schedule confirms an early Nampa game.
What exact things should I check before entering the card?

Check the cancellation deadline in Mountain Time, that the room is specifically two queens and non-smoking, free self-parking, breakfast hours for both Saturday and Sunday, whether late arrival after 10:30 can be noted, and the drive times to the Nampa and west Boise venues. I’d also ask whether a Sunday late checkout can be requested at check-in, since brackets can run oddly.

And Sunday if the bracket moves to Meridian?

Okay, I’ll book Nampa. Should I ask for late checkout now or at check-in?

messages.content: I’m starting the first August recruitment loop and want to map it before I hold anything. Week of Aug. 19: Monday evening counselor reception in Spokane, Tuesday morning high-school visits near Coeur d’Alene, Wednesday afternoon transfer table in Pullman, and Thursday morning counselor breakfast in the Tri-Cities. I’ll be flying from Salt Lake City and need a rental car. Please include Delta if it fits, but don’t force it if the connection is worse. Hotels need easy breakfast, parking, and some reasonable dinner access after the evening pieces.

Yes. The big route decision is whether you fly home from Spokane again or return from Pasco after the Tri-Cities breakfast. Are you allowed to do an open-jaw flight and one-way rental car if the cost is defensible, or does reimbursement push you toward returning the car at the same airport? Also, what is the earliest you can leave SLC Monday?
Open-jaw is allowed if there’s a good reason. I have a campus kickoff until 10:30 Monday, so I can leave SLC after noon. I need to be in Spokane by about 5:00.

Then I’d shape the search this way: Option A, SLC to Spokane and Spokane back to SLC, is likely cheapest and keeps the rental simple, but it forces a Thursday backtrack from the Tri-Cities to Spokane after breakfast. Option B, SLC to Spokane and Pasco back to SLC, is cleaner for the actual loop and protects Thursday, but the one-way car may add a drop fee. Option C, flying into Pasco first, does not fit Monday because it creates too much driving before the Spokane reception. I’d search Monday SLC-GEG departing after noon and arriving by 5, then Thursday PSC-SLC after about 11:30, with a Spokane-return backup after midafternoon.
For Monday night, the reception is at a hotel near downtown Spokane but Tuesday’s first school is near Coeur d’Alene around 8:15. Should I stay downtown, Spokane Valley, or Coeur d’Alene?

I’d lean Spokane Valley or Liberty Lake rather than downtown or Coeur d’Alene. Downtown is easiest after the reception, but parking can be annoying and it leaves more morning drive. Coeur d’Alene makes Tuesday morning easy, but it asks you to drive 35 to 45 minutes after a long reception. Spokane Valley/Liberty Lake splits the difference: manageable post-reception drive, usually free parking, chain hotels with breakfast, and restaurants that stay open late enough for a quick dinner.
The reception could run to 8:45. I’d rather not do a long late drive after shaking hands all evening. Spokane Valley sounds okay if Tuesday morning isn’t awful.

That’s reasonable. From Spokane Valley you’re usually looking at about 30 to 40 minutes to central Coeur d’Alene, less if the school is in Post Falls. I’d filter Monday night for east Spokane Valley or Liberty Lake, free self-parking, breakfast that starts by 6:30, and restaurants or takeout within a few minutes. I would not pay a downtown premium unless the reception hotel itself is reimbursable and clearly easier.
The Tuesday night piece is harder. After the Coeur d’Alene visits I should be done around 1:00. Pullman rooms already look high. Is Lewiston too weird if I need Pullman Wednesday afternoon?

Lewiston is not weird if Wednesday is truly afternoon. Pullman is most convenient but likely inflated because of campus timing. Moscow is a good comfort middle ground, about 15 minutes from Pullman, but availability can be thin too. Lewiston or Clarkston is usually 40 to 50 minutes from Pullman, often cheaper, and better for parking and practical hotels. I would avoid sleeping all the way back in Spokane or Coeur d’Alene Tuesday because that makes Wednesday unnecessarily long.
No Wednesday morning event. There might be lunch with a transfer counselor at 11:45 in Pullman, but she hasn’t confirmed.

If that lunch confirms, Lewiston still works as long as you treat it like a real departure: leave by about 10:35 or 10:45, arrive Pullman with time to park, and do not rely on a last-minute hotel checkout. Moscow would give more cushion, but I wouldn’t spend a lot more for it unless the Lewiston option has weak cancellation terms or poor food access.
I can do a 45-minute drive to save a lot, but I don’t want a sketchy food situation. I’ll be alone.

Then for Tuesday I’d look at Lewiston/Clarkston hotels near the river, downtown, or a main commercial strip with an adjacent restaurant. I’d skip any isolated highway property where dinner means getting back in the car late. The useful filters are free parking, breakfast posted clearly, interior corridors if possible, and either on-site dinner or a restaurant within a short, well-lit walk.
For Wednesday night before the Tri-Cities breakfast, would you drive after the Pullman table or sleep around Lewiston and leave early Thursday?

I’d drive to Kennewick or Richland Wednesday night if the Pullman table ends by about 5:00. Pullman to Kennewick is roughly 2 hours 15 minutes, sometimes a bit more with stops, so you’d arrive around 7:30 or 8:00. That is a much better risk than staying in Lewiston and leaving before dawn for an 8:00 breakfast in the Tri-Cities. The key is making dinner intentional: either eat before leaving Pullman/Moscow or choose a Kennewick hotel with late food nearby.
That makes sense. I can handle one late-ish drive better than a pre-dawn one before a counselor breakfast.

Then the working hotel sequence is Monday Spokane Valley or Liberty Lake, Tuesday Lewiston or Clarkston unless Moscow prices become reasonable, and Wednesday Kennewick or Richland. The airport plan I’d price first is Spokane inbound and Pasco outbound; keep Spokane round trip as the budget backup if the rental drop fee is silly.
Can you give me a practical shortlist of zones and search filters? I’m not ready for specific hotel names yet.

Shortlist by night: Monday, east Spokane Valley or Liberty Lake, with free parking, breakfast by 6:30, and late dinner/takeout nearby after the reception. Tuesday, Lewiston/Clarkston near the river or main commercial areas; Moscow only if the price is close and cancellation is good. Prioritize an adjacent restaurant and a clear drive time to Pullman. Wednesday, Kennewick near Columbia Center, the convention/event corridor, or whichever side is closest to the breakfast; Richland also works if the breakfast is north or west. For flights, search SLC-GEG Monday after noon arriving before 5, and PSC-SLC Thursday after 11:30. For the car, compare GEG-to-PSC one-way against GEG round trip, including drop fee and return-office hours.
Good. Put the risks in plain English so I can share them with my director.

Plain-English version: Spokane round trip may save money, but it adds a long backtrack after the final breakfast and creates more chance of a rushed airport day. Spokane in and Pasco out matches the event path and makes Thursday cleaner, but only makes sense if the one-way rental fee is reasonable. For hotels, staying too far west Monday makes Tuesday morning tighter, staying in Pullman Tuesday may be overpriced because of campus demand, and staying outside the Tri-Cities Wednesday creates the biggest reliability risk for the Thursday breakfast. My practical plan is to price the open-jaw route first and use cancellable hotels in Spokane Valley, Lewiston/Clarkston, and Kennewick.

messages.content: I have updates on the Inland Northwest loop. Spokane reception is confirmed to end at 8:45 p.m., Coeur d’Alene visits now start at 7:50 a.m., and Pullman hotels are tight because of move-in. I found cancellable options in Spokane Valley, Lewiston, Pullman, and Kennewick. Can you rank the hotel sequence before I book?

With those times, I’d rank the sequence as Spokane Valley Monday, Lewiston Tuesday, and Kennewick Wednesday. Pullman would only move up if the price drops or the Lewiston option has a weak cancellation policy. Before I fully bless Kennewick for Wednesday, what time does the Pullman transfer table end, including pack-up?
The table is 1:30 to 4:30, and I should be packed by 5:00. No dinner event in Pullman.

Then Kennewick Wednesday is still the better reliability choice. If you leave Pullman around 5:00, you should reach Kennewick roughly 7:15 to 7:45 depending on stops. That is late but controlled. Staying in Lewiston Wednesday would push the hard drive to Thursday morning before an 8:00-ish breakfast, which is the less forgiving side of the schedule.
For Monday, Spokane Valley versus Liberty Lake? The reception is downtown-ish, not in the Valley.

Spokane Valley is the safer Monday pick because the reception ends at 8:45 and you’ll have more late-food options. Liberty Lake trims a little time Tuesday morning, but it adds more post-reception driving and usually fewer dinner choices late. If the first school is actually in Post Falls, Liberty Lake gets more attractive; if it is Coeur d’Alene proper, Spokane Valley is still fine as long as breakfast starts early.
The first check-in is 7:50 in Coeur d’Alene, then Post Falls after that. I care more about breakfast and coffee than shaving ten minutes.

Pick Spokane Valley, then. Look for breakfast starting no later than 6:30, free self-parking, and a late-arrival note since you may not check in until after 9:15. You can leave the hotel around 6:55 to 7:05 and still have a reasonable cushion for the Coeur d’Alene check-in.
Tuesday: the Lewiston place has breakfast at 6:00, free parking, and a restaurant next door until 9. Moscow is about $230 and breakfast starts at 7. Pullman is $279 and doesn’t list breakfast.

Lewiston wins for Tuesday. The earlier breakfast and adjacent restaurant matter more than being 15 minutes closer to Pullman, especially with no Wednesday morning appointment. I’d rather have you arrive in Lewiston in daylight after the Coeur d’Alene visits, eat without hunting around, and leave midmorning for Pullman.
Wednesday Kennewick has breakfast included, but I don’t really need it because the counselor breakfast is the event. The lobby restaurant closes at 9:30. Is that enough?

Yes, if you leave Pullman close to 5:00. A 9:30 restaurant close gives you enough room to check in and eat, but I’d still have a backup. Call the hotel to ask whether 9:30 is last seating or kitchen close, and identify one nearby takeout option open until at least 10 in case the drive runs long.
Can you list the exact verification calls so I don’t miss one?

Call Monday’s Spokane Valley hotel and verify breakfast start time, free self-parking, late arrival after 9 p.m., cancellation deadline, and approximate drive time to the Coeur d’Alene school area. Call Tuesday’s Lewiston hotel and verify breakfast at 6, restaurant hours next door, free parking, cancellation deadline, and that the room type you are booking is actually available. Call Wednesday’s Kennewick hotel and verify late arrival around 7:30 to 8:30, restaurant last seating versus closing time, parking cost, cancellation deadline, checkout time, and drive time to the counselor breakfast location.
If the Lewiston place only has a king room left, is that a problem for the route?

No route problem. If you are traveling solo and it is non-smoking, cancellable, and in the right area, the king room is fine. I would not pay Pullman move-in pricing just to avoid that. Booking order: hold Spokane Valley Monday, Lewiston Tuesday, and Kennewick Wednesday, all refundable, then finalize the flight and car once the open-jaw price is clear.

Hotels: Spokane Valley and Kennewick holds look fine. Lewiston is the refundable king room. Should I lock those three?

That keeps the driving balanced: short enough after the Spokane reception, practical after the Coeur d’Alene visits, and safest before the Tri-Cities breakfast. Confirm each one is refundable under the deadlines you noted before entering the card.
Can you give me the final booking packet with times and what goes on the reimbursement note?

Booking packet: Flight, Delta SLC to GEG Monday 1:20 p.m. to 2:45 p.m.; Delta PSC to SLC Thursday 2:10 p.m. to 3:50 p.m.; request no-fee window seats and save the airfare receipt with taxes/fees. Hotels: Monday Spokane Valley, late arrival after reception, free parking, early breakfast; Tuesday Lewiston refundable king, breakfast at 6 and restaurant next door; Wednesday Kennewick, late arrival after Pullman drive and dinner access before 9:30. Reimbursement note: Open-jaw air and one-way car were selected because required events end in the Tri-Cities Thursday morning; returning from Pasco avoids backtracking to Spokane, protects the return flight after counselor conversations, and reduces extra driving time.

The cancellation deadlines from the holds are: Monday room cancel by Aug. 17 at 6 p.m. Pacific, Tuesday by Aug. 18 at 4 p.m. Pacific, and Wednesday by Aug. 19 at 6 p.m. Pacific. Does that line up with booking today?

Yes. Book the flight and car first, then enter the hotel cards in the same sitting. Put the cancellation reminders on your calendar in Mountain Time: Aug. 17 at 7 p.m., Aug. 18 at 5 p.m., and Aug. 19 at 7 p.m., plus a morning reminder on each deadline day. Keep the hotel confirmations, airfare receipt, rental estimate with the one-way fee, and the event schedule together so the reimbursement explanation is easy.

Pasco helps dinner and checkout, but it adds morning risk before the one fixed event. Eat after Pullman on the way or bring something, then use Kennewick for the short Thursday drive.
Can you give me the simple sequence so I don't overthink it?

Wednesday: finish the table at 5:45, leave Pullman by about 6:05, fuel before leaving town if you're under half a tank, and aim for Kennewick around 8:15-8:30. Thursday: skip hotel breakfast, check out around 6:20, keep luggage in the trunk, arrive at the counselor breakfast by 7:10, then leave for Pasco with time to refuel near the airport and return the car by 12:15.
So only call Pasco hotels if Kennewick won't do late arrival?

messages.content: I'm switching from the Inland Northwest cleanup to North Texas. I have an early September loop: a Richardson counselor reception Monday evening, Plano and Frisco high-school visits Tuesday morning, a Fort Worth community-college table Wednesday afternoon, and a Denton counselor breakfast Thursday at 7:30. I need SLC flights, a rental car, and hotel zones. I can't tell whether Sunday night or Monday afternoon arrival is smarter, and whether Love Field is worth it.

I can map it. What are the exact travel dates, the Monday reception start time, Tuesday's first visit time, the Wednesday table hours, and how late Thursday you can fly home? Those are the pieces that decide whether Monday arrival is too tight.

Travel week is Sept. 8-11. Reception in Richardson is 6:30-8:00 Monday. Tuesday first Plano school is 8:00, then Frisco late morning. Fort Worth table is Wednesday 1:00-4:30. Denton breakfast is Thursday 7:30. I'd like to be back Thursday afternoon or evening, not late at night. Rental car is fine.

With those times, I'd lean DFW Sunday evening, car there, then hotels in zones rather than one base for the whole trip: Richardson/Plano for the Monday and Tuesday obligations, possibly Grapevine/DFW North or Fort Worth Tuesday, and Denton Wednesday. Monday afternoon arrival can work only if a nonstop lands by about 2:00; any delay plus rental pickup and Dallas traffic makes the 6:30 reception less comfortable.
Sunday evening is less convenient at home, but I can justify it if the Monday risk is real. How would you phrase the trade-off?

Sunday evening buys reliability: land, get the car, eat, and wake up already near Richardson. Monday afternoon saves one hotel night and keeps Sunday at home, but it stacks flight delay, rental pickup, rush-hour driving, hotel check-in, and the reception into one afternoon. For a 6:30 admissions event, I would not choose Monday unless the fare is much better and the flight arrives before 2:00.
If I did Monday, I would prefer not to leave in the morning. So maybe that answers it.

Yes. An afternoon departure from SLC landing after 3:00 puts too much pressure on the reception. Sunday evening is the cleaner plan. For the return, Thursday after the breakfast is fine; look for DFW departures around 1:00 p.m. or later so you can drive from Denton, refuel, and return the car without rushing.
Can you compare DFW and Love Field in plain English?

DFW is the practical airport for the whole loop: more nonstop choices from SLC, a stronger rental-car setup, better position for Fort Worth and Denton, and an easier Thursday return after breakfast. Love Field can be nicer for Richardson/Plano and sometimes has good Southwest timing, but it is weaker for the west and north parts of this route. I would use Love Field only if the nonstop schedule or fare is clearly better.
Include Delta if the timing is close, but I don't need to force it.

Then shortlist DFW first with nonstop options on Delta and American, plus Southwest into Love Field as a comparison. I would avoid adding a connection just for carrier preference; Dallas has enough nonstop service that a one-stop itinerary would need to be much cheaper or land much earlier to be worth the extra failure point.
What hotel areas would you use? I don't want a downtown Dallas hotel.

First zone: Richardson/Plano, ideally west Plano or Richardson near US-75 or President George Bush Turnpike, for the Monday reception and Tuesday 8:00 Plano visit. Second zone: Grapevine/DFW North if you want a central, easy-food reposition before Fort Worth; Fort Worth if you want the shortest Wednesday drive but may pay parking. Final zone: Denton for Wednesday night before the 7:30 breakfast.
Can I make it a two-hotel trip, or is that asking for annoying drives?

Two hotels is workable: stay Richardson/Plano Sunday and Monday, then move to Denton Wednesday after the Fort Worth table. The annoying piece is Tuesday night. If you stay Richardson/Plano Tuesday too, Wednesday's drive to Fort Worth is longer but mostly midday. If you add a Grapevine night Tuesday, you unpack once more but make Wednesday smoother.
So the optional piece is Tuesday night. Grapevine versus Fort Worth versus Denton?

For Tuesday night I would rank Grapevine/DFW North first, Fort Worth second, Denton third. Grapevine balances Tuesday after Frisco, Wednesday to Fort Worth, restaurants, and usually free suburban parking. Fort Worth is best if the Wednesday table setup is early or downtown parking is reimbursed. Denton is cheap, but it pulls you too far north before a Fort Worth afternoon.
What should I watch for before placing holds?

Flights: Sunday DFW arrival not too late for car pickup and dinner; Thursday DFW return no earlier than about 1:00, safer 1:30-3:30. Car: airport pickup and return location, toll policy, and fuel location. Hotels: breakfast start times, parking fees, cancellation deadlines in Mountain Time, late-arrival policy, and whether there is dinner within a short walk or easy drive after evening events.
Where would you sleep before the Denton breakfast?

Denton. A Grapevine or DFW North hotel can work, but it means leaving around 6:00 or earlier for a 7:10 arrival, and I-35E has less forgiveness than I’d want that morning. messages.content: Back from Oregon and I need to open the last fall loop: Front Range, Sunday Nov. 3 through Thursday Nov. 7. Anchors are Monday 7:50 a.m. counselor breakfast in Fort Collins, Monday night college fair in Boulder, Tuesday school visits in Westminster and Lakewood, Wednesday afternoon transfer table in Colorado Springs, and Thursday morning counselor coffee near Denver Tech Center. Can you compare flying into Denver with a rental car versus just driving from Salt Lake? I also need a sensible route order and hotel zones with early breakfast and practical dinner access before I put refundable holds on rooms.

Absolutely. I’d treat this as a reliability question more than a pure cost question. Two quick checks before I rank it: if you fly Sunday, can you leave SLC after lunch or early afternoon, and is the rental car reimbursable if it saves a weather drive? Also, do you need to be home Thursday for anything that would make a later afternoon return a problem?

I can leave after lunch Sunday. Rental car is reimbursable as long as I keep the itemized receipt and note why I didn’t drive. I don’t need to be home Thursday until dinner-ish. My hesitation on driving is early snow on I-80 and being wrecked before that 7:50 breakfast.

Then the cleaner plan is fly plus rental unless the fares are unreasonable. Flight plus rental gives you a short Sunday travel day, enough daylight to get from DEN to Fort Collins, and far less exposure to I-80 weather; the downsides are rental cost, airport pickup time, parking, and possible tolls. Driving avoids airfare and uses your own car, but it puts 8-plus hours on both ends of the trip and makes Monday morning fragile. Because the first commitment is early in Fort Collins, I would not make the Sunday drive unless the forecast is dry and you can leave Salt Lake very early.
If flying, should Sunday night be Fort Collins itself or Loveland? The breakfast is near CSU.

Fort Collins. Loveland is fine on price, but it adds 25 to 35 minutes on the morning you most need predictability. I’d look near CSU or Old Town if rates are reasonable, or Fort Collins south/Harmony if you want easier I-25 access and chain hotels. For the hold, verify breakfast starts by 6:30 or plan a coffee-and-grab backup. Dinner is easier around Old Town or Harmony than by the interstate after 9.
Map the route order assuming I land at DEN Sunday afternoon.

Route shape: Sunday land DEN, pick up the car, and drive straight to Fort Collins before dark. Monday do the 7:50 breakfast, use mid-day for follow-ups or a school stop, drive to Boulder for the evening fair, and sleep somewhere between Boulder and Tuesday’s first school. Tuesday do Westminster and Lakewood, then decide whether to push south that evening. Wednesday be in Colorado Springs for the afternoon transfer table. Wednesday night should probably be DTC or nearby, not Colorado Springs, because Thursday morning is at DTC and you’ll want a simple airport return after.
The Monday night piece is the one I can’t see clearly. Boulder rooms look high. What about Broomfield, Westminster, or Denver West?

My ranking right now: first, Broomfield/Interlocken or Superior, because it is the easiest after the Boulder fair, has lots of dinner options around FlatIron Crossing, and is still workable for Westminster or Lakewood. Second, Westminster, which is good if the Westminster school is first and parking is usually easier, but food can be more scattered depending on the hotel. Third, Denver West or Golden, which is best only if Lakewood is the first Tuesday visit; it makes the late post-fair drive longer. Boulder is worth it only if the fair ends very late or weather is bad.
For Tuesday night, I don’t want to be penny-wise and dumb. Wednesday table is afternoon, not morning, and Thursday coffee is DTC at 8:30.

With an afternoon Colorado Springs table, you have flexibility. If Tuesday visits end by mid-afternoon and the roads are dry, sleeping in Colorado Springs Tuesday is comfortable: you arrive, eat, and have a calm Wednesday morning. If Tuesday runs late or Monument Hill looks icy, sleep north of it, either Castle Rock, DTC, or Denver south, and drive down Wednesday late morning. Wednesday night I’d sleep DTC regardless, because driving up from Colorado Springs before an 8:30 coffee is the fragile move.
Can you give me the hotel zones to hold? I’m not booking tonight, just refundable holds.

Hold one per zone: Sunday Fort Collins near CSU/Old Town if price is okay, otherwise Harmony Road/I-25; Monday Broomfield/Interlocken as first choice, Westminster as backup, and Denver West only if Tuesday starts in Lakewood; Tuesday Colorado Springs north or central if you can arrive before dinner, with Castle Rock or DTC as the weather backup; Wednesday DTC/Greenwood Village near I-25 or Belleview. For each hold, check breakfast start time, free versus paid parking, itemized folio availability, and whether there is a restaurant within a 10-minute walk or a reliable late pickup option.
The fair in Boulder is scheduled to end at 8:15 right now. If I stay Broomfield, am I okay for dinner after?

Yes, Broomfield/Interlocken is one of the safer meal choices after that. FlatIron Crossing and the US-36 corridor have more options than a random Westminster business park, though some kitchens will be closing by 9:30. I’d still eat something before the fair if possible, then use Broomfield for a lighter late dinner or pickup. If you hold Denver West, late dinner gets thinner unless you go out of your way.
What about rental car class and parking? I don’t want a giant SUV if I don’t need one.

Book a compact or midsize SUV only if the price difference is modest; otherwise a standard sedan is fine for normal Front Range roads. AWD is not guaranteed unless the rental class says so, so don’t overpay thinking it solves everything. For reimbursement, keep the rental agreement, final receipt, fuel receipt, hotel parking lines, and any toll charges. Also check whether the hotel lots are surface and free; downtown Boulder and Fort Collins parking are where surprises are more likely.
Thursday return: the DTC coffee should end about 10:15. Is a midday flight okay, or should I go later afternoon?

A true midday flight is too tight if you are returning a rental at DEN. From DTC to the airport can be 35 to 60 minutes, then fuel, rental return, shuttle or walk, security, and weather slack. I’d target a nonstop departing roughly 2:30 to 4:30 p.m. Anything around noon would require leaving the coffee early. After 5 p.m. is safe but wastes the afternoon unless the fare is much better.
Good. Look for Sunday afternoon outbound and Thursday midafternoon nonstop. If seat maps are open, I’d like a window again, but that can wait.

Plan for holds tonight: fly SLC-DEN Sunday afternoon and rent at DEN; sleep Fort Collins Sunday, Broomfield/Interlocken Monday with Westminster as backup, Colorado Springs Tuesday only if the weather and Tuesday end time cooperate, and DTC Wednesday. Driving from Salt Lake stays a backup only if the forecast clears and fares jump. Before placing holds, verify 6:00 to 6:30 breakfast starts for the early mornings, parking charges, cancellation cutoff, late-food options, and itemized folios. For flights, shortlist nonstop Sunday after lunch and Thursday 2:30 to 4:30 p.m.; request window seats wherever the seat map lets you.

Can you put it in a verification list so I can call three properties quickly?

Call list: Fort Collins Sunday: breakfast by 6:30, Sunday dinner nearby after arrival, free parking, itemized folio, and cancellation cutoff for Nov. 3. Broomfield Monday: breakfast must start at 6:00 or have reliable grab-and-go, parking/free lot, late food after 9 p.m., itemized folio, and whether cancellation is due Nov. 3 or Nov. 4. messages.content: I’m mostly through the Front Range bookings. Can we start the early-December admissions conference in the Phoenix area? It’s Sunday Dec. 8 evening welcome through Tuesday afternoon, and there’s an optional Wednesday committee breakfast I may get assigned to. The official hotel is closest but has no breakfast and adds a daily fee. I need a practical comparison before I hold anything.

Yes. Two decisions will drive the rest: whether to arrive Saturday evening or Sunday midday, and whether to keep Wednesday open until the committee breakfast is confirmed. What part of Phoenix is the meeting in, and what are the official block rate and nearby hotel rates you’re seeing?

It’s in Tempe near Mill Ave. Official block is $219 a night plus a $24 daily destination fee, no breakfast. Hyatt Place is $178 and says breakfast included, about 0.8 miles away. Hampton is $169 with breakfast, more like 1.3 miles. SpringHill is $184 with breakfast but closer to 2 miles. Reception is 6:30 Sunday, Tuesday sessions end at 3:00, and the maybe-Wednesday breakfast would be 7:30 to 9:00.

First cut: the official block is the least stressful for walking and meeting access, but the fee and breakfast gap make it expensive. Hyatt Place looks like the strongest practical hold if its breakfast and cancellation terms check out: close enough for daylight walking, easy rideshare after evening events, and still likely cheaper than the official hotel. Hampton saves a little more but adds morning and evening friction. SpringHill only makes sense if it has a useful shuttle or a much better cancellation policy.
The destination fee is what worries me. Our reimbursement policy gets picky about resort or destination fees unless there really isn’t another workable option.

Then I would not make the official block your only safety net. For three nights, the official room is $657 plus $72 in fees before tax. Hyatt is $534 before tax; even a few short rideshares likely keep it comparable or cheaper, and breakfast is simpler. If the official block can be held with no penalty, it’s a backup. Otherwise, I’d focus on a refundable Hyatt hold.
That matches my instincts. For flights, I could arrive Saturday after dinner or Sunday midday. I’d rather not burn an extra night unless Sunday makes the reception risky.

With SLC to PHX nonstops, Sunday can work if you land by early afternoon. Saturday evening buys operational cushion and a calm Sunday morning, but it adds a hotel night and dinner logistics. Sunday midday is fine for a 6:30 reception if the flight arrives by about 1:30, but it becomes risky if the agenda adds any Sunday prep before late afternoon.
No Sunday prep on the draft agenda. Just registration by 5:30 and the reception at 6:30. Can you outline realistic flight windows, not exact booking yet?

I’d check these windows: Saturday Dec. 7 nonstop departing SLC around 6:00 to 7:30 p.m. if you want maximum cushion; Sunday Dec. 8 nonstop departing late morning and landing around 12:15 to 1:30 as the best balance; avoid Sunday arrivals after 3:00. For the return, if Wednesday breakfast becomes required, look for a Wednesday Dec. 11 nonstop around 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. If the breakfast is dropped, Tuesday evening could work after the dean’s dinner only if that dinner ends early enough.
I need to stay through Tuesday night either way; there’s a dean’s dinner Tuesday. Wednesday afternoon sounds safer. Is a rental car overkill?

For a Tempe-only conference, yes, a rental is probably overkill. PHX to Tempe is usually a short rideshare, and hotel parking plus conference traffic would eat into any savings. I’d plan rideshare airport-hotel-airport, then walk in daylight or use short rideshares for evening events.
I don’t mind a walk in daylight, but I don’t want a long walk alone after the reception.

That points back to Hyatt over Hampton. It is close enough for a daylight walk if the route feels comfortable, and short enough that an evening rideshare is not a big budget item. Ask whether the hotel shuttle covers the conference center or only the airport/local radius. If there is no shuttle, it’s still workable; just save rideshare receipts.
What do I need to document for reimbursement if I don’t use the official block?

messages.content: Phoenix is wrapped, and now I need a very different trip: Boise for Lena’s club volleyball weekend, Jan. 24 to 26. Schedule isn’t posted. Team says games could start anywhere between 8 and 10 Saturday. One room with two queens. The team block is near the venue, but they only have a few 2Q rooms and breakfast is not included.

Then the zones stack up like this: Nampa/team hotel is best for the morning drive and team coordination, but weaker for breakfast and late-arrival food; Meridian adds about 18 to 25 minutes to the venue, but has easier Friday dinner, likely included breakfast, and is better for Sunday relatives; downtown Boise has the most food, but adds the most Saturday morning drive and usually more parking hassle. From central Meridian to Nampa, I’d plan to leave the hotel around 6:40, earlier if roads are slick. If breakfast starts at 6:00, it works; if breakfast starts at 6:30, you’ll want a grab-and-go backup.
The road piece is what worries me. We probably can’t leave SLC until 3:45 or 4 on Friday. Is driving still sensible, or should I have a flight backup?

Driving is sensible if the forecast is normal winter, but 4:00 is the latest I’d call comfortable. SLC to Meridian is usually about five and a half hours before weather, gas, and dinner. A realistic arrival is 10:00 to 11:00 p.m.; blowing snow near Twin Falls can push that later. Ask Meridian: exact cancellation deadline, whether late check-in after 11 is protected, breakfast start time Saturday and Sunday, whether they can do breakfast bags if you leave before it opens, any parking fee, and whether the two-queen room is guaranteed rather than just requested. Ask the team hotel the same, plus whether the block rate has a shorter cancellation window or first-night deposit.

Only if Saturday starts very early or Lena really needs to be with the team group. Otherwise the Meridian trade-off is cleaner: easier Friday dinner, breakfast handled, free parking, Sunday relatives nearby, and better cancellation flexibility. The five-minute hotel saves stress Saturday morning but gives some of it back Friday night and at breakfast.

Yes, if both are fully cancellable and neither has a deposit. Put calendar holds for both cancellation deadlines. If one has a 48-hour deadline and the other releases earlier, use the tighter one as the decision date. I would not hold a nonrefundable team room while the tournament schedule is still unknown.
Okay, make me a practical action plan for today.

Today: place a cancellable hold on the Meridian two-queen room if it guarantees the bed setup, breakfast, and free parking; call the team hotel and ask whether any two-queen block rooms are cancellable until at least midweek before arrival; do not book flights now; set a weather check for Wednesday night and Friday morning; and plan a packed dinner or snack option so you can keep moving if I-84 is slow. Wednesday: breakfast at 6:30; checkout/load car by 8:45; leave Bellevue at 9:00, or 8:30 if traffic is red; reach Lynnwood about 9:50-10:05; fuel and keep receipt; park once and keep luggage hidden, with laptop/purse carried in. messages.content: Now that Puget Sound is squared away, I need to start the late-March Central Texas loop. Tentative dates are Sun Mar 23 through Wed Mar 26 out of Salt Lake. Monday at 5:30 p.m. I have an admitted-student reception in Austin, Tuesday at 10:00 a.m. a transfer fair in San Marcos, Tuesday evening an alumni dinner in San Antonio, and Wednesday at 9:00 a.m. a counselor coffee north of Austin. I need help deciding Sunday afternoon versus Monday morning arrival, rental car versus rideshare, and the hotel order.

Yes. A few details affect risk here: do you know when setup begins for the Austin reception, when exhibitors need to be at the San Marcos fair, and whether the San Antonio dinner is downtown or north side? Also, are you willing to change hotels twice if it makes the early starts smoother?

Setup is not final but I would assume around 4:30. San Marcos has not sent exhibitor instructions, so maybe 9:15 arrival for a 10 start. San Antonio venue is not final; could be downtown or Pearl-ish. Wednesday coffee is likely Round Rock or Cedar Park. I can move once without grumbling. Twice is okay if it really reduces risk. Breakfast and not-crazy parking would help.

The basic route works as AUS airport, Austin reception, San Marcos, San Antonio, north Austin, then back to AUS. My first pass: arrive Sunday if the budget allows, rent a car for the whole loop, and avoid downtown Austin unless the rate and parking are reasonable. Monday morning arrival can work on paper, but it puts flight delay, rental-car pickup, Austin traffic, and reception setup all in the same narrow window.
Can you compare the flight windows? If Delta has a clean option, include it, but I do not need it if the timing is worse.

Shortlist: 1) Sunday nonstop SLC-AUS around 1:20-5:05 on Delta: higher fare, best reliability, enough time for rental pickup and dinner. 2) Sunday one-stop via Denver or DFW around midday to early evening: cheaper, still okay, but one delay can make Sunday dinner/check-in late. 3) Monday early one-stop arriving around 12:20-12:45: cheapest, but I would not pair that with a 4:30-ish setup. 4) Monday nonstop arriving around 12:30: better than the one-stop, still tight once you add rental counter, traffic, and parking. For the return, a Wednesday midafternoon AUS-SLC is the cleanest after the 9:00 coffee.
I was hoping not to lose Sunday evening at home. Is the Monday nonstop too tight if I ship materials to the Austin venue?

Shipping materials helps, but it does not solve the main timing risk. If the plane lands at 12:30, you are realistically in the rental car around 1:15 or 1:30, then you still need lunch, hotel or venue stop, and Austin traffic. You may have only 60 to 90 minutes of true cushion before setup. I would take Monday only if the final setup is later than 4:45 and you are comfortable going straight from the airport to the venue.
Okay, assume Sunday arrival. What about full rental car versus rideshares? I am not wild about driving I-35, but I also do not want to be stranded between events.

Full-trip rental is the practical choice. AUS-to-Austin rideshare is easy, but Austin to San Marcos, San Marcos to San Antonio, and then San Antonio back toward north Austin get expensive and less predictable, especially with materials and luggage. A hybrid rental for only Tuesday/Wednesday usually saves little once you add pickup time. I would book a midsize from AUS, keep the luggage covered, and use rideshare only for a local dinner if parking is annoying.
Hotel areas are what I cannot visualize.

Think of it this way. Option A: Austin or Austin airport/east side Sunday and Monday, then north San Antonio Tuesday. Easiest Monday, good dinner access, but Tuesday morning to San Marcos needs an early start. Option B: San Marcos Sunday and Monday, then north San Antonio Tuesday. Cheapest and easiest Tuesday morning, but you drive up to Austin Monday afternoon and back after the reception. Option C: Austin Sunday, San Marcos Monday, north San Antonio Tuesday. Safest event-by-event, but it is three hotels. Option D: stay north Austin Tuesday after the San Antonio dinner. I would avoid that unless the dinner ends very early.
Give me hotel area shortlist, not properties yet. Where should I search tonight?

Search in this order: 1) Austin airport/east Austin for Sunday, or Sunday/Monday if you decide not to move after the reception. Look for breakfast, parking under about $20, and dinner within a short drive. 2) San Marcos along I-35 near the university or outlet area for Monday night, with breakfast starting by 6:30 and free parking. 3) San Antonio north side or Pearl/downtown as a placeholder until the dinner venue lands; if venue is unknown, choose cancellable and do not prepay. 4) Round Rock/Cedar Park only as a Wednesday-morning helper, not as a Tuesday night base after San Antonio.
If I do Austin Sunday and Monday, what time would I need to leave for San Marcos Tuesday?

For a 10:00 fair with a 9:15 exhibitor arrival, leave Austin by about 7:45. If they ask exhibitors to be there at 8:45, leave closer to 7:15. That makes an Austin Monday night possible, but breakfast needs to be early and parking/load-out should be simple. If you stay in San Marcos Monday, Tuesday morning becomes much easier.
Could I stay San Marcos both Sunday and Monday to save cost and just drive into Austin Monday afternoon?

Yes, that is a reasonable budget version. Leave San Marcos by about 2:35 for a 4:30 setup, earlier if the venue is downtown or parking is unclear. Pros: fewer hotel moves, likely free parking, easier Tuesday morning, and lower rates. Cons: Monday reception night ends with a drive back to San Marcos, and a bad I-35 incident would be annoying. I would not choose it if setup moves earlier than 4:15.
Let's wait for the final setup times before deciding. What should I hold as the safest placeholder?

Hold cancellable rooms in the safe sequence: Sunday Austin airport/east side, Monday San Marcos, Tuesday north San Antonio. Also keep a San Marcos Sunday/Monday backup if the savings are large and cancellation is easy. For flights, keep watching the Sunday afternoon nonstop and the Wednesday midafternoon return. For the car, price a single AUS round-trip rental from Sunday evening to Wednesday early afternoon. The next decision point is the Austin setup time plus the exact San Antonio dinner neighborhood.

messages.content: Update on Central Texas. Austin reception setup starts at 4:15 p.m. Monday. San Marcos wants exhibitors on site by 8:45 Tuesday. The San Antonio alumni dinner is north side, not downtown. Also, the convenient Austin hotels are ugly because of a tech event, like $330 to $380 plus high parking. San Marcos still has a cancellable breakfast/free parking option around $149, and north San Antonio has a couple around $160 to $175. Can you rank the hotel areas now?

That changes the ranking. Best balance is now: 1) Austin airport/east side Sunday, San Marcos Monday, north San Antonio Tuesday. 2) San Marcos Sunday and Monday, north San Antonio Tuesday. 3) Austin Sunday and Monday, north San Antonio Tuesday. 4) Anything that puts you north of Austin Tuesday night after the San Antonio dinner. The expensive Austin two-night plan no longer buys enough convenience to justify the cost.
Why is Sunday Austin plus Monday San Marcos better than just San Marcos both nights?

Sunday Austin keeps Monday calm: you are already near the reception city, can check the venue route, eat normally, and avoid a long Monday afternoon drive before setup. Monday San Marcos then protects the 8:45 exhibitor arrival Tuesday. San Marcos both nights is cheaper and has one less move, but Monday becomes the day with the main traffic risk.
Give me the drive times I should be using.

Use these planning numbers: Austin airport/east side to central Austin reception, 20 to 40 minutes depending on venue and parking. Austin to San Marcos after the reception, 40 to 60 minutes. San Marcos hotel to fair, 5 to 15 minutes if you book along I-35 or near campus. San Marcos to north San Antonio, 55 to 75 minutes. North San Antonio to Round Rock or Cedar Park Wednesday morning, 95 to 120 minutes, so that is the early alarm.
The Wednesday early alarm is the part I dislike. Would staying in San Marcos Tuesday after the dinner be smarter?

Only if the dinner ends early and you feel fine driving afterward. North San Antonio to San Marcos after dinner is usually 50 to 65 minutes, and it shortens Wednesday a lot. But if dinner wraps at 8:30 or later, I would rather sleep near the dinner and leave early Wednesday than do a tired late drive on I-35.
Dinner will probably end around 8:45. So north San Antonio Tuesday sounds better.

Agreed. Book Tuesday on the north side. Pick the option with breakfast at 6:00 if possible, free parking, and easy highway access. You may only have time for coffee or something portable before leaving for the 9:00 counselor coffee, but that is still better than a late-night relocation.
For Monday night, is the San Marcos hotel with breakfast and free parking the clear hold?

Yes. Monday San Marcos is the clearest hold because the 8:45 exhibitor arrival is fixed. Check that breakfast starts by 6:30, parking is actually free, and cancellation is not before you expect the final fair packet. Also confirm the room is not prepaid; this is exactly the sort of stay you want to be able to adjust.
And Sunday? Airport/east Austin instead of downtown?

Yes, airport or east Austin for Sunday. Downtown restaurants are nice, but with tech-event rates and high parking, they are not worth it for one night before a Monday reception. Look for a cancellable breakfast rate, parking under about $20, and either an on-site restaurant or several nearby dinner options so Sunday arrival is easy.
Okay, tell me exactly what to hold tonight.

Hold three cancellable rooms: Sunday in Austin airport/east side; Monday in San Marcos near I-35 or campus with breakfast by 6:30 and free parking; Tuesday in north San Antonio/Stone Oak or La Cantera area with breakfast at 6:00 if available and free parking. Backup hold: San Marcos for Sunday/Monday only if the rate is much better and cancellation is easy. Release the expensive Austin two-night options unless a host specifically needs you near the reception venue Monday morning.

Wednesday leave north San Antonio around 6:25, attend the 9:00 coffee, leave by 10:30 if possible, fuel near AUS, and keep every receipt.

What do I do with luggage and fuel on Wednesday? I don’t want to be juggling the bag at the coffee.

Checkout before the coffee and leave the main carry-on locked in the trunk; take only a small tote or laptop bag inside. Park where the car is visible if the school lot allows it. Take the direct airport route, top off gas at an airport-area station, return the rental by noon, and keep the hotel cancellation, fuel, toll, parking, and rental receipts together.

messages.content: Texas is behind me. I need to start the Twin Cities yield trip for mid-April: Monday evening admitted-student reception in St. Paul, Tuesday 11:00 transfer fair in Bloomington, and Wednesday morning counselor breakfast in Minneapolis. Can you help me decide Sunday vs Monday arrival, car vs rideshares, and hotel zone before I place holds?
Yes. Two details will change the recommendation: where in St. Paul is the reception, and are you carrying materials yourself or shipping them ahead?

Reception is near Cathedral Hill, fair is by the Bloomington hotel/convention area, and the breakfast is near the North Loop in Minneapolis. I’m shipping two small boxes to the Monday venue and traveling with a carry-on. Budget target is under about $180 a night if possible.

For arrival, Sunday afternoon is the safer hold. A Monday morning nonstop can work on paper, but if the flight slides, baggage takes time, or ground transport is slow, you lose the recovery window before the reception. I would only use Monday morning if the savings are meaningful and you are comfortable going straight into event mode. A Monday afternoon arrival is too tight.
I can justify Sunday if the hotel cost doesn’t get silly. What zones would you compare?

Shortlist by zone: St. Paul near Cathedral Hill: easiest Monday night, good nearby dinner choices, but breakfast may be paid or unclear and parking often adds cost. Bloomington/MOA-I-494 area: usually stronger breakfast and free parking, easiest Tuesday, simple airport access, but you drive to St. Paul Monday. Minneapolis/North Loop: best for Wednesday and meals, but rates and parking are likely higher and it adds more Tuesday driving.
My instinct is Bloomington because of breakfast and parking. Is the Monday night drive to St. Paul annoying enough to avoid it?

Not enough to make me reject Bloomington. If the reception is at 6:00, leave Bloomington around 4:45 to allow traffic and parking. After the event, the return drive should be easier, likely 25-35 minutes. Tuesday becomes very easy, and Wednesday to North Loop is manageable if you leave early. St. Paul would save Monday hassle but costs you breakfast certainty and parking simplicity.
What about skipping the rental and using rideshares?

Rideshares are feasible from a St. Paul base, but they are less clean from Bloomington because you would need airport transfers plus Monday St. Paul, Tuesday fair, and Wednesday breakfast. Estimate roughly $160-$220 total depending on surge. A compact or midsize rental may be similar once you add fuel, but Bloomington hotels often offset that with free parking. Since you have three suburban/urban stops, I’d take the car if you choose Bloomington.
If I arrive Sunday, do I need the car immediately or could I rideshare to the hotel and pick one up Monday?

If you stay Bloomington, pick up the car at MSP Sunday. It saves a second airport trip and gives you flexibility for dinner, supplies, and Monday timing. If you stay St. Paul, a Sunday rideshare plus a Monday or Tuesday car pickup could work, but it adds logistics and does not help much once Tuesday and Wednesday are in different places.
Give me the tentative package and the reimbursement catches before I start holds.

Tentative package: arrive Sunday afternoon on a nonstop into MSP; return Wednesday after the counselor breakfast, ideally early to midafternoon; rent a car at MSP Sunday evening through Wednesday late morning; hold a cancellable Bloomington hotel with included breakfast and free parking; hold one St. Paul backup only if its cancellation is easy. Reimbursement checks: confirm Sunday night is covered, keep rental plus fuel and parking receipts, note any hotel parking charges, and verify whether breakfast is included or needs to be expensed. Also check each hotel cancellation deadline before placing holds.

The St. Paul code is tempting for Monday night, but once you add paid breakfast and likely parking, Bloomington is still the cleaner three-night base.
Can you show the trade-off plainly?

Plain version: St. Paul code: best Monday evening, walkable dinner after the reception, but no breakfast, likely paid parking, Tuesday drive to Bloomington, and Wednesday drive to Plymouth. Bloomington: best Tuesday, breakfast included, free parking, easy airport access, Monday drive to St. Paul, and Wednesday drive to Plymouth. Would one night in St. Paul and then moving to Bloomington be smarter?

Only if you expect the reception to run late or you need to stay for dinner with hosts afterward. Otherwise, changing hotels adds checkout, luggage, and another check-in for a small gain. One Bloomington base is less fussy: arrive Sunday, unpack once, drive to St. Paul Monday, stay close to Tuesday’s fair, then drive to Plymouth Wednesday.
What rental timing should I use?

Pick up at MSP after the Sunday afternoon arrival and keep it through Wednesday late morning. For Wednesday, leave Plymouth by 9:45-10:00, allow 35-45 minutes to MSP, add 10 minutes to fuel, and target rental return by 11:15-11:30. Anything left before I book?

Book or hold in this order: Sunday afternoon SLC-MSP nonstop, Wednesday return after 1:15, MSP rental car Sunday evening to Wednesday late morning, then the Bloomington cancellable room. Before confirming the hotel, verify breakfast start time, parking included, cancellation deadline, and whether the rate is refundable. Let the St. Paul code sit only as a backup until its deadline. Keep airfare, hotel, rental, gas, parking, tolls, and meal receipts together for reimbursement.

messages.content: Small wrinkle two days out: Plymouth now wants visitor badge pickup by 7:35, and Delta nudged my Wednesday return to 1:55. Flights, Bloomington hotel, and rental car are booked. Do I need to move Tuesday night closer to Plymouth?

I would not move unless you find a no-penalty Plymouth hotel that is clearly better. The timing gain is probably 20 to 25 minutes, and switching adds repacking and cancellation risk. Keep Bloomington, but tighten the morning: checkout 6:20, grab anything portable when breakfast opens, leave by 6:45, and aim to reach Plymouth around 7:30.
Breakfast opens 6:30 exactly, so I can’t sit down. Is there a backup near the school?

Use the hotel only for coffee, fruit, or a wrapped item. Put a protein bar or granola bar in your bag the night before. If you need real food, do it after the counselor breakfast, not before. A Plymouth coffee stop works only if they release you early.
Luggage still in the trunk? I do not want it in the meeting room.

Yes. Check out before leaving Bloomington, put the suitcase in the trunk, and take only your laptop or small tote inside. Keep boxes and luggage out of sight, and use visitor parking close to the school entrance if they offer it.
What is the latest I can leave Plymouth and not sweat the 1:55 flight?

Comfortable is 10:15. Planned latest is 10:30. If you are still there at 10:45, go straight toward the airport area, fuel at the closest practical station, and return the car by noon. Better target is rental return between 11:40 and 11:50.
And if the host wants me to stay for a quick counselor intro after?

Do it only if you are back to the car by 10:30. A five-minute hallway intro is fine; a sit-down follow-up is not. Offer to schedule a call from the airport instead. Keep rental, fuel, parking, and meal receipts together, and leave the hotel key at checkout so there is no reason to backtrack.

messages.content: Home for a minute and now Boise. Sofia’s volleyball tournament is May 17-19 at the Meridian sports complex. Three of us can drive after school Friday, so arrival could be late. Should we stay by the courts or downtown Boise?

If Saturday starts early, stay near Meridian. Downtown gives better dinner choices, but it adds a morning drive and usually paid parking. A practical shortlist would be: Hampton or similar near the sports complex for early breakfast and free parking; Hyatt Place Meridian for more room but often a sofa-bed setup; or downtown only if the first match is late and dinner matters more than Saturday morning ease. What time is first check-in?
First ref assignment says 7:30 Saturday. Sunday could be done by noon or go to finals around 3. I’d like to keep the room under $220.

Then I’d treat Meridian as the base. Downtown is not worth a 20-ish minute drive before a 7:30 assignment. Look for two nights with free parking, breakfast starting by 6 or 6:30, and a front desk that will note late arrival. Under $220 should be realistic near Meridian unless there is another event in town.
It’s me, Miguel, and Sofia. Sofia needs her own bed. Two queens sounds easier than a sleeper sofa after a late drive.

Agreed. For three people arriving late, two queens is simpler than opening a sofa bed at 11 p.m. I’d rank a two-queen room above a king-plus-sofa unless the sofa option is much cheaper or has a separate living area you really want.
We may not roll in until 11:15 or 11:30. Do I need to worry about the room being given away?

Not if you handle it deliberately. Book with a credit-card guarantee, add a late-arrival note, use mobile check-in if the hotel offers it, and call Friday afternoon to confirm you are still coming. If you are delayed past 10, call again from the road and ask them not to mark it no-show.
Downtown dinner is tempting for Saturday, though.

You can still do downtown dinner Saturday after play. Staying downtown means doing that same drive before the 7:30 assignment and paying more for parking. For Friday, I would eat on the road in Twin Falls or Burley and keep Boise arrival as check-in plus sleep, not a dinner plan.

Here are the actual options I’m seeing: Hampton Meridian two queens $181, breakfast 6-10, free parking, indoor pool, cancel by Wednesday 6 p.m. Hyatt Place is $199 but king plus sofa. Downtown is $209 plus $18 parking and no breakfast.

Book Hampton. It has the right bed setup, earliest breakfast, free parking, and the clearest cancellation terms. Hyatt costs more and gives Sofia a sofa bed; downtown costs more once parking and breakfast are included and makes Saturday morning harder.
Should I request late checkout Sunday?

Ask for noon at no charge, but I would not pay for it in advance. Pack the car before the first Sunday match. If they are eliminated early and noon is approved, you can go back for a quick cleanup. If they make finals, the room probably will not help enough to justify a fee.
Can you give me the drive-home plan too?

Book Hampton Meridian for Friday and Saturday, two queens, late-arrival note, cancellation reminder for Wednesday 6 p.m., and ask for free noon checkout. Friday: leave after school, eat dinner on the road around Burley or Twin Falls, call the hotel if arrival slips past 10. Saturday: use hotel breakfast before the 7:30 assignment and drive downtown for dinner only if everyone has energy. Sunday: pack the car before matches, fuel in Meridian before leaving, and head home whenever play ends. If done by noon, lunch and on the road by 1:30 is comfortable; if finals run to 3, try to leave by 4 so you are not getting back to Salt Lake too painfully late.

messages.content: The Boise tournament schedule is finally out. First match is 7:30 Saturday in Meridian, and if they make the final Sunday it could be midafternoon. The Hampton hold expires tonight. Do I keep that or switch to the Boise Bench hotel with better dinner options?

Keep the Meridian Hampton. The clean plan is to eat before you get to Boise, then arrive late and go straight to bed.

Call the front desk after booking and ask: Does breakfast open at 6 a.m. on Saturdays, and can we grab something right at opening? If they hedge, plan on hotel coffee plus road snacks and a later meal after the first match. Parking is listed as free, so you should not need downtown-style parking receipts for the stay.
If Sunday finals go until 3, can we keep the room or is that unrealistic?

Do not count on keeping the room until midafternoon. Ask for free noon checkout, maybe 1 p.m. if they can do it, but pack the car before the first Sunday match. Use the lobby restroom after checkout if needed, keep uniforms/snacks accessible in the car, and leave from the courts once play ends.
Great. Give me the final booking note I can paste into my file.

Book Hampton Meridian for Friday and Saturday, cancellable two-queen room, no prepay if avoidable. Add late-arrival note for Friday around 10:45 to 11:15 p.m. Confirm breakfast really starts at 6 a.m. Saturday, parking is free, and request noon checkout for Sunday. Eat dinner on the road Friday because nearby late options are limited. Sunday: pack car before matches, check out by noon unless the hotel grants later, use lobby restroom if finals run long, fuel in Meridian, and drive home after elimination or the final.
