messages.content: I’m starting the Denver admissions conference planning now. It is Monday June 24 through Wednesday June 26 near the convention center. Monday has an afternoon committee meeting, Tuesday is full sessions, and Wednesday has a closing lunch. Can you compare Sunday versus Monday arrival and the hotel block versus nearby options? I’d also like to know if I can skip a rental car.

Yes. Two details affect the recommendation: what time does the Monday committee meeting start, and is there a hotel reimbursement cap before taxes? Also, are you checking a bag or just doing carry-on?
Committee meeting is at 2 p.m., but they may open the room around noon for badge pickup and informal table work. Hotel cap is $235 before taxes. Carry-on only.

Then Sunday is the safer arrival. For SLC to Denver, there are plenty of nonstops. A Sunday afternoon option around 1:45 to 3:18 gives you time to reach downtown, check in, and get dinner. A Monday morning arrival before 10 looks cheaper, but a modest delay would squeeze badge pickup, lunch, and the 2 p.m. meeting. No layover is needed on this route.
How tight is Monday really if I land before 10?

It works only if everything behaves. Land around 9:55, take the train or rideshare, reach downtown around 11:00 to 11:30, drop your bag, then badge pickup. A 45-minute flight delay or slow train connection turns it into a rushed arrival with no real lunch buffer. If the noon room opening matters, arrive Sunday.
Let’s price it assuming Sunday night, then. The venue is by the convention center.

Shortlist: official conference block at the closest hotel, about $221 before taxes, no included breakfast, expensive parking but irrelevant if you skip a car, best for stepping back between sessions. Hampton downtown/convention center area, about $205 to $218, breakfast included, roughly a 7 to 9 minute walk, good practical choice. Element or Hyatt Place downtown edge, around $189 to $205, breakfast likely included depending on rate, but more like a 12 to 16 minute walk or quick ride. All should stay under the room cap before taxes if the quoted rates hold.
I really do not want a rental car downtown. Is the airport train reasonable on a Sunday afternoon?

Yes, I’d skip the rental car. The A Line from DEN to Union Station is predictable and much cheaper than parking. From Union Station you can take a short rideshare to the hotel, or light rail/free downtown shuttle if the timing is easy. If you are tired, a rideshare all the way from the airport is simpler but usually much more expensive.
What do meals look like if I use the official hotel and there is no breakfast?

For the block hotel, assume paid coffee/breakfast unless the conference agenda lists morning food. Build in two quick breakfasts: one grab-and-go nearby or lobby café on Tuesday, and one before Wednesday sessions. For dinner, downtown is easy enough without a car: convention center, theater district, and Larimer area all have options within a short walk or rideshare. Sunday dinner is the only meal you need to plan intentionally after travel.
I can live without included breakfast if the block saves me from walking back and forth in dress shoes. I just do not want accounting to push back.

The block rate under $235 before taxes is the cleanest reimbursement story. Since you will not have parking, the only extras to watch are breakfast and any destination or facility fee. If meals are reimbursed separately or covered by per diem, the lack of breakfast matters less. I would keep the block hotel as first choice and the Hampton as the practical backup.
Can I hold both for a day or two while I confirm the agenda food?

You can if both are refundable and you calendar the cancellation dates, but I would not let duplicate holds sit long. If the conference block requires a card guarantee and has an earlier cutoff, hold that first. Then hold Hampton only if it has no prepay and a flexible cancellation. Put a reminder 48 hours before the earliest deadline to release one.
Okay. First choice is the official block, backup Hampton. Arrival Sunday. What outbound flight time would you hold?

Hold the Sunday nonstop around 1:45 p.m. from Salt Lake, arriving Denver around 3:18. It gives more buffer than a later afternoon flight and still does not eat the whole day. If that fare jumps, a midafternoon Southwest or United nonstop is fine, but avoid arriving so late that dinner and check-in become the whole evening. Select a window seat if the fare allows seat choice; if it is Southwest, set a check-in reminder.
Return Wednesday after the closing lunch, but not too late if I can avoid it.

I’d avoid anything around 3:25 unless you are willing to leave lunch promptly and already have your bag. A 4:40 or 4:45 nonstop is the best balance: enough time to leave downtown, get to DEN, and clear security without wasting the evening. A 6:15-ish return is safer if you expect post-lunch conversations.
Put the booking and reimbursement notes together. No rental car.

Denver plan: arrive Sunday June 23 on a nonstop SLC-DEN around 1:45 to 3:18; return Wednesday June 26 on a nonstop around 4:40 to 4:45 after the closing lunch. Hold the official conference block first if it is about $221 before taxes and refundable; hold Hampton downtown/convention center only as a short backup if flexible. Skip the rental car. Use A Line plus short rideshare or local transit downtown; keep rideshare receipts if used. Meal plan: Sunday dinner downtown, verify whether Tuesday/Wednesday conference mornings include coffee or breakfast, otherwise budget quick paid breakfasts. Reimbursement file: airfare receipt, hotel confirmation showing nightly rate under cap, hotel folio, train/rideshare receipts, meal receipts if applicable, and screenshots of cancellation deadlines and any hotel fees.

messages.content: Denver changed a bit. They added a Monday 11:15 roundtable, and the official block released one more room type but with a stricter cancellation date. The Hampton is still there, but Tuesday night jumped. Can you re-rank the plan?

With an 11:15 Monday roundtable, Sunday arrival moves from nice-to-have to the practical choice. Monday morning would be too fragile unless you were comfortable missing the roundtable. Send me the updated hotel rates and cancellation dates and I’ll rank them cleanly.

Official block is $219 before taxes, one queen room, cancel by June 14 at 5 p.m. Hampton averages $226 now because Tuesday went up, cancel 48 hours before arrival. Element is $199 but farther from the venue.

Ranked now: 1. Official block, because it is closest, under the cap, and the Monday roundtable plus Tuesday full day make proximity useful. The trade-off is no included breakfast and the stricter June 14 cancellation. 2. Hampton, because breakfast is included and cancellation is easier, but the rate advantage is basically gone and you add walking. 3. Element, because it saves money but adds the most friction.
Breakfast is the only thing making me pause. I do not want to hunt for food before 8 a.m. sessions.

Use the block hotel and make breakfast boring on purpose. Check whether the conference provides morning coffee or continental breakfast. If not, buy yogurt, fruit, or bars Sunday evening and use one nearby coffee stop for Tuesday. That is less hassle than changing hotels for breakfast now that Hampton is almost the same price.
Good. What about flights? Still Sunday afternoon?

Yes. Hold the Sunday early-afternoon nonstop if it is still reasonable. The 1:45-ish departure is better than a later one because you can check in, pick up snacks, and have dinner without rushing. Monday morning should only be a fallback if Sunday fares become unreasonable.
Return Wednesday: closing lunch is listed as 12:15 to 1:15, but those things always linger. Is a 3:30 return risky?

Yes, 3:30 is skinny. You would need to leave lunch almost immediately, retrieve your bag, get to DEN, and hope security is smooth. A 4:45 return is much more comfortable if you leave downtown by about 2:15. A 6:10 return is the safety option if you expect a long debrief, but it costs you the evening at home.
No debrief planned. I want home before bedtime. Rank the exact version to hold.

Hold this version: official block one-queen room at $219, Sunday early-afternoon nonstop to Denver, Wednesday 4:45-ish nonstop back to Salt Lake, no rental car. Backup: same hotel and flights but a 6:10 return only if the closing lunch agenda grows again. Hampton is now only the backup if breakfast becomes confirmed as completely uncovered and inconvenient.
What deadlines do I need on my calendar?

Calendar June 14 at noon as the decision reminder, because the block cancellation is June 14 at 5 p.m. Also add a flight-price check within 24 hours of the hold, and a week-before reminder to verify conference breakfast, A Line timing, and whether the hotel has any extra destination or facility fee. If you briefly hold Hampton, set its cancellation reminder for 48 hours before arrival.
One more detail: the block room is one queen, not two. That is fine for just me, right?

Yes, one queen is fine for this solo trip. Before booking, confirm the room is refundable until June 14 at 5 p.m., the $219 rate is before taxes and within the cap, and there is no required parking or resort-style fee. Final Denver lean: book the official block, arrive Sunday afternoon, return Wednesday around 4:45, skip the car, and handle breakfast with conference food plus simple grab-and-go backup.

messages.content: I’m ready to reserve Denver. The official block room opened back up, but it’s the one-queen room with no breakfast and the earlier cancellation date. Can you help me make the final call on flights and hotel before I click through?

Yes. I’d keep the flight plan we discussed: Sunday afternoon nonstop SLC to Denver so you can check in without rushing, and the Wednesday midafternoon nonstop after the closing lunch. On the hotel, the trade-off is clear: the official block wins for being in or next to the meeting flow, while the nearby breakfast-included hotel wins on easy mornings. Since your Monday roundtable is now the anchor, I’d book the official block and solve breakfast separately.
That’s where I’m leaning. I would rather be close to the meeting rooms. No rental car, one queen is fine for just me, and please request window seats on the flights if they’re selectable.

Good. For the flights, choose a fare that lets you select seats and avoid basic economy if the price difference is modest. Request window seats on both legs; if the only windows left are paid preferred seats, you can either pay only if it is reimbursable or set a reminder to check again at online check-in. For the hotel, the one-queen official block room is appropriate for a solo trip. Confirm the rate is about $219 before taxes, no required parking charge because you will not have a car, and no destination or facility fee.
Should I also hold the Hampton backup for the breakfast, or is that just creating another thing to cancel?

If the block room checks out as refundable until June 14 at 5 p.m., I would skip the Hampton backup. Hampton is easier for breakfast, but being farther from the sessions is the wrong inconvenience for this agenda. I’d only hold Hampton for a day if the official block page shows a surprise fee, a nonrefundable rule, or a rate above the reimbursement cap.
Okay. Ground transport from DEN: still train first?

Yes, train first if it is running normally when you land. Take the A Line to Union Station, then either walk if the hotel is truly close and the weather is fine, or use a short rideshare for the last hop. Keep the train receipt and any rideshare receipt. If your flight is delayed, you have a heavier bag than expected, or there is service disruption, go straight to rideshare from the airport and document it.
The hotel page confirms cancel by June 14 at 5 p.m. local time, parking is $49 but optional, and I don’t see a destination fee.

That is bookable. Take screenshots of the cancellation rule, nightly rate, taxes, and the no-fee/optional-parking language. Add a calendar reminder for June 14 at noon so you have time to cancel before the 5 p.m. deadline if anything changes.
Breakfast is the only thing I’m still uneasy about. I don’t want Monday to start with a scramble.

Plan it simply: Sunday dinner downtown after check-in; Monday buy breakfast near the hotel before 9:45, then head to the roundtable area early. Check whether the conference provides coffee or pastries Tuesday and Wednesday, but do not rely on it. For dinners, use the conference reception if one is included; otherwise pick something within a short walk of the hotel so you are not managing transportation at night.
Flights and block room are booked. Give me the final booking note for my file.

Denver conference booking note: booked Sunday June 23 nonstop SLC-DEN in the afternoon, arriving with time for downtown check-in; booked Wednesday June 26 nonstop DEN-SLC around 4:45 p.m. after the closing lunch. Window seats requested/selected where available; verify seat numbers again at check-in. Hotel: official downtown conference block, one-queen room, about $219 before taxes, cancel by June 14 at 5 p.m. local time. No rental car. Use A Line to Union Station plus walk/short rideshare; rideshare direct from DEN only if delayed or train service is disrupted. Meals: no included hotel breakfast, so budget quick paid breakfasts and use nearby downtown dinners. Reimbursement file: airfare receipt, hotel confirmation, cancellation screenshot, hotel folio, train/rideshare receipts, and meal receipts if allowed.

messages.content: Denver is in four days. The app added Sunday evening badge pickup, and Monday seating starts earlier than the old agenda. Also, I saw a note about A Line evening maintenance. Can we tighten the timing?

Yes. Assuming the Sunday flight still lands around 3:18, you have enough cushion, but I would not make the train the only plan. Use the A Line if service looks normal when you land; otherwise take rideshare straight from DEN. The goal is hotel by about 5, badge pickup shortly after, then dinner.
Correct, 3:18 landing, carry-on only. Badge pickup is 5 to 7 Sunday.

If there is a maintenance delay longer than 15 to 20 minutes, switch to rideshare. Either way, check in first if the hotel is on the way, then go to badge pickup around 5:30 or 5:45.
Monday seating starts at 10:30 now, with the roundtable at 11. No hotel breakfast.

Monday: be dressed and out for breakfast by 8:45. Pick a quick paid option within a block or two, or grab coffee/yogurt from the hotel market if the line is long. Return to the room by 9:45, take materials with you by 10:10, and be in the seating area at 10:25. If you miss Sunday badge pickup, shift earlier and go to registration around 9:45.
Wednesday closing lunch ends at 1. Flight is about 4:45. What should I do with bags?

Wednesday checklist: check out before sessions and leave your bag with the bell desk; keep laptop, ID, and any receipts with you. After the closing lunch, leave by 1:10, pick up the bag, and depart the hotel by 1:25. Rideshare is the safest buffer for a 4:45 flight; train is okay only if service is clean and you are moving by about 1:20. Target DEN by 2:15, which leaves room for security, a snack, and any gate change.

messages.content: Denver is done, so I’m starting the late-August Pacific Northwest loop. Draft is: Monday high-school visits in Portland, Tuesday evening college fair in Beaverton, Wednesday 8 a.m. counselor breakfast in Eugene, Thursday afternoon Tacoma visit, and Thursday evening Seattle fair. Can you compare open-jaw versus round-trip Portland, car versus rail, and hotel bases with breakfast and easy dinner access?

Yes. One detail will affect the Thursday plan: where is the Seattle fair, downtown or somewhere like Bellevue/Northgate? With the schedule as written, I already lean open-jaw into Portland and home from Seattle, with a rental car, but the Seattle venue decides whether Thursday night should be downtown, SeaTac, or Southcenter.

Seattle fair is at the downtown convention center, 6 to 8 p.m. Tacoma visit is 1:30 Thursday. Beaverton fair is 6:30 to 8:30 Tuesday. Monday visits are Portland proper and one NE Portland school. I’ll have a rolling bag plus one small materials box.

Here’s the practical routing comparison. Open-jaw SLC-PDX and SEA-SLC with a one-way rental car: best schedule, no backtracking after the Seattle fair, and easiest for materials; likely higher than a Portland round trip because of the one-way car fee. Round-trip Portland: cheaper airfare, but after Seattle you either drive three hours late Thursday or wake up very early Friday to get back to PDX. Rail hybrid: workable on paper, but fragile with materials and multiple suburban stops. Recommendation: open-jaw plus rental car.
The Portland round trip may be about $150 cheaper in airfare. Is the backtracking still that bad?

For this itinerary, yes. The Thursday Seattle fair ends at 8, so a same-night drive to Portland means a late arrival near midnight before flying the next day. Waiting until Friday means a predawn drive with traffic and no cushion. That savings is not worth the fatigue and missed-flight risk unless the open-jaw price is dramatically worse after the rental quote.
Open-jaw then. Look at nonstop holds. If Delta lines up, that’s fine, but I don’t want to force a bad time or a connection.

Nonstop shortlist: Sunday SLC-PDX, Delta around 2:10 to 3:15 or Alaska around 4:25 to 5:30. Friday SEA-SLC, Delta around 1:15 to 4:05 or Alaska around 3:05 to 5:55. I’d hold the Delta 2:10 outbound and 1:15 return if pricing is close because the times fit cleanly. Avoid connections for this loop. Request window seats after ticketing if they are available.
The 2:10 Sunday departure works, and Friday 1:15 is fine if I’m staying near SeaTac Thursday. What about car versus train?

Rent the car. Rail would add transfers, rideshares, and schedule risk between Portland, Beaverton, Eugene, Tacoma, and downtown Seattle. Car hold: pick up at PDX Sunday around 3:45 or 4, return at SEA Friday around 11:30, midsize car or compact SUV, one-way drop allowed. Verify the one-way fee, total taxes, and whether parking is reimbursable.
Hotels are the bigger thing. I want easy breakfast, and Tuesday night needs dinner solved because I’ll get to Eugene late.

Best base pattern: Sunday and Monday in Beaverton/Tigard for Portland and the Tuesday fair; Tuesday night in Eugene; Wednesday night in Federal Way or Tacoma; Thursday night SeaTac/Southcenter. Hotel ideas: Hyatt House Beaverton or Hampton Beaverton area for breakfast and nearby restaurants; Home2 Suites Eugene Downtown/University or Hyatt Place Oakway for breakfast or close food; Hampton/Fairfield in Federal Way for breakfast and free parking; Homewood or Hampton near Southcenter/SeaTac for breakfast, dinner access, and an easy Friday airport run.
Would Salem be smarter Tuesday night so I’m not driving all the way to Eugene after the Beaverton fair?

Salem is easier Tuesday night but worse Wednesday morning. Beaverton to Salem after the fair is about 55 to 75 minutes; Salem to Eugene in the morning is another 65 to 80, and you’d need to leave around 6:15 for an 8 a.m. breakfast. Driving to Eugene Tuesday is closer to two hours and a late arrival, but it protects the breakfast. I’d choose Eugene and plan dinner before the fair or bring something for the drive.
Let’s do Eugene. Cancellable queen rooms, no prepaid if possible. Parking needs to be clear for reimbursement.

Good. Holds I’d place: Beaverton/Tigard for Sunday-Monday, queen room, breakfast included, parking fee shown clearly; Eugene Tuesday, queen room, late-arrival note, breakfast start verified; Federal Way Wednesday, queen room, breakfast and free or clearly priced parking; Southcenter/SeaTac Thursday, queen room, breakfast, and restaurants nearby. For each one, screenshot cancellation deadline, nightly rate, parking language, and breakfast details.
For Wednesday, Federal Way might make Thursday easier than Tacoma, right?

Yes. Federal Way splits the difference well. It is usually 20 to 30 minutes to Tacoma, but allow 45. After the 1:30 Tacoma visit, leave for downtown Seattle by about 3:15 or 3:30, park once, eat early near the convention center, and walk into the fair without trying to check into a downtown hotel.
Can I avoid downtown Seattle hotel parking Thursday?

Yes. Use downtown parking only for the fair, then drive to Southcenter or SeaTac afterward. That avoids an overnight downtown hotel parking charge and puts you close to the airport for Friday. If you are hungry after the fair, Southcenter has more late practical options than a random airport hotel block.
Give me the holds to place and what can wait. I’ll send this to my director with the rationale for the open-jaw cost.

Recommended holds: 1) Flights: hold Sunday SLC-PDX nonstop around 2:10 p.m. and Friday SEA-SLC nonstop around 1:15 p.m.; avoid connections. 2) Car: one-way rental, PDX pickup Sunday about 4 p.m., SEA return Friday about 11:30 a.m.; verify one-way fee and total taxes. 3) Hotels: Beaverton/Tigard Sunday-Monday with breakfast and dinner nearby; Eugene Tuesday with late-arrival note and breakfast verified; Federal Way Wednesday with breakfast/free or clearly priced parking; Southcenter or SeaTac Thursday with breakfast and easy Friday airport access. Rationale for director: open-jaw costs more than a Portland round trip, but it avoids a late-night or predawn three-hour backtrack after the Seattle fair, protects the Friday return, and reduces fatigue during a multi-city recruitment week. messages.content: Texas is wrapped up, so I need to start the late-October Upper Midwest loop. Draft is Sunday SLC to the Chicago area, Monday suburban high-school visits plus an evening fair near Oak Brook, Tuesday morning counselor breakfast in Madison, Wednesday Milwaukee high-school appointments, and a Thursday late-afternoon counselor meetup now planned around Wauwatosa. Can you compare Chicago round-trip versus flying into Chicago and home from Milwaukee, and tell me if I should keep a rental car the whole time? I also need hotel bases that won’t leave me stranded for dinner.

I can. Before I rank it: what are the rough fair end time Monday, the Thursday meetup end time, and are you planning to fly home Friday rather than Thursday night? Also, any nightly hotel ceiling I should use for the first pass?

Assume Monday fair ends around 8:15, Thursday runs 4:30 to 6:30, and I want to fly home Friday. Sunday departure can be after lunch because I have a morning handoff. For hotels, I would like to stay around $240 before tax when possible. Breakfast included is helpful, but I care more about not having a silly drive before a 7 or 8 a.m. event. Delta is nice from SLC if the schedule is comparable, but do not force it.

Then Chicago-in and Milwaukee-out is the cleaner working plan. Quick comparison: Chicago round-trip is probably cheaper by roughly $150-$250 after fare differences, but it adds a Wauwatosa-to-Chicago backtrack Thursday night or a Friday morning drive to O'Hare, plus tolls and weather risk. Chicago-in/Milwaukee-out may cost more and may add a one-way car fee, but it protects Thursday evening, reduces fatigue, and keeps Friday simpler. I would keep one rental car from Chicago pickup to Milwaukee return; trains and rideshares look fussy for Oak Brook, Madison, and suburban Milwaukee with materials and luggage.
For Chicago, would you aim for O'Hare or Midway?

O'Hare is my first choice because it usually has more SLC afternoon choices, more rental inventory, and an easier angle to Oak Brook. Midway is workable if it has a clearly better nonstop or fare, but I would not take Midway just to save a small amount. For the car, the one-way fee is acceptable if it is visible upfront and not much over the cost of the extra gas, tolls, and time of backtracking.
Can you sketch the hotel nights? I do not want the Madison breakfast ruined by a 5 a.m. drive from Oak Brook.

Best sequence on the draft times: Sunday night Oak Brook or Oakbrook Terrace; Monday after the fair, drive to Madison and sleep near the breakfast venue; Tuesday night Madison again if Wednesday appointments start later, or Milwaukee/Wauwatosa if Wednesday starts early; Wednesday and Thursday nights in Wauwatosa, Brookfield, or Milwaukee West. The only awkward piece is the Monday late drive to Madison, but it is still better than leaving Oak Brook before dawn Tuesday.
How bad is that Monday drive after the fair? Would Rockford make more sense?

Oak Brook to Madison after 8:30 p.m. is usually about 2 hours 10 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes, so you could arrive around 10:45 or 11:00. Rockford splits the pain, but it creates a Tuesday morning drive of about 1 hour 10 minutes before a breakfast event, which is the wrong side of the trade-off. I would only use Rockford if Madison rates are unreasonable or late check-in is a problem.
Okay, Madison Monday. I will need food that night.

Do not count on a real dinner after arriving in Madison. Eat something near Oak Brook before leaving if the fair food is light, and keep a sandwich or protein box in the car. For the Madison hotel, I would favor late check-in, a lobby market, and at least one nearby restaurant or delivery option over a prettier location.
What flight options would you shortlist?

Outbound Sunday: shortlist a 1-3 p.m. SLC to O'Hare nonstop if the fare is reasonable; a similar United or American nonstop is fine if it lands earlier or costs materially less; keep a Midway option only as a price check. Return Friday from Milwaukee: look for one-stop itineraries through MSP, Detroit, Atlanta, Denver, or Chicago with a comfortable connection. I would avoid very early departures because they waste the benefit of staying near Wauwatosa, and I would avoid anything with two stops unless finance forces it.
Rank the return choices. I would rather not get home too late, but connection quality matters more than carrier.

Ranking for now: first, a late-morning or early-afternoon MKE-SLC one-stop with about 70-100 minutes to connect; second, a midafternoon MKE-SLC with a longer but not absurd connection if the first option gets too tight; third, driving to O'Hare for a cheaper or nonstop return; last, a pre-8 a.m. Milwaukee departure or any two-stop routing. The Chicago return needs a big savings to justify the backtrack.
Give me hotel areas or examples to hold, not final bookings yet.

Oak Brook: look at Oakbrook Terrace or Oak Brook proper near the fair, with free parking and food nearby; Hyatt House, Hilton Garden Inn, or a comparable Marriott/Hilton property would be practical. Madison: first choice is downtown or near the UW/counselor breakfast if the rate is tolerable; Hampton Inn downtown or a campus-adjacent Hilton/Marriott works if late check-in is confirmed. If rates spike, Middleton is the backup, but it adds morning drive time. Milwaukee: Wauwatosa, Brookfield, or Milwaukee West near Mayfair/Research Park; Residence Inn, SpringHill Suites, or a similar property with breakfast and parking would fit the logistics.
What deadlines should I put on the calendar?

Put three holds on a calendar: flights by fare-lock expiration, hotels by each refundable cancellation cutoff, and car by any free-cancel deadline. I would also set a reminder 10 days out to release the Chicago round-trip benchmark if the open-jaw premium is still reasonable, and another reminder 72 hours before travel to recheck breakfast times, parking, and late arrival notes.
Can you summarize the recommendation for the approval request?

Recommended plan for approval: fly SLC to Chicago on Sunday afternoon, preferably into O'Hare unless Midway is clearly better; rent one car in Chicago and return it in Milwaukee; fly home Friday from MKE. This costs more than a Chicago round-trip but avoids the Thursday night or Friday morning backtrack after Wauwatosa, reduces fatigue, and protects the Madison breakfast. Hotel sequence: Oak Brook/Oakbrook Terrace Sunday, Madison Monday and likely Tuesday, Wauwatosa or Milwaukee West Wednesday-Thursday. Meal notes: eat or pack dinner before the Monday Madison drive, verify breakfast hours at Madison and Wauwatosa hotels, and choose properties with nearby restaurants rather than isolated highway stays.

Tuesday: use the Hampton breakfast at 6:00, but carry a bar in case the room is crowded. Wednesday and Thursday: Residence Inn breakfast should work unless a school visit starts very early; buy one backup item Tuesday night. Friday: grab coffee only if it is quick, then airport timeline first.
Late dinners?

Yes. Short version: drive if the I-84 forecast is clean; fly-and-rent only helps if Monday weather between Salt Lake and Boise looks messy. You still have to handle the Boise/Nampa to Twin Falls stretch either way, so flying does not remove the winter-road issue entirely.
Give me the trade-offs plainly.

Drive: leave Salt Lake around 1:00 p.m. Monday, reach Boise about 6:30 to 7:00 with one stop, no airport or rental delay, lowest cost, flexible Wednesday return. Risk is weather and fatigue on I-84. Fly and rent: take a Monday afternoon SLC-BOI nonstop, rent at Boise, then either one-way the car toward Twin Falls or backtrack to Boise. It is easier Monday but more expensive and less flexible, especially if the Twin Falls flight timing or one-way rental is poor.

For now, hold refundable hotels and plan to drive. Put a weather decision point on Sunday evening and again Monday by 9:00 a.m. If snow, wind, or chain controls are likely on I-84, pivot to the afternoon Boise flight and a rental. If the roads are just cold and clear, driving is the simpler loop.

Monday: stay in Boise near downtown or Boise State if the breakfast is central. That protects the 7:30 start and leaves dinner options nearby. Meridian is fine only if the breakfast is west Boise; it helps Nampa but adds morning risk. Tuesday: move to Twin Falls after the Nampa fair if you can safely drive the two hours that night. That makes Wednesday morning much calmer than leaving Boise before dawn.
I like that, but the Nampa fair may run until 8:30. Is the late drive to Twin Falls still okay?

It is acceptable if the weather is dry and you eat before leaving Nampa. Plan 8:45 departure, arrive Twin Falls around 10:45, and keep check-in notified. If the roads are wet, icy, or visibility is bad, stay Nampa/Meridian Tuesday and leave very early Wednesday, but that is the less comfortable plan.
Shortlist practical hotels with breakfast and dinner access. Nothing resorty.

Boise options: Hampton Inn & Suites Boise-Downtown, breakfast included, restaurants walkable, paid parking; Hyatt Place Boise/Downtown, easy food nearby, breakfast depending on rate; or Homewood Suites Meridian if the breakfast location ends up west, with easier parking but a longer Tuesday morning. Twin Falls options: Fairfield Inn & Suites near Pole Line, Hampton Inn Twin Falls, or TownePlace Suites. All keep you near Blue Lakes/Pole Line restaurants and set up an easy Wednesday school visit.

No. If you are approved to use the university vehicle or mileage reimbursement, skip the rental. Okay, let’s use that one. Make it two queens for the three of us, and note that we’ll have tournament bags in the car. Anything special to request?

Saturday breakfast worries me. Hotel breakfast starts at 6:30 and they want players warming up by 7:25.

Load the car before Sunday games and keep late checkout only if they grant it for free. If they’re out early, leave after lunch. messages.content: I’m switching back to work travel. I have a late-February Front Range yield loop: Wednesday 7:30 counselor breakfast near Boulder, Wednesday 6:30 admitted-student reception near Denver Tech Center, Thursday 8:15 setup for a transfer fair in Aurora, and a Thursday 5:30 alumni counselor meetup in Fort Collins. Can you help me decide fly versus drive and where to hold hotels?
Absolutely. Two things affect the reliability of this one: when can you leave Salt Lake on Tuesday, and do you need to be home Thursday night or is Friday morning acceptable?
I can leave Tuesday after 1:00. Friday morning is acceptable. I’d only try Thursday night if it’s genuinely clean, not a sprint from Fort Collins to the airport.

Then I’d compare it this way:

Fly + rental: fastest, avoids the long winter I-80 drive, and gives you a car for the scattered events. Best if you arrive Tuesday afternoon or early evening.

Drive from Salt Lake: more flexible with materials and no rental counter, but it adds a full winter driving day each way and gives you less margin if weather turns.

Given the 7:30 Wednesday breakfast and the late Thursday Fort Collins event, flying Tuesday and returning Friday is the cleaner planning base.
I’m leaning fly unless the rental makes it silly. Could I survive with one hotel base, or is this a split-nights trip?

One base is possible, but not elegant. Broomfield/Westminster is the least-bad single base: reasonable for Boulder, not awful to DTC/Aurora, and north enough for Fort Collins. The downside is you’d be doing a late drive back north after the DTC reception and then an early drive southeast to Aurora.

Split nights reduce risk: Tuesday near Boulder/Broomfield, Wednesday near DTC/Aurora, Thursday near the airport after Fort Collins for a Friday flight.
Three hotels is annoying. What about Broomfield Tuesday and Wednesday, then airport Thursday?

That cuts one check-in, but Thursday morning becomes the weak spot. From Broomfield to an 8:15 Aurora setup, you’d want to leave quite early and still carry traffic risk. Since the DTC reception ends around 8:00 or later Wednesday, moving to a DTC/Aurora hotel that night makes Thursday much calmer.
The DTC reception is scheduled to end at 8:15. You’re right; I don’t want a pre-dawn traffic gamble to Aurora.

Then I’d use this driving pattern: Tuesday fly in, pick up rental, sleep Boulder/Broomfield. Wednesday breakfast near Boulder, midday work block, then drive south before peak traffic and stay DTC/Aurora after the reception. Thursday do the Aurora fair, drive to Fort Collins midday with a lunch stop, then after the 5:30 meetup either stay near the airport or, if the flight is later Friday, stay north and drive down in the morning.
Please shortlist hotels by area. Breakfast helps, and dinner access matters after the reception. Nothing fancy.

Shortlist to check first:

Boulder/Broomfield Tuesday: Hyatt House Boulder/Broomfield or a Hampton/Residence Inn in Broomfield-Interlocken. Look for included breakfast, easy parking, and nearby casual dinner.

DTC/Aurora Wednesday: Hyatt Place Denver Tech Center, Hampton Inn Denver Tech Center South, or a practical Aurora South hotel near the fair site. Favor whichever is closer to the Thursday venue and has food within a short drive.

Airport Thursday: Hampton/Hyatt Place-style options in Gateway Park or Peña Station. They usually make Friday morning rental return simpler than sleeping deep downtown.
If you had to hold only a couple refundable rooms now, which ones?

Hold one Broomfield/Interlocken room for Tuesday and one DTC/Aurora room for Wednesday. I’d wait on the Thursday airport room until flights are narrowed, unless the refundable rate is painless. The first two nights are driven by event timing; Thursday depends on whether the Friday return is early or late morning.
Good. For flights, I do not want a connection on Salt Lake to Denver unless something is really off.

Agreed. For this route, target a nonstop Tuesday after 1:00 that lands with enough daylight and rental-car buffer. I’d avoid the last flight of the night. For Friday, a midmorning nonstop gives you time to return the rental without making the airport hotel feel pointless.
Delta if it’s close, but don’t pay a big premium. And window seat if I can choose it.

Got it. I’ll compare nonstop options by timing and price, with Delta favored only if it’s comparable. I’ll also note whether a window seat can be selected at booking or whether it has to wait until check-in.
Can you give me the practical version to send myself? I don’t need booking language yet.

Practical plan: fly SLC to Denver Tuesday afternoon after 1:00, rent a car, and avoid connecting flights. Hold Tuesday night in Broomfield/Interlocken for the Boulder breakfast. Move south Wednesday afternoon and hold Wednesday night near DTC/Aurora so the Thursday 8:15 setup is low-stress. After the Aurora fair, drive to Fort Collins with a lunch buffer before the 5:30 meetup. Tentatively plan Thursday night near the airport for a Friday midmorning nonstop home, but finalize that once fares and return times are checked. For hotels, prioritize included breakfast where it actually helps and easy dinner access after the DTC reception.

Ranking now: 1) Friday return from Denver: best reliability, because you can eat after Fort Collins, sleep near DEN, and handle rental return without sprinting. 2) Thursday night only if there is a very late nonstop and you are willing to skip a real dinner. 3) Thursday connection: I would not choose it for this loop. The risk is the Fort Collins-to-DEN drive plus rental return, bag/security, and a tired end of day.
That matches my gut. What about hotels—can I still avoid moving every night, or is that going to create worse mornings?

One base is possible, but each version hurts a different event. A Broomfield/Interlocken base helps Boulder and is decent for Fort Collins, but makes the Aurora campus morning longer and parking uncertainty worse. A DTC/Aurora base helps the transfer fair but makes the earlier Boulder check-in a pre-dawn drive. The least stressful working plan is split: Tuesday Broomfield/Interlocken, Wednesday Aurora or DTC, and then likely Thursday near DEN if you choose the Friday return. It is more packing, but the hotel changes follow the route instead of fighting it.
If Boulder availability is tightening, which Tuesday area should I target first?

Start with Broomfield/Interlocken, not central Boulder. It keeps the Boulder drive around 15–25 minutes without paying campus-event prices, and it has easier parking and dinner. Louisville or Superior is the backup if Broomfield jumps. I would avoid downtown Denver Tuesday because the earlier check-in makes that unnecessary stress.
For Wednesday, Aurora versus DTC? Parking worries me more than restaurant variety at this point.

Then lean Aurora/Anschutz if you can get a refundable rate with breakfast and parking that is not absurd. You’ll be closer for the morning setup and can scout the campus garage the night before. DTC is more comfortable for dinner, but it adds another variable on the one morning where parking is already constrained. Ask the host which garage exhibitors should use, whether there is an unload zone, and whether the visitor lot uses an app.
What drive-time risk should I respect most, especially with Fort Collins in the mix?

For Boulder, the risk is campus traffic and check-in moving earlier, so leave Broomfield with a 20-minute cushion. For Aurora, build in 15–20 minutes just for parking/payment, even if the hotel is close. For Fort Collins, do not leave Aurora hungry or right at the last possible minute; northbound traffic can look fine and then clog. I’d rather you arrive early and answer email in the car than eat the whole buffer on I-25.
Can you add breakfast and dinner backups and give me the clean ranking to use when I start holding rooms?

Clean plan: first, hold Tuesday in Broomfield/Interlocken with free parking and breakfast if available. Second, hold Wednesday in Aurora/Anschutz; use DTC only if Aurora rates are ugly. Third, hold Thursday near DEN if the Friday nonstop is reasonably priced, because it protects the airport morning. Food backups: Tuesday dinner near Broomfield/FlatIron Crossing; Wednesday do not rely entirely on the Boulder host breakfast, so bring a bar or yogurt and get coffee after setup; Wednesday dinner near Aurora/Anschutz or DTC depending on the hotel; Thursday eat lunch before leaving Aurora, then do a quick Fort Collins dinner after the meetup or fall back to Tower Road near the airport hotel. Flight ranking: Friday return first, late Thursday nonstop distant second, Thursday connection no.

messages.content: Denver is wrapped enough that I need to start the Pacific Northwest loop. Tuesday morning counselor breakfast in Salem, Tuesday evening admitted-student reception in Beaverton, Wednesday transfer table in Vancouver, Washington, and Wednesday evening alumni meetup near Tacoma. Can you compare Portland round-trip versus flying into Portland and home from Seattle, and help me figure out hotel areas? I want breakfast and late dinner logistics not to be chaotic.

Yes. The airport decision is mostly about the end of the loop, not the start. Portland round-trip is usually simpler for the rental car, but after the Tacoma meetup it creates either a late 2.5 to 3 hour drive back toward Portland or a very early Thursday airport morning. Portland-in and Seattle-out adds a one-way car return, but it fits the actual route much better. Before I rank it too hard: what time can you leave Salt Lake on Monday, and when do you need to be back Thursday?
I can leave Monday after a noon meeting, so afternoon is best. Thursday I need to be back by late afternoon. If Delta has a sensible option, include it, but not if the connection is worse.

Then I would look first at a Monday afternoon nonstop SLC to PDX, roughly a 1:30 to 3:30 departure window, on Delta or Alaska if the times work. For Thursday, the cleaner target is a SEA to SLC nonstop late morning or early afternoon. I would only use a Portland return if it saves real money, roughly $250 or more after the one-way rental fee, or if the Seattle return forces a bad connection.
What does the driving pattern look like? I am undecided on whether Salem the first night is worth the extra hotel move.

Basic route: PDX to Salem Monday is about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 if you land before the worst evening traffic. Salem to Beaverton after the Tuesday breakfast is usually 55 to 75 minutes. Beaverton to Vancouver after the reception is 35 to 45 minutes later in the evening. Vancouver to Tacoma on Wednesday can be 2 to 2.5 hours depending on I-5. Tacoma to SeaTac after the meetup is usually 35 to 45 minutes. If the Salem breakfast check-in is early, Salem Monday is worth it. If breakfast starts later, Beaverton or Tigard Monday could reduce one move, but it makes Tuesday morning more fragile.
The Salem check-in may be 7:30. Beaverton probably ends around 8:30 p.m. Tacoma is likely done around 8-ish, but not confirmed.

With a 7:30 Salem check-in, I would protect Tuesday morning. My practical plan is: Monday night in Salem, Tuesday night either Vancouver or north Portland, Wednesday night near SeaTac. It is three hotel nights in three places, which is annoying, but each drive has a purpose and you avoid the worst late-night backtrack. The risky version is Portland round-trip plus a Wednesday night drive south after Tacoma; I would not choose that unless the price difference is large.
Could Tuesday night be Beaverton instead of Vancouver so I am not packing up after the reception?

It can. Beaverton Tuesday is easier immediately after the reception: short drive, quicker dinner, simpler check-in. The trade-off is Wednesday morning from Beaverton to Vancouver, which can be 35 to 60 minutes with bridge traffic and parking time. Vancouver Tuesday is better if the transfer table has an early setup or if parking on that campus is fussy. Beaverton Tuesday is better if the event runs late or the host adds a dinner.
Food is the thing I do not want to scramble over. Breakfast hours too, especially Salem.

For Salem, only hold a hotel where breakfast is listed at 6:00 or 6:30 and the venue is within about 15 minutes. If breakfast starts at 6:30 and check-in is 7:30, still buy yogurt or a bar Monday night as a backup. For Beaverton after the reception, use Cedar Hills Crossing, downtown Beaverton, or Washington Square as dinner fallbacks, but check closing times because 8:45 can be late for a full meal. For Vancouver, the waterfront has better restaurants but more parking friction; Jantzen or Delta Park is easier for parking but thinner on late food. After Tacoma, eat near the meetup if it ends on time; otherwise drive to SeaTac and use an airport-area late option or hotel bistro.
Which areas should I actually hold tonight while the hosts are still confirming exact times?

Hold refundable rooms in three buckets. First, Salem near I-5, Commercial Street, or Mill Creek for Monday, with easy parking and breakfast verified. Second, hold two Tuesday possibilities for now: Beaverton or Cedar Hills if Tuesday comfort matters more, and Vancouver, Jantzen, or downtown Vancouver if Wednesday setup timing becomes tight. Third, hold SeaTac or Angle Lake for Wednesday night rather than downtown Tacoma, because it protects the Thursday flight without making you drive all the way back to Portland.
What about Salem Monday, Beaverton Tuesday, and SeaTac Wednesday? That feels logical on the map.

That is a reasonable sequence if the Vancouver table starts late morning. It gives you the best Tuesday evening recovery: finish Beaverton, eat nearby, sleep nearby. The only exposed piece is Wednesday morning Beaverton to Vancouver, especially if you need to unload materials before a before-lunch table. If Vancouver setup is 10:30 or later, I am comfortable with Beaverton Tuesday. If it is before 9:30, I would switch Tuesday to Vancouver or Jantzen.
The Vancouver time is not confirmed. I only know Wednesday sometime before lunch.

Then hold both Tuesday options for a couple of days: one Beaverton or Cedar Hills room and one Vancouver or Jantzen room, both refundable. Put cancellation reminders a day before each deadline. Once Vancouver confirms, release one. I would not let that uncertainty keep you from choosing the Seattle return if the fare is reasonable; Tacoma already makes Seattle the cleaner exit.
Can you give me a clean shortlist with the flight choice, hotel holds, and what would change your mind?

Clean shortlist: first choice flight is SLC to PDX Monday afternoon, then SEA to SLC Thursday late morning or early afternoon, nonstop if available. Use Portland round-trip only if Seattle return plus the one-way car fee is more than about $250 higher or the SEA flight forces an awkward connection. Rental car: pick up at PDX Monday and return at SEA Thursday. Hotel holds: Monday Salem I-5 with breakfast verified; Tuesday hold both Beaverton/Cedar Hills and Vancouver/Jantzen until the transfer-table time lands; Wednesday SeaTac or Angle Lake. Decision triggers: keep Salem Monday if breakfast check-in stays before 8:00, choose Vancouver Tuesday if setup is before 9:30, and keep SeaTac Wednesday if Tacoma ends after 8:00.

Hotel sequence is where I am hesitating. Salem Monday is obvious now, but Tuesday is the question. Is Vancouver worth the extra drive after the Beaverton reception?

Given the earlier Salem check-in and tighter Beaverton inventory, I would use the three-property sequence: Monday Salem, Tuesday Vancouver or Jantzen, Wednesday SeaTac. The fewer-move version, like Monday and Tuesday in Beaverton, now has two problems: higher rates and an early Wednesday drive into a campus-parking situation. The Tuesday night drive from Beaverton to Vancouver is not fun after a reception, but it is shorter and calmer than gambling on Wednesday morning.
I do not love hotel changes, but I hate the long late drive more.

Then the three-property plan matches that. It keeps the longest drive, Vancouver to Tacoma, in the daytime on Wednesday, and it turns the post-Tacoma segment into a manageable SeaTac drive instead of a backtrack to Portland. I would choose function over unpacking comfort on this one.
What should I do about Vancouver parking? The host sounded nervous about visitor spaces.

Ask the host for the exact lot name, permit process, and an overflow option before you book the Tuesday hotel. Plan to arrive 45 minutes early. If you are carrying materials, drop them at the building first, then park. Do not rely on the small visitor lot as the only plan. For the hotel, pick based on the campus address: downtown or waterfront if the table is central Vancouver, Jantzen if you want easier hotel parking, or Columbia Tech Center if the campus is east. If parking is limited, closer beats prettier.

Beaverton: first choice Cedar Hills Crossing if the reception is nearby; second, downtown Beaverton for quick restaurants; third, Washington Square if you are closer to 217 and it is not too late. If the event runs past 8:45, assume fast casual or hotel pantry rather than a long sit-down meal. Tacoma: if you are released right at 8:15, eat near the venue on 6th Ave, Proctor, or the waterfront depending on location. If there is any delay, drive straight to SeaTac and use a late airport-area option.
Give me the final rank I should use when I book tomorrow.

Book in this order: first, open-jaw flights, SLC to PDX Monday afternoon and SEA to SLC Thursday late morning or early afternoon. Second, rental car one-way PDX to SEA; accept the one-way fee if the total stays reasonable. Third, Monday Salem near the breakfast venue with verified early breakfast or at least grab-and-go. Fourth, Tuesday Vancouver area, leaning closest to the campus parking plan rather than Beaverton. Fifth, Wednesday SeaTac or Angle Lake. Keep Portland round-trip only as a price emergency, and release the Beaverton hold once the Vancouver parking instructions are usable.

Hotels are Monday Hampton Inn & Suites Salem, Tuesday Homewood Suites Vancouver-Portland, Wednesday Hampton Inn & Suites Seattle-Airport/28th Ave. This sequence protects the 7:05 Salem check-in, shortens the Wednesday campus arrival, and keeps you close to the airport after Tacoma.
Use one-bed rooms. Queen if selectable, non-smoking. I will have two bins and a carry-on, so intermediate car is fine. Also add window seats if there are open ones.

Add to booking: one-bed non-smoking room at each hotel, queen selected where the room type allows it; if the hotel only lists king for the one-bed refundable rate, that is still better than two doubles for this trip. For flights, request window seats on both legs during seat selection, and avoid Basic so the seat request is not blocked or delayed.
What times should I put for the rental car?

Use PDX pickup 3:45 or 4:00 p.m., depending on the scheduled arrival, so the counter does not treat you as late. Use SEA return around 10:00 a.m. for the 12:20 flight. That gives time for fuel, rental return, shuttle or walk, and bag drop. If fuel lines are bad Thursday morning, protect the airport buffer and let the reimbursement note show the fuel charge if needed.
Parking and breakfast checks?

Hampton Salem: confirm free self-parking and breakfast starting at 6:00; still buy a backup breakfast item Monday night because 7:05 is tight. Homewood Vancouver-Portland: breakfast is usually early enough for Wednesday, but verify the posted start time and whether parking is included on this rate. Hampton Seattle-Airport/28th Ave: expect airport-area parking to be paid or limited, roughly the $15 to $25 range unless the rate says otherwise; breakfast should be available before a 10:00 car return, but it is not critical. Also budget for Vancouver campus visitor parking or a paid overflow lot.
Dinner backups in the note too, please.

Dinner notes: Monday Salem, eat near the hotel or pick up something on the way from PDX so the early morning is simple. Tuesday after Beaverton, use Cedar Hills Crossing or downtown Beaverton before driving to Vancouver; if the reception runs late, grab something quick rather than waiting for a sit-down. Wednesday after Tacoma, eat near the venue only if you are out right at 8:15; otherwise drive to SeaTac and use an airport-area late option or the hotel market.
And cancellation dates and receipts, then I am clicking.

Cancellation reminders, assuming the flexible terms shown stay the same: Salem cancel by Sunday 6 p.m.; Vancouver cancel by Monday 6 p.m.; SeaTac cancel by Tuesday 6 p.m. Save or screenshot the terms before purchase. Receipt checklist: airfare receipt, seat or fare upgrade receipt if separate, rental estimate and final rental receipt showing the one-way fee, fuel receipt, each hotel folio, hotel parking if charged, Vancouver campus or overflow parking, Tacoma parking if charged, and any baggage or materials fees. After booking, download the Vancouver parking map and confirm the window-seat assignments.

Use this: Mon: after PDX/rental, drive straight to Salem, check in, then buy a breakfast backup before you settle in. Tue: skip hotel breakfast; check out by 6:35 with coffee/banana/yogurt from the backup stop, 7:05 counselor check-in, then drive north. Vancouver: try visitor/permit parking first, but switch to overflow by 12:05 rather than circling; keep the host's map downloaded. Tacoma: aim for 4:50, try the signed alternate entrance once, and if it is not obvious go directly to C lot. Build in the extra walk. Dinner: don't book anything tight; either a simple Tacoma dinner at 7:45 if parking is easy, or eat near the SeaTac hotel after you get back.
And Thursday morning? I need fuel, car return, and bag drop without cutting it close.

Protect it this way: breakfast at the SeaTac Hampton around 7:30, leave the hotel by 8:45, fuel by 9:00, rental return by 9:20, shuttle/walk to the terminal and bag drop by 10:00. That leaves room for a receipt issue or security line before the 12:20 flight. Put the fuel stop in your map now, and keep the rental, fuel, hotel folio, parking, and baggage receipts separate.

messages.content: Back at my desk after the PNW loop. I need a first pass for the late-April enrollment-management conference in Minneapolis. Registration opens Sunday afternoon, sessions Monday and Tuesday, closing workshop ends Wednesday at noon. Can you compare Sunday SLC flight windows and hotel options? Official hotel block is convenient but close to my $250 pre-tax cap; a couple nearby business hotels include breakfast.
Sure. For Sunday, is the goal to arrive before registration opens, or just sometime before it closes? That changes whether an afternoon departure is safe or too tight.
Comfortably before 4 if the price isn't silly. I can leave earlier Sunday; arriving after registration starts would make the evening annoying.

Then flight shortlist: 8:30-9:30 a.m. nonstop SLC-MSP, arrives around lunch: best buffer and simplest; 11:00-noon nonstop, arrives midafternoon: workable if no checked bag delay; 2:00-3:30 p.m. departure: too late unless you are fine skipping registration; one-stop via DEN/PHX: only use if it saves real money and has at least about an hour connection. I'd shop the morning and late-morning nonstops first.

Hotel rates I see: official block $246 before tax, no breakfast listed, 72-hour cancel. Hampton downtown $189 with breakfast, 10-minute walk. Hyatt Place $205 with breakfast, maybe 12-minute walk. Hilton Garden $214, restaurant on site but no free breakfast, 8-minute walk.

Hotel read: official block wins on convenience and bad-weather certainty, but it burns nearly all the cap and breakfast is extra or unclear. Hampton is best value if the walk is straightforward: free breakfast, lower rate, restaurants nearby, and room to absorb taxes/fees. Hyatt Place is similar with a slightly longer walk but usually easy meal logistics. Hilton Garden is the dinner-convenience play because of the restaurant, but breakfast costs may erase the rate advantage. Check whether any add amenity or destination fees; finance may care even if the room rate is under cap.
I don't want to feel stranded after sessions, and Tuesday alumni dinner may be optional. They haven't set the restaurant.

Then I would not pay the block rate just for the dinner. Downtown or North Loop dining should be a short rideshare if the dinner moves, and the breakfast-included hotels keep mornings easy. The official hotel becomes worth it if the dinner is in the conference hotel, the weather forecast looks ugly, or you will be carrying materials back and forth.
What about cancellation? The block cutoff is Friday.

Before Friday, hold a refundable nearby room if the policy is clean. If the official block is still refundable and no deposit, you can hold it as insurance too; if it has turned prepaid or nonrefundable, skip it unless finance approves. Screenshot the rate, taxes, cancellation deadline, and breakfast language.
If I'm only holding one room, which one? The Hampton refundable queen is still there.

Hold the Hampton downtown queen room if the walking route is direct and the cancellation is at least 48-72 hours out. It gives you the best reimbursement cushion and breakfast. Choose Hyatt Place instead only if its route is better lit or closer to the conference entrance, or if the Hampton shows a fee at checkout.
Give me the things that would change your mind.

Flight: switch from morning to late-morning only if the savings are meaningful and it still gets you downtown by about 3:30; avoid the afternoon arrival unless registration can be handled Monday. Hotel: switch to the official block if a refundable room reappears within about $25 a night of Hampton/Hyatt, Tuesday dinner lands there, or weather makes the walk a bad bet. Otherwise hold the refundable breakfast hotel and revisit once the agenda and dinner location land.

Only if it is much cheaper and you can pick up materials Monday. With taxi/rideshare time, a 4 p.m. landing probably means conference check-in closer to 5. I'd use the 10-11 a.m. departure for a calmer first night.
Okay. Return after the Wednesday noon workshop?
Choose an MSP-SLC nonstop at 3:30 p.m. or later. That gives you time for the workshop to run over, a quick lunch, hotel bag pickup, and airport transfer. A 1-2 p.m. departure is too tight.
Seat selection and arrival logistics? If there are decent windows, I'd take them.

Request window seats on both legs if available. Arrival plan: carry-on only if you can; rideshare from MSP to downtown is simplest with materials, about 20-30 minutes outside peak traffic. If you land around 2, you can drop bags by 3 and reach registration without rushing. For the North Loop dinner, rideshare both ways unless you end up walking with a group.
Any final reminders before I book?

Book: Sunday late-morning nonstop SLC-MSP, Wednesday mid/late-afternoon nonstop MSP-SLC, refundable Hampton downtown queen with breakfast. Put the hotel cancellation deadline from the confirmation on your calendar, save the prepaid-block screenshot as the reason you declined it, and keep airfare, hotel folio, rideshare/light-rail, baggage, and alumni-dinner receipts separate.

messages.content: Quick Minneapolis wrinkle. The app now says Sunday badge pickup is 2:00 to 5:00, and the airline moved my outbound a bit later. Hotel says they’ll hold bags but won’t promise early check-in. Can we sanity-check the first afternoon and Wednesday?
Yes. The bag choice is the one detail that changes the Sunday risk. Are you planning carry-on only, or do we need to assume a checked bag?
Assume carry-on. If I check anything it would only be last minute, and I’d rather not build the plan around that.

Then Sunday still works. If the flight lands around 1:20, aim to be off the plane and moving by 1:40, downtown about 2:15, hotel bag drop by 2:30, and badge pickup around 2:45 to 3:00. No early check-in needed. If you end up checking a bag, add 20 to 30 minutes and skip any airport food stop.
Would you do light rail or rideshare from MSP?

Carry-on plus decent weather: light rail is fine and predictable, roughly 30 minutes to downtown plus the walk. If it’s raining, you’re tired, or the flight lands after 1:45, use rideshare and go straight to the Hampton. Either way, don’t stop at the conference venue first with luggage.
Good. Also confirm meals. I don’t want to discover Sunday night that nothing convenient is open, and Tuesday’s alumni dinner is farther from the venue now.

Use hotel breakfast Monday through Wednesday. For Sunday, pack a snack or grab something after badge pickup; don’t rely on lunch at MSP. Tuesday dinner in North Loop: walk only if weather and shoes cooperate, otherwise rideshare from the conference venue and back to the hotel. Put the dinner address in your calendar now.
And Wednesday after the noon workshop?

Protect it like this: check out before the workshop and leave your bag with the hotel. At noon, go straight back, collect the bag by 12:20, and head to MSP by 12:30. That should put you at the airport around 1:15 to 1:35, which is comfortable for a mid/late-afternoon nonstop. If the workshop runs over, leave anyway; the airport window matters more.

messages.content: Minneapolis is behind me, and now I have a small Idaho thing. Monday late-afternoon counselor coffee in Twin Falls, Tuesday morning breakfast near Nampa, Tuesday evening admitted-family meetup downtown Boise. Can you compare driving from Salt Lake versus flying into Boise and renting?
I can. The key question is when you can realistically leave Salt Lake on Monday. Do you have a morning campus commitment, or can you get on the road early?
I can leave after a 9:00 handoff. So maybe 9:45 or 10:00 if I’m packed. Coffee in Twin Falls is 4:30. Tuesday breakfast is currently 8:00-ish, and Boise is 6:30.

Here’s the practical comparison:

Drive SLC-Twin Falls-Nampa-Boise: best fit for the route, no backtracking, car is with you all day. Watch-out: long Monday and I-84 delay risk.

Fly SLC-BOI + rental: predictable flight segment, but you’d land in Boise, rent a car, then drive back west/south to Twin Falls. It saves little once airport time is included.

Fly into Twin Falls: only worth checking if timing is perfect; smaller-market connections make this less reliable for a 4:30 event.
So driving is probably the answer. How would you lay out the actual route?

Leave Salt Lake by 10:00. Build in one real stop and target Twin Falls by 2:30 to 3:00, which gives you a cushion before 4:30. After coffee, drive toward Nampa or Meridian rather than all the way downtown unless you need a Boise dinner that night. Twin Falls to Nampa/Meridian is about two hours in normal conditions.
Should I use one Boise-area hotel or split it?

Three workable areas:

Twin Falls Monday: least night driving, but it creates a very early Tuesday to Nampa.

Nampa/Meridian Monday: best balance for Tuesday breakfast, easier parking, lots of practical hotels and food nearby.

Downtown Boise Tuesday: best for the evening meetup and dinner, but parking may cost extra.

I would not make downtown Boise your Monday-night base unless you’re okay arriving late and then backtracking to Nampa in the morning.
I’d rather not have a 5 a.m. start Tuesday. Easy meals matter on this one too.

Then I’d plan to drive and stay Monday in Nampa or Meridian. Look for a refundable hotel with breakfast or at least coffee next door, free parking if possible, and quick access to I-84. For Tuesday night, decide after the Boise end time is firm: downtown if the meetup runs late, Meridian if you want cheaper parking and a simpler checkout.
What are the road and parking risks?

Road: check Idaho 511 the day before and Monday morning, especially I-84 construction pockets and wind advisories. Add 30 to 45 minutes to the SLC-Twin Falls leg. Parking: Twin Falls is usually easier, but confirm with the venue. Downtown Boise is the one to plan for—garage cost, validation, or a hotel self-park fee.
Give me the meal backups so I’m not improvising.

Monday: eat before Twin Falls or pick up something immediately after coffee, then drive to Nampa/Meridian. Tuesday: use the breakfast event as the main morning plan but have hotel coffee as backup. Before the Boise meetup, do an early dinner downtown if there’s a gap; if not, keep a snack in the car and choose a late dinner within walking distance of the venue or hotel. Preliminary call: drive, Monday night Nampa/Meridian, Tuesday night still dependent on the final Boise end time.

messages.content: Idaho updates before I book: Nampa breakfast now wants me there at 7:15 Tuesday, Boise meetup may end closer to 8:45, and Twin Falls confirmed easy lot parking. The best breakfast hotel is refundable but farther from downtown. Downtown is better for dinner but paid parking.
That later Boise end time changes the return question. Is a Tuesday-night drive back to Salt Lake still seriously on the table, or can we treat Wednesday morning as acceptable if the case is strong?
Finance would prefer one hotel night, but I can justify a second if driving home that late is a bad idea. I need the ranking.

Ranked:

1. Two nights, split areas: Monday Nampa/Meridian, Tuesday downtown Boise. Best for the 7:15 breakfast and the late downtown finish. Costs more and adds one hotel move.

2. Two nights at the Nampa/Meridian breakfast hotel. Cheapest comfortable version, free/easier parking, good Wednesday breakfast. Downside: 20 to 30 minutes back after the Boise event.

3. One night only, then drive home Tuesday. I would avoid this. After an 8:45 finish, you’re likely reaching Salt Lake around 2:30 or later, before weather or fatigue.
How bad is the downtown parking difference?

Probably not trip-changing. Meridian/Nampa may be free. Downtown Boise might be roughly $15 to $25 for self-parking, sometimes more if valet is the only option. For one Tuesday night, the parking premium is easier to justify than a five-hour late drive. Just make sure the hotel parking receipt is itemized.
If I book now, which overnight area would you actually choose?

I’d book Monday in Nampa/Meridian and Tuesday downtown Boise. The earlier Nampa arrival makes Monday location matter, and the 8:45 downtown finish makes Tuesday location matter. This keeps both event days clean instead of forcing one hotel to be mediocre for everything.
What if I keep both nights at the Meridian breakfast hotel to avoid moving?

That’s the reasonable fallback. It works if the hotel is close to I-84, parking is free, and you eat before the Boise meetup or plan a simple late snack afterward. I’d choose it over driving home Tuesday, but below the split plan because it adds that late post-event drive back to Meridian.
Okay, split plan. Give me Tuesday timing and meals.

Tuesday: leave the Meridian/Nampa hotel by 6:45 for the 7:15 breakfast. Keep luggage in the car after checkout. After the breakfast, do any Nampa follow-up, then head toward Boise midday and park/check in downtown when the room is available. Eat an early dinner near the venue if you have a gap before 6:30. If not, pick a downtown late-dinner option within a short walk after the meetup.
And Wednesday morning back to Salt Lake?

Leave Boise after breakfast, ideally 8:00 to 8:30. Fuel before getting fully on the road, check Idaho 511 before checkout, and plan one stop around the Burley/Twin Falls or Pocatello stretch depending on traffic. You should be back in Salt Lake early to midafternoon without the Tuesday-night fatigue problem. Book both rooms refundable if the rates allow.

Downtown Boise may have a nightly garage/self-park charge, so make sure it appears on the hotel folio instead of as a separate mystery charge. Save both hotel confirmations, final folios, fuel receipts, and a mileage log with odometer start/end.
And the Monday-to-Wednesday timing? Also how do I keep boxes secure between Nampa and Boise?

Monday: leave Salt Lake after the morning handoff, aim for Twin Falls early afternoon, then Meridian by early evening. Tuesday: check out before the counselor breakfast, keep personal luggage covered in the trunk, and take only the folder/bin you need into each stop. After the afternoon Boise stop, check into the downtown hotel before the 6:30 meetup and move extra materials to the room. Wednesday: breakfast, checkout around 8:15, fuel, check Idaho 511, then head back with one stop around Twin Falls/Burley or Pocatello.
Give me meal backups too, so I’m not grabbing vending-machine dinner.

Final trip note: book Meridian Monday refundable with parking included; book downtown Boise Tuesday refundable, breakfast verified, parking charge shown clearly. Meals: Monday eat before Twin Falls or pick up dinner near the Meridian hotel. Tuesday use the counselor breakfast, keep a snack and water in the car, and either do a 4:45 early dinner downtown or a late dinner within walking distance after 8:45. Wednesday use hotel breakfast and plan a road lunch stop. Keep recruitment boxes out of sight, transfer extras to the room before the evening event, and put all mileage, parking, fuel, and hotel folios in one receipt folder.

messages.content: Switching gears to family travel. My niece’s graduation is near Sacramento in late May. It’s me, Marco, and Sofia. We can leave after school and work Friday, ceremony Saturday afternoon, relatives’ brunch Sunday, and come home Monday. Is flying worth it or should we just drive?

For three people, driving will be cheaper, but late-May weekend traffic makes it a long push. Flying into Sacramento with a rental car is cleaner if the ceremony timing matters. Before I narrow it: what part of Sacramento is the ceremony in, where are relatives based, and what is the earliest realistic Friday departure?

Ceremony is by Sac State. Relatives are mostly Carmichael and Fair Oaks. Sofia is out around 3:15 and Marco can be home by 4. We need a real two-queen room, not a sofa-bed setup, and breakfast at the hotel would help.

Then I’d treat Friday evening flying as the front-runner if the fare is reasonable. Quick comparison: drive Friday after 4 means arriving well after midnight, and Monday is another 9.5 to 11 hours with holiday traffic. Friday nonstop SLC to SMF around 6:15 gets you in around 7 local, rental car by about 7:45. A later one-stop is cheaper sometimes but puts you at the hotel close to 11. Saturday morning nonstop works for the ceremony but cuts into family time.
Can you shortlist hotel areas? I don’t know Sacramento well enough to tell if airport hotels are a bad idea.

I’d skip the airport unless the price is much better. Best areas for this trip: Cal Expo/Arden is closest to Sac State and has easy restaurant access, but availability can be tighter. Rancho Cordova is practical for Fair Oaks/Carmichael, usually easier parking, and still manageable to Sac State. Roseville is comfortable with lots of restaurants, but it adds more driving before and after the ceremony.
What would you hold while my sister firms up the brunch timing?

Hold a refundable two-queen room first. Option 1: Hampton Inn & Suites Sacramento-Cal Expo/Arden, if two queens are available and breakfast is listed. Option 2: Hyatt Place or Hampton in Rancho Cordova, only if the room description clearly says two queen beds. I would not hold a prepaid closest-in room yet; family schedules are still moving.
And flights? I’m okay paying more than the drive if it keeps us from being wrecked all weekend.

Flight plan to watch: Friday evening nonstop SLC-SMF, then Monday afternoon return. A Saturday morning nonstop is the backup if school timing shifts. I’d avoid the Friday one-stop unless it saves a lot, because the connection plus late car pickup is exactly where the weekend starts feeling messy.
Monday return should not be late. Work and school Tuesday are already going to be painful.

Then aim for a Monday early-afternoon return, roughly 1:30 to 2:30 out of SMF. That leaves time to check out, return the car, and get home before evening. If that fare spikes, the next acceptable option is early evening, but I’d avoid anything that lands close to bedtime.
Okay, no booking yet. Give me the practical shortlist for tonight.

Shortlist: 1) Preferred travel plan: fly Friday evening nonstop SLC to SMF, rent a car, return Monday early afternoon. 2) Backup travel plan: Saturday morning nonstop if Friday timing gets squeezed. 3) Hotel hold: refundable two-queen with breakfast in Cal Expo/Arden if available. 4) Backup hotel hold: refundable two-queen in Rancho Cordova, with nearby dinner options and easy parking. I’d hold the hotel tonight and wait on flights only until Sofia’s Friday release time is confirmed.

messages.content: Update on Sacramento: Sofia’s exam release moved later, closer to 4:20. The affordable Friday option I’m seeing now connects and lands around midnight. Saturday has a Delta nonstop in the morning, but we’d miss part of the family lunch. The closest hotels are now prepaid. Help me make the call?

This is an arrival-reliability trade-off. I’d be very cautious with a Friday connection that lands near midnight: one delay means a miserable car pickup and a very short night. Saturday nonstop is less convenient socially, but it is much safer for the ceremony. What time is the Saturday lunch and when do you need to be at the venue?
Lunch is 11:30 in Carmichael. Ceremony check-in is 1:30 and it starts at 2. The Saturday nonstop lands at 9:50 if it stays on time.

That works, especially if you use carry-ons. Land 9:50, off the plane around 10:10, rental car by 10:35 or 10:45, Carmichael around 11:15 to 11:35. If you check a bag, assume 20 more minutes and you may miss the first part of lunch, but you still protect the ceremony.
Marco is asking if driving Friday night or early Saturday is still smarter.

I wouldn’t. Friday after a 4:20 release puts you into Sacramento in the middle of the night, and holiday traffic could make it worse. Saturday pre-dawn driving risks arriving right at ceremony check-in with no recovery margin. The Saturday nonstop is the better compromise.
Okay, fly. Hotel choices now: refundable Rancho Cordova with two queens and breakfast, refundable Roseville with two queens and breakfast, or prepaid Cal Expo. Which one?

Take Rancho Cordova refundable. It keeps you closer to Carmichael/Fair Oaks and still reasonable to Sac State. Roseville is fine but adds more cross-town time, and prepaid Cal Expo is not worth it with family plans still shifting. Check that the room says two queen beds, not queen plus sofa.
Rental car size? We’ll have garment bags and probably carry-ons.

Book an intermediate SUV or midsize SUV if the price difference is modest. Pickup Saturday around 10:30 at SMF and return Monday around 12:15 for an early-afternoon flight. One named driver is enough unless Marco truly expects to drive; adding a second driver can raise the cost.
Use the Saturday nonstop and Monday afternoon return. What seat and receipt details should I pay attention to?

Avoid basic economy if you want assigned seats together. Choose one side of a row, like A-B-C, so you have a window and stay together. Save the airline receipt, rental confirmation, hotel confirmation, and final hotel folio. For the hotel, confirm cancellation deadline, parking cost if any, breakfast hours, and the exact bedding before you submit.
Should I hold the Friday connection until tonight just in case my sister moves lunch later?

I wouldn’t hold it unless it is truly refundable without a fee. Final plan: book the Saturday morning Delta nonstop SLC-SMF, Monday early-afternoon return, intermediate SUV, and refundable Rancho Cordova two-queen room with breakfast. Tell your sister you’ll arrive late morning and may slide into lunch a few minutes late, but the ceremony timing is protected.

Before you pay, one seat question: for the four of you, is the priority all sitting together, or would you split into window pairs if that is the only way?
Together first. If there are two window-and-middle pairs near each other, grab those. I do not want one kid stuck across the plane.

Good. Choose two pairs in adjacent rows if possible, with an adult in each pair. If the map cannot keep all four together, do not pay extra for scattered window seats; keep the group together and check again 24 hours before departure.
Hotel option is the refundable Rancho Cordova two-queen room. It includes breakfast and parking, cancellation is Thursday by 6 pm, and it is farther from the ceremony than I wanted.

I would book that one. The distance is the acceptable trade-off: you get two queen beds, breakfast, free parking, and flexibility. For dinner, plan on casual food near the hotel Saturday night rather than driving back toward the ceremony area after a travel day.
Car-wise, intermediate SUV? We will have four carry-ons, a garment bag, and probably Sofia's backpack. Also, graduation clothes in carry-ons?

Intermediate or midsize SUV is enough. Put the garment bag and one ceremony outfit per person in carry-ons; do not let those ride in checked luggage. Pick up the car right after landing, and assume 30 to 45 minutes from touchdown to leaving the rental lot.
We will miss at least the first part of my sister's Saturday lunch. Can you give me the simple timeline and receipt notes?

Timeline: Saturday land late morning, pick up the SUV, text your sister from the car, and join lunch when you can. Keep snacks handy. Saturday evening: easy dinner near the Rancho Cordova hotel. Sunday: hotel breakfast, ceremony and brunch, then family time without moving hotels. Monday: breakfast, check out, return the car with a fuel receipt, and fly home early afternoon. Save flight confirmations, hotel folio, rental agreement, gas receipt, and any cancellation emails.
