messages.content: Next trip: late-June admissions institute in Kansas City. Registration opens Sunday evening 5 to 7, workshops are Monday and Tuesday, and there is an optional campus-partner breakfast Wednesday morning before flights home. I need flight and hotel options from SLC, preferably not a stressful connection.
Got it. Two quick things before I narrow it: is the hotel cap measured all-in with taxes and parking, and are you planning to rent a car or rely on walking and rideshare?

Cap is effectively all-in for reimbursement. The conference hotel looks okay at the base rate, but with taxes and parking it goes over. I do not need a car if the hotel is close enough. Included breakfast would help because the Monday and Tuesday mornings start early.

For Sunday outbound, I would compare three windows: 1) Morning departure: safest for registration, but eats most of Sunday. 2) Midday or early-afternoon with one connection: likely best balance if the layover is comfortable and arrival is around dinner time. 3) Later afternoon or evening: cheapest sometimes, but it makes 5 to 7 registration too tight or impossible.
That is exactly the worry. If I miss registration, I am not sure they will make Monday morning easy. Delta is fine if it is comparable, but I care more about not sprinting through a connection.

Then treat the later arrival as a backup only. Look for one connection with at least about an hour between flights, not a 35-minute airport dash. A Delta route through Minneapolis or another orderly hub is worth considering if the price is close; if another carrier gives a calmer connection and similar arrival, take the calmer itinerary.
What about coming home Wednesday? The breakfast is optional, but it may be useful.

Return trade-off: a late-morning or midday flight works only if you skip most of breakfast or leave immediately after it, then move fast on checkout and rideshare. A mid- or late-afternoon flight lets you attend breakfast, answer email for an hour, and get to the airport without a tight handoff. I would avoid anything before noon unless the agenda changes.
Hotel options are the bigger mess. The conference hotel is adjacent to sessions and has restaurants, but it is over cap once parking is in. What nearby options should I hold?

Shortlist: A) Conference hotel: easiest walk and on-site food, but reimbursement risk and parking pushes it over. B) Nearby business hotel within a short walk or 5-minute rideshare: best practical choice if it includes weekday breakfast and free or cheaper parking. C) Cheaper hotel farther out: may meet cap, but you will spend the savings on rideshares and lose convenience after evening events.
I am okay with a short walk in daylight, but I do not want to be hunting for dinner after sessions. It is just me, so a queen room is fine.

Then hold the nearby business hotel if it is refundable. Check three items before clicking: breakfast hours on Monday and Tuesday, whether there are casual dinner spots within a block or two, and the exact cancellation deadline in local time. A queen room is fine; do not pay extra for the conference block unless reimbursement approves the overage.
Should I hold flights now too, or wait for the agenda packet next week?

I would hold the hotel tonight because refundable rooms under cap can disappear. For flights, wait if fares are stable, but do not wait on the Sunday midday window if there is a 24-hour cancellation option and the price is reasonable. The registration timing makes schedule reliability more important than saving a small amount.
Give me the order of operations so I do not overthink it.

Do this: 1) Hold the refundable nearby business hotel under the cap, with breakfast verified. 2) Put the conference hotel on the waitlist only if it does not require a deposit or if reimbursement pre-approval is likely. 3) Watch Sunday midday or early-afternoon one-connection flights that arrive before registration closes; avoid short layovers. 4) For Wednesday, favor mid- or late-afternoon unless the partner breakfast gets canceled. 5) Keep screenshots of the hotel rate, taxes, parking, cancellation deadline, and the conference hotel over-cap comparison for reimbursement.

Cancellation is Sunday before arrival at 6 pm hotel local time. Breakfast is listed 6:30 to 9 weekdays. Sessions start at 8:30.
That works. Breakfast at 6:30 gives you enough margin to eat, return to the room, and leave around 8:05 or 8:10. If there is a first-day check-in line, leave a few minutes earlier Monday.

Flights: Sunday early-afternoon Delta with one connection gets me into Kansas City around 6:20. Connection is 78 minutes. Return choices are 12:10 Wednesday or 4:45 Wednesday. The 12:10 is cheaper by about $60.

Take the 4:45 return unless you need to be home earlier. The 12:10 makes the optional breakfast, checkout, and airport ride feel compressed. $60 is not enough savings to create that kind of morning squeeze.
Agreed. No one is expecting me back Wednesday afternoon. And yes, if the seat map has window seats, take those; closer to the front only if it does not mean a middle.

Flight plan: Sunday early-afternoon Delta, one connection with the 78-minute buffer; Wednesday 4:45 return. Select window seats where available, and avoid middle seats even if they are closer to the front. If a window opens later, adjust during check-in.
Do I need a rental car because of the dinner move south?

No, not for one off-site dinner. Use rideshare unless the institute offers a shuttle. A rental adds parking, reimbursement clutter, and downtown driving for very little benefit. For Monday dinner, use something walkable near the hotel or the conference area.
What should I put in the booking notes for receipts and cancellation?

Booking notes: hotel is refundable queen room under cap; cancellation deadline Sunday 6 pm local time; breakfast included 6:30 to 9 on weekdays; save folio with taxes separated. Flights: save receipt, itinerary, seat selections, and any baggage fee receipt if applicable. Ground: rideshare receipts for airport transfers and Tuesday dinner. Also keep the conference hotel waitlist and over-cap screenshot in case finance asks why you booked off-block.
Can you give me the final itinerary summary in one chunk?

Final Kansas City plan: fly from SLC Sunday early afternoon on the one-connection Delta itinerary, arriving around 6:20 pm, with window seats requested where available. Stay at the nearby refundable business hotel in a queen room under the reimbursement cap; use included weekday breakfast before Monday and Tuesday sessions. Skip the conference hotel waitlist unless a compliant room opens. Tuesday dinner: rideshare to the restaurant south of the meeting hotel. Wednesday: attend the partner breakfast if useful, check out calmly, work a bit if needed, then take the 4:45 pm return. Save hotel, flight, rideshare, and rate-comparison receipts.

Badge pickup is 7:30 to 8:30. The hotel can hold packages; they just will not promise a room before standard check-in. Monday badge pickup reopens at 7:30, but first session is 8:30.

If the app says landing 7:10 while I am in the connection airport, do I still try for Sunday badge pickup?

Airport to hotel is rideshare, right? I have not used the new MCI setup.

Rideshare is fine for MCI. Use the designated app pickup at the terminal and keep the taxi stand as backup if surge looks silly. A rental on Sunday adds garage, return, and parking friction for very little value.
What about Tuesday dinner in the rain? The restaurant is about 15 minutes south. I hate the idea of getting stranded, but a rental feels excessive.

A short rental is only worth it if the forecast turns into severe-weather alerts or you add multiple errands. messages.content: I have the first draft of an August recruitment loop and need to make it coherent before I ask the office to approve it. Monday afternoon high-school visit in Fort Collins, Tuesday counselor breakfast in Boulder, Tuesday evening fair in Denver, Wednesday morning visit in Colorado Springs, and Thursday noon transfer-center meeting in Pueblo. Starting from Salt Lake City. Can you compare drive versus fly and rent versus one-way routing?

Yes. Before I rank them, what are the exact event times, how much recruitment material are you moving, and are you free to leave Sunday afternoon or only Monday morning? Those affect the arrival buffer a lot.

Fort Collins is 2:15 to 3:00 Monday. Boulder breakfast 7:30 to 8:30 Tuesday. Denver fair 6:00 to 8:30 Tuesday. Colorado Springs visit 9:30 Wednesday. Pueblo meeting noon to 1:00 Thursday. I will have a carry-on and one 25-pound rolling display bag. I can leave Sunday afternoon if needed, but I would rather not lose the whole Sunday.

Quick comparison: fly into Denver and rent is the cleanest if you can keep Monday unhurried; driving your own car is simplest for materials but costs you a long SLC-to-Colorado day on each end; a one-way plan only helps if you finish near Colorado Springs and can avoid the drive back to Denver. For reliability, I would not use a Monday flight that lands after about 10:30. That still gives rental pickup, the drive north, lunch, and a cushion before Fort Collins.
I would rather avoid a dawn flight, but I do not want the Fort Collins visit to start with me already tense.

Then the two practical versions are Sunday late-afternoon flight into Denver, or a Monday morning flight that lands by 10:30. Sunday costs one more hotel night but makes Monday calm. Monday saves the night, but a delay, rental line, or traffic north can eat the whole buffer. A noon Denver arrival is too tight for a 2:15 Fort Collins visit.
The office might approve Sunday night if it prevents a same-day-arrival problem. What would the Sunday-in, Thursday-home timeline look like?

Sunday: fly SLC to Denver late afternoon or early evening, pick up the rental, sleep Fort Collins or Loveland. Monday: do the Fort Collins visit, then drive to Boulder or a nearby U.S. 36 area hotel. Tuesday: Boulder breakfast, work/admin block, then Denver Tech Center area for the evening fair. Wednesday: drive to Colorado Springs for the morning visit, then decide whether to sleep Colorado Springs or Pueblo. Thursday: Pueblo at noon, then either COS for a later afternoon flight or DEN for an evening flight.
The Denver fair is at a school near the Tech Center. I do not need downtown. I do need an easy dinner after the fair.

That points to DTC, Greenwood Village, or maybe Lone Tree for Tuesday night. You should get easier parking than downtown, lots of chain-hotel options, and restaurants still open after an 8:30 fair. I would not pay downtown rates for this loop.
Where should Monday night be: Boulder proper, Longmont, or just stay in Fort Collins?

Fort Collins is too far for a 7:30 Boulder breakfast. Longmont is workable if you want easier parking and rates, but it adds a morning drive. Boulder proper is the calmest if the breakfast is central or on campus, though it may cost more. Louisville or Superior can be a middle ground if Boulder rates are high.
The Boulder breakfast is near Pearl Street. Longmont sounds a little risky for that early.

For Pearl Street at 7:30, I would lean Boulder if the rate is acceptable. If Boulder is overpriced, use Louisville or Superior rather than Longmont; you stay on the right side of the commute and still avoid some Boulder parking pain. Since breakfast is part of the event, hotel breakfast that morning matters less.
Do I need to ship materials, or can I fly with them?

If the display bag is checked-size, I would avoid making it the only copy of your materials. Put essentials in your carry-on: visit folder, name tags, QR sheet, and a small brochure stack. Ship a non-critical box to the first hotel or Fort Collins host, and include a return label if you can.
It is the rolling display bag, technically checked size. I can ship a small box to the first hotel.

Then fly-and-rent still works. Ask the Sunday hotel to accept packages under your name and arrival date, and confirm any handling fee. Keep Monday-critical items with you. If the office wants the full fair kit every day, driving becomes more attractive, but for one shipped box plus carry-on essentials, flying is fine.
What is the clean hotel sequence for the approval note?

Sunday: Fort Collins or Loveland. Monday: Boulder, or Louisville/Superior if Boulder is too expensive. Tuesday: DTC or Greenwood Village. Wednesday: Colorado Springs north if you want better dinner choices and a short drive after the school visit; Pueblo if you want the easiest Thursday morning. With a noon Pueblo meeting, Colorado Springs still works.
If we finish Pueblo around 1:00, which airport routing should I ask them to price?

Ask for two priced versions. Primary: fly SLC to DEN Sunday late afternoon or early evening, rent at DEN, return the car at DEN Thursday, and fly home after 6:30 pm. Secondary: same inbound, but drop the car at COS and fly home after about 4:00 pm if the fare plus one-way rental fee is not much higher. Driving is the backup if materials get heavier. In the approval note, flag package acceptance at the Sunday hotel, parking costs in Boulder and DTC, and meals: event breakfast Tuesday, easy DTC dinner Tuesday, and a simple Wednesday dinner in Colorado Springs or Pueblo.

Pueblo is dropped for this round. Thursday coffee is 8:30 to 9:15 near Union Station. I would like to be home Thursday afternoon, not late evening.

Would you still fly in Sunday night, or is Monday morning okay now?

Monday morning is okay if the flight lands at DEN by 10:30 and you are not waiting on a checked display bag. Fort Collins at 2:15 still needs a cushion for rental pickup and the drive north. Sunday is calmer, but with Pueblo gone and rental prices lower, Monday morning is a defensible approval request.
I will ship materials to the first hotel and carry the visit folder with me. Let's plan on Monday morning if there is a flight that lands before 10:30.

Then use this sequence: Monday fly SLC to DEN, pick up the rental, Fort Collins visit, then sleep Boulder or Louisville/Superior. Tuesday Boulder breakfast, then the Denver Tech Center fair, and sleep DTC or Greenwood Village. Wednesday keep that Denver-area hotel for a second night, drive to Colorado Springs for the afternoon visit, and come back after.
Same Denver hotel Tuesday and Wednesday? I was wondering if moving after Colorado Springs would be smarter.

Stay put Tuesday and Wednesday. Moving after the Colorado Springs visit creates a late check-in and another parking question. DTC or Greenwood Village keeps Tuesday easy and usually has restaurants nearby. For Thursday, leave around 7:30 for Union Station, pay for one downtown garage, then head to DEN after the coffee.
How should I handle the Boulder cancellation issue versus breakfast?

Prioritize cancellation while the hosts are still shifting things. Since Tuesday breakfast is the counselor event, an included hotel breakfast Monday night is nice but not worth a strict cancellation penalty. If Boulder proper has a reasonable cancellable rate, take it. If not, Louisville or Superior with easy parking is the safer approval choice.
What exactly should I send for sign-off?

Send this: Monday morning SLC-DEN flight landing before 10:30, round-trip rental from DEN, materials shipped to the first hotel, Fort Collins visit at 2:15, Monday night in Boulder or Louisville/Superior on a cancellable rate. Tuesday: Boulder counselor breakfast, then DTC fair, with Tuesday and Wednesday nights at one DTC/Greenwood Village hotel that has reasonable parking and nearby dinner. Wednesday: drive to Colorado Springs for the afternoon visit and return to Denver after. Thursday: Union Station coffee 8:30 to 9:15, return the rental at DEN, and fly home after about 12:30 or 1:00. Note the downtown hotel was avoided because parking would erase the convenience.

Yes, pay-later. Nothing huge unless they substitute it. I need to fit the box out of sight if possible.

Hotel shortlist: Boulder base is Boulder Garden Inn, queen non-smoking, breakfast 6:30-9:30, parking $12/night, cancel by Thu Aug 15 at 6 pm, about $219. Louisville/Superior Suites has a queen studio, breakfast 6:00-9:00, free parking, cancel by Sat Aug 17, about $189, but it is 15-20 minutes farther from the Tuesday breakfast. South Denver: Hampton Greenwood Village, queen, breakfast 6:30-9:30, parking $8/night, cancel by Tue Aug 20, restaurants next door. Residence Inn DTC is roomier but parking is $15.
Take the Boulder Garden Inn even with the Aug 15 cancellation, as long as it is not prepaid. For south Denver, Hampton sounds easier after the fair.

That works. I’d book Boulder Garden Inn for Sun/Mon, cancellable but not prepaid, queen non-smoking; parking budget $24. Hampton Greenwood Village for Tue/Wed, queen non-smoking; parking budget $16. Both list breakfast early enough for the school-day departures, but I’d screenshot the hours with the reservations.
Can you give me the Sunday-through-Thursday driving timeline and the dinner plan? Keep dinners low-effort.

Timeline: Sunday land 4:10, car by 4:45, drive to Boulder, check in around 5:45; dinner near the hotel or Pearl Street, no reservation needed. Monday keep the Boulder base for the Fort Collins visit and any north-side stops; casual dinner in Boulder. Tuesday breakfast in Boulder, then leave for south Denver late morning, check into Hampton before the afternoon prep block; dinner near the hotel. Wednesday leave by 10:30 for Colorado Springs, visit early afternoon, drive back toward downtown Denver for fair load-in, then return to Greenwood Village after the fair. Thursday leave hotel about 7:00 for the Union Station coffee, return car at DEN around 12:30, fly 2:20.

messages.content: The Denver fair load-in email finally arrived and it is annoying. For Wednesday they want us at the 14th Street dock at 4:15, no unattended carts, and the garage they recommend is not connected. Also the Union Station coffee moved to 8:00 Thursday. Fair is 5:30 to 7:30. I should be able to leave Colorado Springs by 2:30 unless the counselor runs long. Hotel checkout is noon and breakfast starts at 6:30.

Keep the hotel. Wednesday: leave Colorado Springs by 2:35, aim for the downtown garage by 4:00, and use the paid garage over street parking so you are not circling with boxes. Take the laptop and purse into the fair; leave only sealed brochure boxes under the cargo cover or a blanket.

Drive. With luggage and leftover materials, rideshare adds handoff risk and may not save time. Leave Greenwood Village at 6:45, park in a Union Station-area garage by 7:40, and walk in with only the coffee folder and laptop.
Should I check out before the coffee, then?
Yes. Check out before you leave, ask the desk for a grab-and-go item if breakfast is not fully set, and load the car under the hotel canopy. Do not rearrange bags once you are downtown.
Dinner after the fair: I do not want to wander downtown with the banner.

Then make dinner a hotel-area plan. After the fair, load out, go straight back to Greenwood Village, and eat at one of the restaurants next to the Hampton or place a mobile order before leaving the garage. Budget parking as: hotel $16 total, downtown fair garage about $25-35, Union Station garage about $12-20. The only real timing risk is Colorado Springs running late; if you are not on I-25 by 2:45, call the fair contact and ask whether load-in can be held at the registration table.

messages.content: Colorado is wrapped up and I’m starting the mid-September Pacific Northwest loop. Draft schedule is Sep 15-19: Monday 7:30 counselor breakfast in Vancouver, WA, Monday evening Portland fair, Tuesday school visits around Salem, Wednesday 1:00-4:00 transfer fair in Eugene, and Thursday 10:30 counselor coffee near Corvallis. I need a route comparison before I ask for approval: fly-and-rent, open-jaw, or drive the whole thing from Salt Lake.

I can rank those. A few details will affect whether the open-jaw is worth it: how much material are you taking, are you okay flying out Sunday afternoon, do you need to be home Thursday night, and will the office allow a one-way rental if the fee is reasonable?

Two boxes of brochures plus the pop-up banner. I can ship one box to the first hotel, but not the banner. Sunday afternoon is fine. I’d like to be home Thursday night. A one-way rental is okay if it is not ridiculous.

First pass: 1) Fly SLC-PDX Sunday, rent, return from EUG Thursday: least backtracking, best if the EUG return has one comfortable connection; watch the one-way car fee and smaller-airport disruption risk. 2) Fly SLC-PDX round trip, rent and return at PDX: simplest flights and rental, likely cheaper, but adds the Corvallis-to-PDX drive Thursday after coffee. 3) Drive SLC-Vancouver-Salem-Eugene-Corvallis-SLC: maximum material control and no flight risk, but two very long travel days and probably more fatigue than savings. My practical primary would be to price 1 and 2 side by side; keep 3 as backup only if shipping or fares fail.
I’m not excited about a tiny Eugene connection. If the return from Eugene has one short layover that is 70 minutes or more, fine. If it is a 40-minute scramble, I would rather drive back to Portland.

Good boundary. Approval version: open-jaw wins only if the Eugene return has one connection with about 70-75 minutes or better and gets you to SLC Thursday evening. If the connection is tighter, choose the Portland round trip even though it adds the drive. The full-drive plan should not be the requested plan unless the material load grows.
Sketch the actual Sunday-to-Thursday routing for the two flight versions.

Open-jaw route: Sunday fly SLC-PDX, pick up car, sleep Vancouver or north Portland. Monday breakfast in Vancouver, Portland fair, then drive to Salem for the night. Tuesday Salem visits, then drive to Eugene. Wednesday Eugene fair, then sleep Corvallis if the Thursday coffee is there and the Eugene flight is late enough; otherwise stay Eugene. Thursday Corvallis coffee, drive to EUG, drop car, fly home. Push to Eugene Tuesday night. Because Salem starts early, you should be done early enough to drive south before dinner. Staying in Eugene Tuesday gives you a calmer Wednesday, lets you check the fair location ahead of time, and avoids a morning I-5 drive with materials in the car.

messages.content: Back from the Oregon loop and I already have the next puzzle. Can you help me shape an early October North Texas route before I send it for approval? Probably five boxes plus the banner tube if I don't ship. Hotel cap is $185 before tax unless there's a reason. Airfare can be higher if it saves real staff time. Initial read: open-jaw is the plan to defend. Option 1, SLC to Dallas and Austin back to SLC, follows the route south and avoids a Thursday backtrack; the trade-offs are possible higher airfare, a one-way rental fee, and a materials plan. Option 2, Dallas round trip, may price cleaner and avoids a car drop fee, but Round Rock back to DFW is about 3 to 3.5 hours before traffic, so any late meeting or I-35 slowdown makes the return less reliable. Option 3, driving from Salt Lake, solves materials but costs multiple travel days and fatigue; I would only use it if flying plus shipping becomes impossible.
Can you sketch the overnight areas? I can handle three hotels if it actually helps, but I don't want to make a mess.

I would use three hotel areas. Sunday and Monday: Plano, Richardson, or Addison, not downtown Dallas. That protects the Plano breakfast and gives better odds of free parking and breakfast under the cap. Tuesday: either Fort Worth south/Arlington if the visits run late, or Waco if you can leave Fort Worth by mid-afternoon. Wednesday: Round Rock or Georgetown after the Waco fair if the fair really ends around 5. That puts you close to Thursday's meeting and Austin airport.

Also choose an SUV or at least a vehicle with covered cargo space so the boxes are not visible while you are at dinner or between visits.

It is a little easier for central Dallas, while DFW usually has stronger SLC nonstop options and is fine for Plano/Richardson. I would compare both Dallas airports, but I would not give up a good DFW Sunday afternoon nonstop for a weaker Love Field connection.
For materials, I don't know if I should check, ship, or drive.

I would not drive from Salt Lake just for five boxes. Best plan: ship the heavy brochures to the first confirmed receiving point, ideally the Monday fair or the first hotel if they will accept packages without a big handling fee. Carry the scanner, tablecloth, small counselor packets, and anything irreplaceable. If you must fly with the banner tube, treat it like a checked item and keep the receipt. After Dallas, keep remaining materials in the SUV for Waco and Round Rock.
How bad is the Dallas round trip if we need cheaper airfare?

It is not impossible, but it is the weaker operational plan. After a late-morning Round Rock meeting, you would drive north to DFW, refuel, return the car, and clear security before an evening flight. That is a long final day and leaves little buffer if the meeting runs over or I-35 is slow. I would only switch to Dallas round trip if Austin return pricing is dramatically worse or if the Austin options require multiple stops, long layovers, or a very late Salt Lake arrival.
Breakfast and dinner access matter because the days are going to be weird. Flag that in the approval note.

For hotel areas, I would write it this way: North Dallas/Plano-Richardson for Sunday and Monday because it supports the Plano breakfast, has free-parking hotels under cap, and still works for the Dallas fair with pre-reserved event parking. Round Rock/Georgetown Wednesday because it protects Thursday morning and has easier dinner options than arriving late from Waco on Thursday morning.

A late nonstop is a backup if the price is reasonable, but it creates a long airport wait or a late night. I would switch back to Dallas only if Austin is several hundred dollars higher after the one-way car fee, or if the only Austin options are unreliable connections. For refundable room holds once dates are firm, start with Plano/Richardson for Sunday/Monday, Waco for Tuesday, and Round Rock/Georgetown for Wednesday.

Arizona Athletic Grounds in east Mesa. Realistically we can leave our house at 3:30 Friday. If we drive, it would be after school too. First match time is not posted yet, but the coach warned us to plan for early.

With a 3:30 Friday start, flying is much kinder to Saturday. Driving is roughly 10.5 to 11.5 hours before longer stops, so you would be arriving very late or splitting the drive and losing Friday night anyway. A late-afternoon SLC-PHX flight gets you to a rental car and east Mesa hotel around dinner or shortly after.
What about just sending one parent with her? I am trying not to make this a giant production.

That is the lowest-cost flight version, but it has trade-offs: one parent handles the gear, meals, possible bracket changes, and any late-night return alone. For an early Saturday start, I would rank it: fly all three if fares are reasonable, fly one parent plus athlete if cost is the deciding factor, drive only if flights are unusually high or you can leave much earlier.
The team block says it is about 7 minutes from the venue, $179, but I do not see cancellation terms or breakfast. What other areas should I consider?

Shortlist the areas this way: East Mesa/Gateway area is closest to the venue and easiest for warmups, but dining can be more limited. Gilbert/SanTan Village adds about 15 to 20 minutes and gives better dinner choices. Mesa Riverview/Tempe is better for airport access and food, but it is too far for an early first serve.
We need one room with two queens, parking, and breakfast if possible. I do not want to be hunting for food before a 7 a.m. warmup.

Then I would hold a refundable two-queen backup near East Mesa or Gilbert with breakfast and free parking, even if it is a few minutes farther than the team block. The team hotel is only worth holding if they confirm: cancellable deadline, two queens guaranteed, breakfast status, parking cost, and no resort or event fee.
Can you put the family schedule impact in a quick table?

Plan | Friday impact | Saturday risk | Notes. Fly all three | Leave home about 3:30, catch late-afternoon/early-evening flight, hotel by evening | Low | Best rest, highest cost. Drive all three | Arrive around 2 a.m. or later with stops | High | Cheapest transport, worst for early play. One parent flies with athlete | Similar timing to flying all three | Low to medium | Cheaper, but more solo logistics.
Should I book the team block now while I wait on the game schedule?

Only if you can get the cancellation terms in writing today. Otherwise, hold the refundable backup first. For this weekend I would plan on flying Friday, staying two nights in a two-queen room near East Mesa or Gilbert, using the hotel breakfast as the morning plan, and choosing a Sunday return late enough to survive a bracket run. We can tighten flights once the first match and last possible final are posted.

messages.content: Mesa update: first match is 8:00 Saturday, and the latest Sunday final could start around 4:30 with awards after. The team block now only has nonrefundable rooms. A refundable hotel about 12 minutes farther has two queens, breakfast, and free parking. Help me choose.

Given the 8:00 Saturday start, I would fly rather than drive. I would also skip the nonrefundable team block. The refundable hotel costs a little more in drive time, but it protects you if the bracket shifts or anyone gets sick, and breakfast plus free parking offsets part of the rate difference.
The refundable one is $164, cancelable until Thursday, breakfast starts at 6:00, two queens confirmed. The team block is $149, nonrefundable, and breakfast is not included.

That makes the refundable hotel the better value. For $15 more before taxes, you get cancellation flexibility, confirmed bedding, breakfast, and parking. For Saturday, plan to be downstairs at 6:05, eat quickly or grab items to go, leave by about 6:35, and arrive with cushion for a 7:15ish warmup.
Flights are close. Friday options: 4:25, 5:15, or 6:05 out of Salt Lake. Sunday return options are 7:30 or 9:10. Monday morning is available but ugly for school and work.

I would avoid Monday. For Friday, the 5:15 is the safest balance if school pickup makes 4:25 rushed; the 6:05 is fine but pushes dinner and hotel arrival later. For Sunday, choose 9:10. A 7:30 return is too tight if a 4:30 final runs long, awards happen, and you still need to reach PHX, return the car, and clear security.
The 9:10 return costs about $45 more per person than the 7:30. Still worth it?

For this schedule, yes. The extra $135 buys a real buffer against missing the flight. Missing the 7:30 would likely cost more than that and turn into either a very late rebooking or Monday travel anyway.
Do we need a rental car if the hotel mentions a shuttle?

Yes, I would rent a car. Tournament shuttles are rarely flexible enough for warmups, food runs, and bracket changes. A midsize car should work unless you are carrying extra team gear; free hotel parking makes that easy.
Okay. Book the refundable hotel, Friday 5:15, Sunday 9:10, and a car. Give me the notes for the confirmation email to my spouse.

Confirmation notes: Fly SLC-PHX Friday on the 5:15 option after school/work; return Sunday on the 9:10 option to protect a possible late final and awards. Book the refundable two-queen hotel 12 minutes farther from the venue: $164, cancelable until Thursday, breakfast from 6:00, free parking. Skip the nonrefundable team block because it lacks breakfast and flexibility. Rent a midsize car for airport, venue, and food runs. Saturday plan: breakfast at 6:05, leave hotel 6:35, warmup buffer for the 8:00 match. Sunday: keep bags in the car, choose an easy early dinner near the venue or airport after brackets, and leave for PHX as soon as awards finish. Save flight, hotel, rental, parking, and any tournament-fee receipts.

Friday still works: breakfast at 6:00 Saturday, leave the hotel by 6:35, and you have room for parking and warmup. For seats, check the app now for any pair plus single; if not, ask at the gate and prioritize one parent next to your teen. Sunday is workable if awards finish by about 6:15. If the final starts late or goes long, the 9:10 return gets tight.
Give me a firm airport cutoff so I am not doing math from the bleachers.

Leave the venue by 6:35 at the latest. That gives you the drive to PHX, a fuel stop if needed, rental return, and a reasonable security buffer. Leaving at 6:45 is uncomfortable but maybe survivable; leaving at 7:00 is where I would expect stress.
Would you switch us to Monday morning just to be safe?

I would keep the 9:10 unless Monday morning is painless for school and work. Monday buys calm, but it adds another hotel night and makes everyone miss Monday. The current return is the right compromise as long as you treat 6:35 as the real gym departure time.
Okay, keep it. What exactly should I put in the hotel note?

Use this: Late arrival guaranteed by card; family arriving Friday around 7:30-8:00 PM after flight into PHX. Please hold the two-queen room and note late check-in. Please confirm free parking and breakfast starting at 6:00 AM. Also ask whether there is any issue parking after 8:00 PM and whether the room type is guaranteed, not just requested.

messages.content: Mesa is behind us, and now I have the draft Midwest route. It would be Sunday Nov. 10 through Thursday Nov. 14: Monday 8:00 counselor breakfast in St. Paul, Monday evening fair in Minneapolis, Tuesday school visits around Eau Claire and La Crosse, Wednesday evening transfer fair in Madison, and Thursday late-morning counselor meeting near Milwaukee. I need to tell my director which routing makes sense before I ask for approval.

Got it. Before I rank it, two practical questions: how much recruitment material are you moving, and do you need to be home Thursday night, or could Friday morning be acceptable if the route gets messy?

Two medium brochure boxes, table throw, and the banner. I can check one bag or ship a box. I really need to be home Thursday night if practical. I do not want to chase the cheapest option if it creates a bad Thursday.

Then I would rank the route shapes this way: 1) Fly into Minneapolis-St. Paul and home from Milwaukee: best fit for the actual path, but price the one-way rental fee. 2) Fly round trip MSP: possibly cheaper airfare and rental, but Thursday becomes a long backtrack from Milwaukee to MSP. 3) Fly into MSP and return from Chicago: useful backup if Milwaukee fares are unreasonable, but Chicago traffic and airport transfer time are real risks. 4) Drive the whole trip from Salt Lake City: best for materials control, worst for time, weather exposure, and fatigue.
I was worried the one-way car fee would make the open-jaw version look wasteful.

It may look higher on the rental line, but compare it against the cost of five extra hours Thursday, possible winter driving, fuel, parking, and the risk of missing a return. For approval, I would frame the open-jaw plan as buying schedule reliability, not convenience.
What about Chicago because Milwaukee is not that far from O'Hare?

Chicago is a reasonable backup for the return only. I would not start there because Chicago to St. Paul is too much deadhead driving. Returning from O'Hare or Midway after the Milwaukee meeting could work if flights are much better, but you would need to protect tolls, traffic, rental return, and weather. Milwaukee is cleaner if the fare is not outrageous.
Can you sketch the open-jaw route like I would actually drive it?

Sunday: fly SLC to MSP, pick up the rental, sleep St. Paul/Roseville. Monday: breakfast in St. Paul, keep the car parked or near the hotel midday, fair in Minneapolis that evening, then sleep St. Paul/Roseville or just east of the cities. Tuesday: drive to Eau Claire and La Crosse visits, then sleep La Crosse if the day runs late or Madison if the last visit ends early enough. Wednesday: Madison prep and evening transfer fair, sleep Madison. Thursday: drive to the suburban Milwaukee meeting, return the car at MKE, fly home after lunch.
Would you drive to Eau Claire after the Monday evening fair?

Not unless Tuesday's first appointment forces it. After an evening fair, load-out, and mid-November darkness, that drive is a fatigue risk. I would rather stay on the east side of the Twin Cities and leave early Tuesday with coffee and a clean weather check.
The materials in the rental car worry me a little.

Use a midsize SUV or crossover if reimbursement allows, keep the boxes low and covered, and do not leave the banner or high-value packets visible overnight. Better: ship one brochure box to the St. Paul breakfast site or first hotel, check one box or duffel, and carry the banner with you. Save shipping and baggage receipts either way.
What hotel areas should I look at before I send this?

For Sunday and Monday, look at St. Paul or Roseville first: easier breakfast/fair access, likely parking, and better odds of breakfast included. Woodbury or Hudson helps Tuesday morning but adds Monday evening logistics. For Tuesday/Wednesday, Madison east or near the fair is practical if parking is included and dinner is nearby. For Thursday, only use a Milwaukee-suburb hotel if you decide to move after the Madison fair or if the meeting host adds something Wednesday night.
What flights should I ask them to price? Delta is fine if the timing works, but I care more about not creating a terrible connection.

Ask for SLC to MSP Sunday afternoon or early evening, nonstop if available or one simple connection if not. For Thursday, ask for MKE to SLC after 2:00 PM with no more than one comfortable connection. Also ask them to price ORD or MDW as a backup return and MSP round trip as a comparison, but not as the recommended plan.
Can you give me the approval paragraph? I want to send it before I get pulled into visits.

Send this: Recommended routing is SLC-MSP on Sunday and MKE-SLC on Thursday with a one-way rental car. This follows the event path from St. Paul/Minneapolis to Eau Claire/La Crosse, Madison, and Milwaukee without requiring a Thursday backtrack. Please also price MSP round trip and a Chicago-area return as backups, but those add winter-driving and timing risk. I will look for hotels with breakfast, parking, and nearby dinner options, and I will either ship one materials box ahead or check materials so boxes are not left exposed in the vehicle.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa chose the open-jaw MSP inbound/MKE outbound as the most reliable route, leaned toward St. Paul over Roseville when the small price difference bought easier Monday logistics, kept Madison for the late Wednesday fair, and treated Milwaukee as an optional weather backup rather than the main overnight.

messages.content: Midwest update before I book holds: La Crosse moved earlier Tuesday, Madison confirmed the transfer fair runs until 9:15 Wednesday, and the Milwaukee meeting stayed Thursday at 10:45 in Wauwatosa. I would rank them: 1) MSP inbound and MKE outbound, still the best match. 2) Chicago-area return only if MKE jumps dramatically in price. 3) MSP round trip, acceptable only as a budget fallback. The 2:20 MKE return after a 10:45 Wauwatosa meeting is much calmer than finishing the meeting and then driving back toward Minneapolis.
For Sunday night, is St. Paul worth about $18 more than Roseville?

If the breakfast is in St. Paul and the St. Paul hotel also includes parking and breakfast, yes, the $18 is defensible. Roseville is fine if the room is cleaner or cancellation terms are better, but it adds a morning drive and another chance for traffic before the 8:00 breakfast.
Does the earlier La Crosse visit make Roseville too far for Monday night?

It makes the start early but not impossible. If you keep the St. Paul/Roseville base Monday night, choose the east/southeast side of that area, pack the car after the fair, and plan a very early departure. I would avoid anything west of Minneapolis. If the La Crosse visit is before 10:00 and weather looks bad, consider a refundable midpoint backup, but I would not add that unless the forecast forces it.
I can tolerate the early start. I do not want to add another town unless we have to.

Then the clean overnight sequence is: Sunday St. Paul, Monday St. Paul or Roseville on the east side, Tuesday Madison after the La Crosse/Eau Claire visits, Wednesday Madison again after the late transfer fair, then Thursday morning Madison to Wauwatosa and MKE after the meeting.
What about sleeping near Milwaukee Wednesday so Thursday morning is easier?

That helps Thursday but creates the worse drive at the worse time. Leaving Madison after a 9:15 fair means load-out, dinner or no dinner, then 75-90 minutes in the dark. Staying in Madison gives you a normal checkout and a controlled Thursday drive. I would only hold Milwaukee as a weather backup if it cancels late enough.
The MKE flight is 2:20 to MSP, 88-minute connection, then into SLC around 6:45. The MSP round trip has a 5:05 nonstop home.

Take the MKE option if approval allows it. The 88-minute connection is reasonable, and the airport is close enough after Wauwatosa. The 5:05 MSP nonstop looks nice on paper, but it depends on a long post-meeting drive with no weather or traffic problem. That is the weaker reliability choice.
Which refundable rooms should I hold today?

Hold these first: 1) St. Paul Sunday night, breakfast included, free parking, close to the Monday breakfast. 2) Roseville Monday night only if St. Paul is over cap or the cancellation terms are better; otherwise keep St. Paul both nights to simplify. 3) Madison Tuesday and Wednesday nights, preferably near the fair or on the east side with parking and a restaurant nearby. 4) Optional Milwaukee-area Wednesday backup only if it has same-day or late-Tuesday cancellation. Cancel any backup once the forecast and final host addresses are firm.

Cancellation windows are Saturday for St. Paul, Monday evening for Madison, and Tuesday evening for Brookfield.

Great. Anything else before I put the receipts into Concur?

Can you give me a tight packing and receipt checklist? I leave Sunday.

Checklist: printed schedule plus host phone numbers; Delta change email and new boarding passes; rental agreement and fuel receipt; hotel folios with parking separated; campus parking or gate instructions for Milwaukee; materials inventory photo before pickup and before return; one snow brush or scraper from home; boots or shoes that can handle slush; phone charger in the car; all receipts photographed nightly. Do not leave counselor cards, scanner, or folio bag in the SUV overnight.

messages.content: The recruiting trip is finally wrapped, so now I need to face Thanksgiving. My spouse's family confirmed San Diego. We can leave after early school release Wednesday Nov. 27 and need to be back Sunday Dec. 1 at a sane hour for Monday school and work. Four of us. Relatives have very limited sleeping space, so probably a hotel. Can you compare flying versus driving?

I can. For that holiday window, flying will protect Monday better, but driving may be much cheaper if fares have jumped. I need the relatives' neighborhood and the earliest realistic airport departure. Also, should I assume all four travel together, or do you want me to price a split plan with only part of the family going?
All four if we can make it work. They are near Clairemont Mesa Boulevard and I-5. We could leave the house around 1 PM Wednesday. If airfare is awful, driving is still on the table.

Here is the practical comparison. Fly all four: Southwest nonstop SLC-SAN 5:20-6:25 Wednesday and SAN-SLC 3:05-5:55 Sunday, about $408 per person or $1,632 total; Delta nonstop 3:45-4:50 Wednesday and 6:15-9:10 Sunday, about $462 per person or $1,848 total; cheapest late combo is about $1,504 total but lands close to midnight Sunday. Drive: about 750 miles each way, 11-12 hours without much margin; direct Wednesday after school gets you in very late, and splitting through Las Vegas adds motel cost and cuts into Thanksgiving morning. Hotel areas: Kearny Mesa/Clairemont is closest, Mission Valley has more food, Old Town is workable but parking is often pricier.
If we can keep airfare under about $1,700, I would rather fly. The Southwest timing looks best. For the hotel, two queens, breakfast, parking, and easy food would help.

One trade-off: Southwest saves money and includes bags, but seats are not assigned. For four people on a holiday flight, I would set check-in alarms or add EarlyBird if the price is reasonable. Delta costs about $216 more total on the current fares and lets you choose seats now. Is the savings worth the open seating for this trip?
For this one, yes. The teenagers can handle not sitting right next to us. Let's do Southwest and set check-in alarms.

Then I would hold the Hampton Inn San Diego-Kearny Mesa. It is closest to the Clairemont/I-5 area, about $189/night refundable, two-queen room available, breakfast starts at 6:00, free parking, and there are casual restaurants on Convoy and Clairemont Mesa nearby. Backups: Holiday Inn Express Mission Bay at about $204 with breakfast but some parking uncertainty, or Homewood Suites Mission Valley around $229 with more space but higher parking and a longer drive to relatives.
Hold the Hampton. Relatives can pick us up Wednesday, but not Sunday, so rideshare back to the airport is fine. Please make sure the Sunday return does not wreck Monday.

Held: Southwest outbound Wednesday 5:20 PM SLC to 6:25 PM SAN, return Sunday 3:05 PM SAN to 5:55 PM SLC. That return is the best balance I found because it avoids the late-night holiday crowd and gets everyone home before dinner. Hampton Kearny Mesa is held Wednesday through Sunday in a two-queen refundable room. Add a rideshare budget of about $35-$50 for the Sunday hotel-to-airport trip depending traffic.
Can you send me a quick family-thread summary with the budget?

Send this: Thanksgiving plan is to fly all four of us to San Diego instead of doing the 11-12 hour drive each way. Southwest nonstop leaves SLC Wednesday at 5:20 PM and returns Sunday at 3:05 PM, landing around 5:55 PM so Monday is protected. Airfare is about $1,632 total. Hotel hold is Hampton Inn San Diego-Kearny Mesa, two queens, breakfast included, free parking, close to Clairemont/I-5 and nearby casual food, about $756 before taxes for four nights. We will set Southwest check-in alarms and use rideshare to the airport Sunday.

The Southwest quote from the family text moved, so can you help me lock the real flight and hotel before I buy? Four of us, SLC to San Diego Wednesday 11/27 and back Sunday 12/1.

Protect Monday. One checked family bag at most, plus carry-ons. I would also rather not rent a car unless it makes the weekend dramatically easier.

Right now Delta Main Cabin has 16A/16B and 17A/17B open, so that gives you two pairs and two windows. The evening return buys more visiting time but gets everyone home close to bedtime and leaves less room for holiday delays.
That makes sense. Before I book, can you verify the Hampton breakfast and parking are actually included? I do not want a holiday surprise.

The Hampton listing shows complimentary breakfast daily and complimentary self-parking. For Thanksgiving week I would still add a note to confirm holiday breakfast hours, but it is not showing as a paid add-on. The two-queen nonsmoking room is refundable until Monday 11/25 at 11:59 PM hotel time.
Okay, reserve that hotel. For the flights, book Delta with the 4:40 Sunday return, one checked bag, and those paired seats if still open.
I can do that. Last local-transport check: are your relatives definitely handling Wednesday airport pickup and the Thanksgiving/Friday shuttling, with you using rideshare back to SAN on Sunday?

messages.content: Now that Thanksgiving is behind us, I have a January Denver workshop to figure out. It is downtown, starts Monday Jan. 13 at 1:00 PM, runs all day Tuesday, and closes Wednesday at 11:30. Can you compare a Sunday afternoon flight, a Monday morning flight, and driving from Salt Lake? I also need the official hotel block compared with nearby hotels that include breakfast.
Absolutely. Before I rank them, is there any required prep before the 1:00 PM Monday kickoff, and would the extra Sunday hotel night be reimbursable if it is justified for winter arrival reliability?

No prep before 1:00, but I cannot be late. The university will reimburse either airfare or mileage. An extra night should be okay if the reason is solid. I do not need a car downtown, and breakfast matters Tuesday because the agenda starts at 8:00.

Then my ranking is: Sunday afternoon nonstop flight first, Monday morning flight a distant second, and driving only if the forecast is unusually clear. Sunday flying gives you a buffer, avoids I-80/I-25 winter risk, and lets you arrive before dinner. Monday morning technically works, but one cancellation or deicing delay could put the 1:00 kickoff at risk. Driving is reimbursable, but it adds fatigue, road-closure uncertainty, and downtown parking.
Can you put numbers around it? My director will ask why I am not just driving.

Driving is roughly 520 miles each way, so the reimbursed mileage can be substantial before you even add downtown parking at about $40 to $55 per night. It is also 8 to 9.5 hours each way in good weather. A nonstop flight is likely in the $220 to $320 range, plus airport train or rideshare. The Sunday hotel night is the extra cost, but it directly protects an on-time Monday arrival.
What if I flew Monday morning on the first nonstop?

The first nonstop can work on paper: leave SLC around 7:00 AM, land around 8:30, and get downtown by 10:00 if everything runs cleanly. The problem is that January deicing or a cancellation leaves very little recovery room. A 9:00 AM departure is too tight for a mandatory 1:00 PM start. If you must do Monday, use the first nonstop, carry on only, and keep the organizer warned. I would not choose it if Sunday is reimbursable.
Okay, Sunday afternoon flight. I do not need a rental car. What hotel options look reasonable?

For Sunday Jan. 12 to Wednesday Jan. 15, I would compare these: official workshop hotel block at $229 per night, about a 2-minute covered walk to the meeting space, no breakfast included, on-site restaurant, and parking around $49 if you drove. Hampton downtown/Convention Center area at about $174, breakfast included, queen room, 6- to 8-minute walk or short rideshare, casual food nearby. Home2 or Hyatt Place downtown at about $181 to $189, breakfast included, larger room, closer to 10 minutes on foot, with dinner nearby but less convenient in cold weather.
Breakfast is appealing, but a 10-minute icy walk after a reception is not. Is the Hampton walk exposed?

Mostly exposed, though it is straightforward. If sidewalks are icy, budget short rideshares for morning or evening moves, maybe $8 to $15 each. The official block wins on convenience and late-night food. Hampton wins on breakfast and rate. Since you are flying, the official hotel parking fee should not matter unless plans change and you drive.
Does the official block's lack of breakfast create a receipt problem?

Not a problem, just more line items. With the official hotel, breakfast would come out of per diem or a separate meal receipt. With Hampton, breakfast is included on the room folio, which simplifies early Tuesday. For the official hotel, watch for destination fees or dining credits because Concur may need those explained.
Can we hold two refundable rooms while I ask my director? One official block and one breakfast option.

Yes, as long as neither is prepaid. I would hold the official block as the weather-and-convenience backup and Hampton as the cost-conscious primary. Same dates: Sunday Jan. 12 check-in, Wednesday Jan. 15 checkout. It is just you for this trip, correct, and a standard queen room is fine?
Just me. Queen is fine, non-smoking, and no prepaid rates. I also want dinner access Sunday after landing.

That points to two sensible holds. Hampton is fine if you arrive early evening: there are casual restaurants nearby, and Union Station or the theater district is a short rideshare. The official block is easier if you land late or it is snowing because the restaurant is in the building. I will add late Sunday arrival possible, non-smoking, quiet room if available.
For flights, what is the best Sunday afternoon target from SLC, and what should I do Wednesday after the 11:30 close?

For Sunday, target a nonstop leaving SLC between about 2:30 and 5:00 PM. That gets you downtown by dinner without burning the whole day. For Wednesday, book DEN to SLC no earlier than 2:30 PM; that gives you time to leave the venue around noon, get to the airport by train or rideshare, and still have a comfortable security buffer.

Next step is to release one hotel once your director confirms the lodging approach.

messages.content: Denver is wrapped, and now Idaho landed on my desk. Boise round-trip flight: convenient outbound, but after Pocatello you would backtrack several hours to Boise, so I would not recommend it unless airfare is dramatically cheaper. Open-jaw: fly SLC to Boise, rent one-way, drive Boise to Nampa to Twin Falls to Pocatello, then return from Idaho Falls to SLC. That is the best schedule fit if the one-way rental fee is reasonable and you ship or consolidate materials.
Open-jaw sounds best, but I do not want some weird two-stop return from Idaho Falls.

I would avoid that too. Idaho Falls to Salt Lake City usually has a short nonstop on Delta/SkyWest, and that is the return to check first. Pocatello airport is closer but has thinner schedules, so Idaho Falls is the safer return airport. Boise to Salt Lake City also has nonstops, so the open-jaw can be two simple flight legs with no connection.
Okay, use Idaho Falls for the return comparison. What does the overnight sequence look like?

Recommended sequence: Tuesday fly or drive into Boise, handle the evening reception, then sleep in Meridian or Nampa so the 7:30 AM breakfast is easy. Wednesday after breakfast, drive to Twin Falls for the transfer table. After that, drive on to Pocatello and sleep there Wednesday night. Thursday do the high-school visit, then drive about 50 minutes to Idaho Falls for the return flight.
Would it be safer to sleep in Twin Falls Wednesday and drive to Pocatello Thursday morning?

Driving Twin Falls to Pocatello Wednesday late afternoon gives you more recovery room. If the Twin Falls event ends after dark or the forecast is ugly, then the backup is to ask the Pocatello school for a later Thursday visit, not to gamble on a predawn drive.
That makes sense. Give me hotel areas with breakfast, parking, and dinner nearby. Nothing fancy.

For Tuesday night, look at Nampa near the Civic Center or Idaho Center, or west Meridian if rates are better. Those areas usually have free parking, breakfast-included brands, and easy chain restaurants. Downtown Boise is better for dinner but worse for the 7:30 Nampa start. For Wednesday night, use Pocatello along I-15/Bench Road or near the ISU/Yield area depending on the school address; both have free parking and quick dinner options on Yellowstone Avenue. For Twin Falls, you may not need an overnight, but Blue Lakes Boulevard is the best backup area if roads force a stop.

For reliability, I would target a late-morning or noon nonstop to Boise and hand off the 11 AM meeting if you can.
Protect the reception. I can hand off the 11 AM meeting. If the flight is around noon, I am fine.

For airfare, compare SLC-BOI plus IDA-SLC against round-trip Boise and against mileage reimbursement for full drive. For the rental, confirm the one-way drop fee and that a compact SUV or midsize can hold the banner and boxes. For weather, note that open-jaw reduces total driving but does not eliminate I-84/I-86 exposure. For materials, ship one box to the Boise reception site if they can receive it, and carry the banner plus one box in the rental.

Fallback should be full drive, not Boise round-trip flying. Drive SLC to Boise Tuesday with an earlier start, overnight Nampa/Meridian, drive Nampa to Twin Falls to Pocatello Wednesday, then Pocatello to SLC after the Thursday school visit. It is longer behind the wheel, but it keeps materials simple and avoids the Boise backtrack after Pocatello. Add a weather check 48 hours out and permission to leave Monday evening or ship materials if I-84 looks bad.
Please make that into a short attachment for approval. Do not book yet.

Fly SLC to Boise around noon Tuesday, rent a car at BOI, attend the Boise evening reception, and stay Tuesday night in Nampa or west Meridian for the Wednesday 7:30 AM counselor breakfast. Continue Wednesday to the Twin Falls transfer table, then drive to Pocatello Wednesday evening and stay near I-15/Bench Road or ISU for the Thursday morning high-school visit. Return Thursday from Idaho Falls to Salt Lake City on a mid- or late-afternoon nonstop if available. Hotels should include parking and breakfast, with nearby dinner options. Items to price before approval: open-jaw airfare, one-way rental/drop fee, full-drive mileage comparison, and cost or feasibility of shipping one materials box to Boise. Backup if one-way rental is denied: full drive from Salt Lake City with the same Nampa/Meridian and Pocatello overnights; avoid Boise round-trip flying because it creates a long backtrack after Pocatello.

messages.content: I’m two days out on Idaho. Forecast now shows a snow band on I-84 between Burley and Twin Falls Tuesday morning, and the Boise venue moved the materials drop to 3:30 PM. Nampa says they can do a grab-and-go breakfast. Also, the restaurant closest to the Pocatello hotel is closed Wednesday. I’d like to avoid rebuilding the trip unless Tuesday gets too tight.

I would not rebuild yet. Keep the Tuesday departure, but set a real cutoff. If Monday evening still shows open roads and no heavy I-84 warning, leave early Tuesday. If the band shifts earlier, road status turns red, or the forecast pushes the SLC-Boise drive past about 6.5 hours, add the Monday night buffer in Twin Falls/Jerome.
I can leave by 5:15 Tuesday. What should I check and when?

Monday 6:00 PM: check ID 511 and the NWS point forecast for Burley, Jerome, and Twin Falls. If closures, chain restrictions, or heavy snow are likely after 6:00 AM Tuesday, book the buffer. Tuesday 4:45 AM: if roads are open and moving, go; if I-84 is closed, call the Boise venue and your supervisor before leaving.
Okay, no Monday room unless that trigger hits. Where should I stop?

Fuel Monday night in Salt Lake. Tuesday, make only short stops: Snowville or Malta if needed, then Jerome/Twin Falls once you are through the worst of the band. Avoid making Burley the planned long stop if conditions are active. Target Boise by 1:30, which still protects the 3:30 drop.
Does the grab-and-go change Wednesday morning?

Yes: request it at Nampa check-in, leave by 7:05 with only the counselor tote, and keep the rest packed. After the breakfast, top off fuel in Nampa or Jerome, then continue to Twin Falls with lunch buffer before the table.
Pick the Pocatello dinner and give me the tiny checklist.

Use Jakers near I-15 as the first dinner plan; call from Twin Falls when you pack out. If the wait is long, switch to takeout and eat at the hotel. Tiny checklist: Monday 6 PM road decision; Tuesday 4:45 AM road check; fuel before leaving SLC; boxes covered and separated by event; Boise garage receipt; Nampa grab-and-go request; Wednesday dinner call before leaving Twin Falls; save hotel folios, garage, meals, and any required fuel receipts; pack scraper, gloves, boots, charger, badge/QR, table cloth, name tags, and extra pens.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa selected the open-jaw Texas plan over a DFW round trip, rejected a Thursday-night drive back to Dallas, and set a Friday SLC landing target of no later than 4 PM. She asked to include Delta only when comparable, with timing and connection reliability taking priority. She wants Tuesday lodging in Plano near Legacy West, North Austin lodging near Highland/Mueller/Domain, easy breakfast where possible, and practical late dinner access after evening events. Austin materials will be carried in the rental car rather than checked.

Exactly.

messages.content: Idaho is wrapped, so I’m on the Texas yield puzzle. Mid-March: Tuesday evening admitted-student reception in Plano, Wednesday 7:30 counselor breakfast in Fort Worth, Thursday 4:30 transfer/alumni meetup in Austin. Materials can ship to Plano but not Austin. Can you compare DFW in/AUS out versus a DFW round trip, plus hotel areas and food logistics?

Yes. Two details change the reliable flight windows: what are the exact dates, and what time do you need to be on site for setup in Plano and Austin? Also, when you say back before Friday evening, what is the latest SLC landing time that still works?

March 18 to 21. Plano is 6 to 8:30 at a Legacy West-area venue, and I should be there by 5:15. Fort Worth is 7:30 to 9 in the Cultural District. Austin is at ACC Highland, 4:30 to 7, setup by 4. Family dinner is 6:30 Friday, so I want to land in SLC by 4. Include Delta if it has sane times, but schedule matters more.

My read: open-jaw is the clean plan. Fly SLC to DFW Tuesday, rent one car, drive Plano to Fort Worth to Austin, then fly AUS to SLC Friday. Target Tuesday arrival at DFW by 2:30, 2:45 latest, so a true afternoon SLC departure is too thin for a 5:15 setup. For Friday, target an AUS departure between about 8:30 and noon, landing SLC by 3:30. DFW round trip only makes sense if airfare is dramatically cheaper after adding extra drive time, tolls, gas, and risk. Shortening Austin is a program decision, not a travel efficiency win.
That matches my instinct. Can you spell out why the DFW round trip is the weak option? Finance sometimes just sees lower airfare.

The airfare line may look better, but the trip gets less reliable. After the Austin event, driving back to DFW Thursday night means leaving around 7:30 and arriving near midnight before a flight day. Waiting until Friday means a 3-plus-hour drive, Dallas-area traffic, rental return, and security before the flight, so you would need a later DFW departure and a tighter margin for the 4 PM SLC landing. The open-jaw uses the work geography instead of fighting it.
Good. No Thursday-night drive back. What about hotel areas? I need an easy breakfast if possible and somewhere to eat after the Plano reception.

For Tuesday, stay in Plano near Legacy West, Granite Park, or the Frisco/Plano edge. That keeps setup simple and gives you real late-dinner choices after 8:30. Limited-service hotels there are more likely to include breakfast; the nicer full-service places may have paid breakfast but better on-site dining. I would avoid downtown Dallas for this one. For Wednesday and Thursday, use North Austin: Highland, Mueller, or The Domain. Highland is closest to ACC; The Domain has the easiest dinner options and still keeps the event drive manageable.
Would it be smarter to stay in Fort Worth Tuesday after the Plano reception?

Only if the counselor breakfast requires a very early setup. Otherwise it trades one inconvenience for another: you would finish in Plano, eat late or skip dinner, then drive 50 to 70 minutes and check in around 10. Staying in Plano lets you handle the reception cleanly and eat nearby; you would just leave around 6:05 Wednesday for a 7:30 Fort Worth start.
Let’s keep Tuesday in Plano. For Austin, I’ll have one small box, table cloth, and banner. I can carry those in the rental car and avoid a checked bag.

That makes the open-jaw stronger. Ship the Plano materials to the venue or host hotel for Monday delivery, with your name, event date, and a hold-for-arrival note. Keep the Austin kit separate in the rental car, and ask the Austin hotel to store it if you arrive before check-in. If anything has to be shipped home after Austin, use a pre-labeled return from the hotel or campus mailroom rather than carrying leftovers onto the flight.
Can you outline the day-by-day timing? I need to see whether Wednesday is ridiculous.

Wednesday is full but reasonable. Tuesday: land DFW by 2:30, allow 30 to 45 minutes for rental pickup, 35 to 50 minutes to Plano, check in, then be at the venue by 5:15. Dinner after 8:30 stays in Legacy West/Plano. Wednesday: leave Plano about 6:05, arrive Fort Worth around 7:10, breakfast 7:30 to 9, then drive to Austin late morning with a lunch stop; arrival should be about 1:30 to 2:30. Thursday: work from the North Austin hotel, leave for ACC Highland by 3:15, event 4:30 to 7, dinner near Highland/Mueller/Domain. Friday: leave the hotel about two hours before the AUS flight.
Any flight connection traps? If there is no nonstop home from Austin that lands by 4, what connection is acceptable?

For Tuesday inbound, I would strongly favor a nonstop to DFW because a missed connection would threaten the 5:15 setup. For Friday from Austin, one connection is fine if it is comfortable: roughly 60 to 90 minutes at DFW, DEN, PHX, or similar. I would avoid anything under 45 minutes, anything with two stops, or anything that lands SLC after 4 even on paper. If Delta is late or awkward, AA, United, or Southwest are fair game.
Exactly. Don’t make it sound like Delta is required. Comparable is fine; arrival time wins.

Got it. The flight screen should say: first filter by arrival reliability, then by connection quality, then by carrier and price. Tuesday must protect the Plano setup. Friday must protect the SLC-by-4 landing. A comparable Delta option can stay on the list, but it should not beat a cleaner itinerary.
Now give me the supervisor approval questions. I need the plain recommendation, not a huge spreadsheet.

Plain recommendation: approve open-jaw airfare, SLC to DFW Tuesday and AUS to SLC Friday, with one rental car picked up at DFW and returned at AUS. Approval questions: 1) Is open-jaw airfare allowed when it reduces driving risk and total work time? 2) Are one-way rental return fees, tolls, parking, and fuel reimbursable? 3) Is the Wednesday Fort Worth-to-Austin drive acceptable within the workday? 4) Who confirms receipt and storage of the shipped Plano materials? 5) May the Austin kit ride in the rental car, with hotel storage if needed? 6) Should hotels prioritize included breakfast, or lowest refundable rate?
Perfect. Put that into a clean note I can paste, including the sentence on why we are not doing DFW round trip.

Paste-ready note: Recommended plan is an open-jaw Texas yield itinerary: fly SLC to DFW on Tuesday, March 18, arrive by 2:30 PM, pick up one rental car, stay Tuesday night in Plano near Legacy West, attend the 6 to 8:30 PM reception, then drive early Wednesday to the 7:30 AM Fort Worth counselor breakfast. After breakfast, drive to Austin and stay Wednesday and Thursday in North Austin, preferably Highland, Mueller, or The Domain for ACC Highland access, included-breakfast options, and practical dinner choices after the Thursday event. Return Friday, March 21, from AUS to SLC on a nonstop or one-stop itinerary that lands by 4 PM. We are not recommending a DFW round trip because the apparent airfare savings would add a late-night or high-risk Friday drive from Austin back to Dallas, reducing schedule reliability for the required Friday return. Approval needed: open-jaw airfare, DFW pickup/AUS return rental including any drop fee, tolls and parking, Plano materials receipt/storage, Austin materials carried in the rental car, and whether refundable hotels with breakfast may be prioritized.
